## Contamination Indication

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Contamination Indication Settings [sWN ContaminationConfig]

</summary>

Define how and under which conditions the device shall indicate a potential contamination of the optics cover to enable preventive cleaning.

**Telegram structure: sWN ContaminationConfig**

| Telegram part       | Description                                                                                | Variable | Length | Additional details                                                  | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                                                                    | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type        | Write                                                                                      | String   | 3      |                                                                     | `sWN`                                                                       | `73 57 4E`                                                                                |
| Command             |                                                                                            | String   | 19     |                                                                     | `ContaminationConfig`                                                       | `43 6F 6E 74 61 6D 69 6E 61 74 69 6F 6E 43 6F 6E 66 69 67`                                |
| Strategy            | Strategy code                                                                              | Enum_8   | 1      | No output:<br>All sectors contaminated:<br>One sector contaminated: | `0<br>1<br>2`                                                               | `00<br>01<br>02`                                                                          |
| Response time       | How fast (in seconds) the sensor reacts after a contamination                              | Uint_16  | 2      | Value range 3 ... 60<br>Default: 3                                  | `+3d … +60d (03h … 3Ch)`                                                    | `00 03 … 00 3C`                                                                           |
| Threshold warning   | Sensitivity                                                                                | Enum_8   | 1      | High:<br>Medium:<br>Low:                                            | `0<br>1<br>2`                                                               | `00<br>01<br>02`                                                                          |
| Sector preselection | Selection of either custom sectors or used weather protection hood                         | Enum_8   | 1      | All sectors:<br>Weather protection hood:<br>Custom sectors:         | `0<br>6<br>255d (FFh)`                                                      | `00<br>06<br>FF`                                                                          |
| Length              |                                                                                            | UInt_16  | 2      | Always:                                                             | `7`                                                                         | `07`                                                                                      |
| Custom sectors      | Enable/ disable individual sectors when custom sectors got selected in Sector preselection | Array    | 7      | Active: 1<br>Inactive: 0<br>Default value of all sectors is active  | `0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1` | `00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01` |
| Enable Warning      | Warning monitoring                                                                         | Bool_1   | 1      | Off (False):<br>On (True):                                          | `0<br>1`                                                                    | `00<br>01`                                                                                |
| Enable Error        | Error monitoring                                                                           | Bool_1   | 1      | Off (False):<br>On (True):                                          | `0<br>1`                                                                    | `00<br>01`                                                                                |

**Telegram structure: sWA ContaminationConfig**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                              | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                  |
| ------------- | ----------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Answer      | String   | 3      |                    | `sWA`                 | `73 57 41`                                                 |
| Command       |             | String   | 19     |                    | `ContaminationConfig` | `43 6F 6E 74 61 6D 69 6E 61 74 69 6F 6E 43 6F 6E 66 69 67` |

### Change CoLa TCP Timeout [sWN EtherColaTransmitTimeout]

</summary>

Change CoLa TCP Timeout.

**Access:** Authorized client user level is required.

**Request: `sWN EtherColaTransmitTimeout`**

| Telegram part / meaning                  | Variable type | Length (bytes) | Values, ranges, and notes                   |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Write                                    | String        | 3              | CoLa A: sWN                                 |
| Adjust CoLa TCP Acknowledge timeout time | String        | 24             | CoLa A: EtherColaTransmitTimeout            |
| New timeout time in ms                   | Uint_16       | 2              | Default: 15000<br>CoLa A: +250d ... +15000d |

**Response: `sWA EtherColaTransmitTimeout`**

| Telegram part / meaning                  | Variable type | Length (bytes) | Values, ranges, and notes        |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Answer                                   | String        | 3              | CoLa A: sWA                      |
| Adjust CoLa TCP Acknowledge timeout time | String        | 24             | CoLa A: EtherColaTransmitTimeout |

The timeout change takes effect after the sensor is restarted.

**Request example**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWN EtherColaTransmitTimeout +250<ETX>
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1F 73 57 4E 20 45 74 68 65 72 43 6F 6C 61 54 72 61 6E 73 6D 69 74 54 69 6D 65 6F 75 74 20 00 FA 8E
```


**Response example**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWA EtherColaTransmitTimeout<ETX>
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1C 73 57 41 20 45 74 68 65 72 43 6F 6C 61 54 72 61 6E 73 6D 69 74 54 69 6D 65 6F 75 74 5B
```

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Poll One Telegram [sRN LMDscandata]

</summary>

Asking the device for the measurement values of the last valid scan. The device will respond, even if currently no measurement data is created (e.g. due to standby or log in).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

> **Important:** The `sRN LMDscandata` and `sEN LMDscandata` telegrams must not be sent via CoLa A. Use CoLa B for these data telegrams; sending them over CoLa A can result in data loss.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description       | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                      | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Read              | String   | 3      |                    | `sRN`         | `73 52 4E`                         |
| Command       | Only one telegram | String   | 11     |                    | `LMDscandata` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61` |

**Example: sRN LMDscandata**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRN{SPC}LMDscandata<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sRN LMDscandata<ETX>
```

```text
sRN LMDscandata
```

```text
02 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0F 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 05
```

```text
73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61
```


**Telegram structure: sRA LMDscandata**

The response uses the scan-data structure documented for `sRA/sSN LMDscandata` below. The `sEA LMDscandata` telegram is the subscription acknowledgement, not the scan-data payload.

</details>

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Send Data Permanently [sEN LMDscandata]

</summary>

Start or stop continuous transmission of measurement data. Data is transmitted as configured as soon as measurement data is generated by the device. No data is generated when there is an active log in, the laser is shut off (e.g. in Standby mode), the motor is stopped, the data format is Compact, or the device is in certain error modes (e.g. Device not ready).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

**Telegram structure: sEN LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                      | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                          |
| ------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Event         | String   | 3      |                    | `sEN`         | `73 45 4E`                         |
| Command       | Data telegram | String   | 11     |                    | `LMDscandata` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61` |
| Measurement   | Start/stop    | Enum_8   | 1      | Stop:<br>Start:    | `0<br>1`      | `00<br>01`                         |

**Example: sEN LMDscandata**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sEN{SPC}LMDscandata{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sEN LMDscandata 1<ETX>
```

```text
sEN LMDscandata 1
```

```text
02 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01 33
```

```text
73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01
```

LMDscandata - reserved values

Valid distance measurement values are values starting from 16d upwards; everything below has the following meaning:

| DIST     | RSSI   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0d       | 0d     | Invalid measurement value; caused by very low remission (extremely dark object), object distance not within measurement range (too close or too far away) or selected filter settings at device |
| 1d - 15d | 0d     | Reserved, currently not in use                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ≥16d     | >0h | Valid measurement values                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ≥16d     | 254d   | Reflector detected                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ≥16d     | 255d   | Reserved                                                                                                                                                                                        |

Higher measurement values will be given out with a zero, that means no measurement value detected.

| Read encoder speed                           | String        | 8              | CoLa A: LICencsp          |
| [Speed in m/s as float according to IEEE754] | Real          | 4              | CoLa A: 0h … FFFFFFFFh    |

**Request example**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRN LICencsp<ETX>
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0C 73 52 4E 20 4C 49 43 65 6E 63 73 70 62
```


**Response example**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRA LICencsp 0<ETX>
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 52 41 20 4C 49 43 65 6E 63 73 70 20 00 00 00 00 4D
```

</details>

</section>

# LRS4000 Electrical Connection and Pin Assignment

> Wire the LRS4000 power, Ethernet, encoder, and digital I/O connectors to a controller using the documented M12 pin assignments.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/electrical-connection/

# Electrical Connection

Compatible with: LRS4000

The LRS4000 has separate M12 connectors for power, Ethernet, and digital
I/O/encoder signals. The tables below reproduce the assignments from LRS4000
operating instructions 8026337/1VNC, pages 34–35.

To check whether the sensor still receives its minimum supply voltage at the end of a long cable, use the [Cable Dimensioning](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cable-dimensioning/) calculator.

## Power 

This connection uses a male, 5-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![PWR connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/lrs4000-pwr.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">PWR connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Vs` | Supply, +10 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 2 | — | Reserved; do not connect |
| 3 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 4 | `IN8/OUT8` | Configurable digital input 8 or output 8 |
| 5 | — | Reserved; do not connect |

## Ethernet

This connection uses a female, 4-pin, D-coded M12 connector.

![Ethernet connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/lrs4000-ethernet.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">Ethernet connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Ethernet** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `TX+` | Transmit + |
| 2 | `RX+` | Receive + |
| 3 | `TX-` | Transmit − |
| 4 | `RX-` | Receive − |

## IOs and Encoder

This connection uses a female, 8-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![I/O and encoder connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/lrs4000-io.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">I/O and encoder connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**IOs and Encoder** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IN1` | Encoder input 1 |
| 2 | `IN2` | Encoder input 2 |
| 3 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |
| 4 | `IN4/OUT4` | Configurable digital input 4 or output 4 |
| 5 | `IN5/OUT5` | Configurable digital input 5 or output 5 |
| 6 | `IN6/OUT6` | Configurable digital input 6 or output 6 |
| 7 | `GND INx/OUTx` | Common reference for all digital I/O |
| 8 | `IN7/OUT7` | Configurable digital input 7 or output 7 |

# LRS4000 Motor Synchronization

> Synchronize LRS4000 scan start angles with PTP over Ethernet or with an index signal between a reference sensor and synchronized sensors.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/motor-synchronization/

# Motor Synchronization

Motor synchronization coordinates measurement start angles across several
LRS4000 sensors. It can increase the effective scan frequency or resolution
of a combined system. The sensor shifts its measurement start angle between
−180° and +180°; set the phase for each device individually.

LRS4000 supports two synchronization methods.

## PTP Synchronization

Synchronize the LiDAR sensors over Ethernet to a central PTP master. The
sensors then share a system time and operate synchronously. The OpenAPI
reference exposes the `SyncMode` and `SyncPhase` settings and provides the
`MotorSyncStatus` endpoint.

## Synchronization Through Inputs and Outputs

Use one LRS4000 as the reference device and configure the remaining devices
as synchronized devices.

1. On the reference device, set the motor synchronization source to **No
   source**, define its start angle, and configure an output with the index
   signal as its source.
2. On each synchronized device, set the motor synchronization source to
   **Line (index signal at IN1)** and define its start angle.
3. Connect each synchronized device's IN1 to the reference device's output
   that generates the index signal.

Combine measurement data from multiple devices in the customer application.

## Check Synchronization Status

Read the `MotorSyncStatus` endpoint in the
[LRS4000 REST API reference](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/api-rest-openapi/). The documented values
distinguish between no clock/rotation synchronization, time synchronization
only, and synchronized operation.

## Related Articles

- [LRS4000 REST API | OpenAPI](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/api-rest-openapi/)
- [Time Synchronization](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/time-synchronization/)
- [3D scan recording](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/3d-scan-recording/)

# LRS4000 Firmware Release Notes

> LRS4000 firmware history, update guidance, feature changes, fixes, and known issues from versions 1.10.0 to 1.4.0.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/release-notes/

# Release Notes

This page summarizes LRS4000 firmware changes, fixes, compatibility notes,
and known issues. The releases apply to the LRS4581R. Check the device serial
number and firmware version before applying release-specific information.

## General Information

The extended-range capability is available for eligible devices. Firmware from
version 1.7.0 supports that mode only on devices produced from November 2024
with serial number `SN2442xxxx` or higher. Earlier devices may be updated, but
do not gain the extended-range feature.

## Update Instructions

Use SOPAS ET or Sentio Creator for firmware updates. Downgrading firmware is not
recommended.

For the steps, see [Firmware Update](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/#sopas-et).

## Firmware V1.10.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Redesigned web interface, cybersecurity page, HTTPS for web services, distance-data recording, and Perpendicular Distance.

**Improvements:** SOPAS ET web-server access and encoder settings presentation.

**New features.**

- The web interface was redesigned, and a cybersecurity page was added to
  show open ports and user levels and manage related settings.
- Web-server and REST configuration can use HTTPS.
- Distance-data recording is available through the SICK data recorder;
  download the software from the device web interface.
- Perpendicular Distance functionality was added.

**Improvements.**

- SOPAS ET can enable a disabled web server and now links to the device web
  interface instead of emulating it.
- Encoder settings are shown under inputs and outputs; encoder functionality
  is unchanged.

**Bug fixes.**

- Invalid device IP address ranges are now rejected by the sensor, preventing
  the fatal device error that could occur with an invalid address.
- Several minor field-evaluation bugs have been fixed.
- DHCP fallback behavior has been corrected to use static IP.

**Incompatibilities.**

- `sWN EtherCoLaAEventsEnable` is no longer available. CoLa A event output is
  generally allowed, but do not use it for LMDscandata because data may be
  lost.
- `sWN ScanDataEnable` has no effect. Use the data-output format setting to
  disable output.

**Known issues.**

Device temperature is displayed as 20 °C in the web interface and by
`sRN OPcurtmpdev`. This display and telegram behavior are planned for removal
in a later firmware version.

## Firmware V1.9.1

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R; **Release date:** 2026-04

**Improvements:** Softer motor startup after power-on.

**Bug fixes.**

- Activating field-evaluation groups through inputs 1 to 3 no longer causes
  device errors. The incorrect offset between physical inputs and the input
  selections in the group tab has also been corrected.
- The device no longer enters an overload error after startup when multiple
  configured groups would overload it if all were active simultaneously.

**Known issues.**

After reboot, an IP address in the `169.254.x.x` range may cause a fatal
device error. Return the device to `192.168.0.1` and install current firmware
through SOPAS ET as a recovery procedure.

## Firmware V1.9.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New feature:** Adds Sensitivity Mode.

**Sensitivity Mode.**

The mode can extend range and improve detection of highly reflective targets.
Observe the operating conditions in the table below. Using a mode outside its
stated ambient-light conditions may reduce detection probability and increase
noise.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Firmware V1.9.0:** maximum range in standard and extended-range mode (10% remission) and maximum ambient light per sensitivity mode.</p>

| Sensitivity mode | Maximum range, standard mode (10% remission) | Maximum range, extended-range mode (10% remission) | Maximum ambient light |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Normal | 55 m | 100 m | 80 klux |
| Sensitive | 65 m | 115 m | 30 klux |
| Very Sensitive | 70 m | 120 m | 10 klux |

**Incompatibilities.**

The device temperature sensor was removed. `OPcurtmpdev` no longer works.

## Firmware V1.8.1

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**Improvement:** Adds an adjustable TCP transmit timeout for CoLa connections.

`EtherColaTransmitTimeout` adjusts the transmit timeout for TCP connections
on ports 2111 and 2112. The default remains 15 seconds; the setting can be
changed from 250 milliseconds to 15 seconds to speed reconnection after an
unexpected disconnect.

**Bug fixes.**

The release fixes CoLa A/B commands being ignored after reconnecting over an
unstable network on TCP ports 2111 and 2112.

**Known issues.**

The GUI depicts the input/output connector as male A-coded, although the
connector should be female A-coded.

## Firmware V1.8.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Field-evaluation detection history and teach-in, additional GUI languages, and a cybersecurity tab with a hash calculator.

**Improvements:** Compact timestamps, date/time interface, and maximum region-of-interest range.

**New features.**

- The home page shows field-infringement detection history, with links to
  related field-evaluation pages.
- Teach-in can capture a static background manually or through an input.
  The taught background can be used for blanking and contour evaluation.
- A detection-list shortcut was added to field evaluation.
- Chinese, Japanese, and French were added as GUI languages.
- The cybersecurity tab groups security functions. Its hash calculator is
  required for changing passwords through CoLa A/B or logging in through a
  SICK software driver.

**Improvements and bug fixes.**

- The field-evaluation setting previously labeled **Do not regard an echo as
  object detected** is now labeled **Ignore missing echo**.
- Detection history has a revised graphical layout.
- Start and stop timestamps in Compact output are now transmitted as Linux
  system time.
- The date and system-time GUI has been updated.
- The maximum region-of-interest scanning range has increased from 200 m to
  300 m to cover all possible LRS4000 distance values.
- Loading application defaults now resets the LED enablement state correctly.
- SOPAS ET device import has been corrected so that all parameters are
  included in parameter export.

**Known issues.**

The input/output connector is depicted as male A-coded in the GUI, but should
be female A-coded.

## Firmware V1.7.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R; extended-range feature only on eligible production units

**New features:** Extended-range mode, field evaluation, online help, user-level management, and distance measurement between two points.

**New features.**

- Extended-range mode increases measurement distance up to 300 m. It is
  selected through the scan configuration, which also changes the scale
  factor. Eligibility is limited to devices produced from November 2024 with
  serial number `SN2442xxxx` or higher.
- Field evaluation supports up to 16 user-defined fields, subject to field
  shape and concurrent application load.
- Online help provides topic descriptions and guided tours.
- Other web-interface user levels can be enabled after logging in at Service
  level; CoLa A/B user levels are unaffected.
- The scan view can measure the distance between two points.

**Improvements and bug fixes.**

- The distance filter has been renamed **Scanning range filter**, and its
  graphical presentation has been updated. The scan view now shows the
  ignored scan area in gray.
- The separate start and stop buttons for 3D scan recording have been
  combined into one button that changes function. Recording can therefore
  be started and stopped without moving the mouse.
- The 3D scan view has an updated appearance and additional options.
- The diagnostics overview provides additional message filters, including
  filtering by occurrence time and showing only active messages.
- A fatal device error has been fixed for configurations combining an
  angular area below 360° (12.5 Hz / 0.02° or 25 Hz / 0.04°) with the echo
  filter set to **First echo** or **Last echo**.
- The scan-data viewer has been adapted for compatibility with updated
  Chromium browsers.

**Incompatibilities.**

The default echo-filter value changed from `FIRST_ECHO` to `LAST_ECHO`.

**Known issues.**

During 3D scan recording, an overtime measurement stop may leave the button
showing **Stop**. Pressing it a second time restores the **Start** state.

## Firmware V1.6.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Scan merge, Compact streaming over TCP, motor synchronization, and system diagnosis.

**New features.**

- Scan merge creates a 3D point cloud using position and orientation from the
  internal IMU or an external encoder. A rotation offset can compensate for
  rotation around a pivot; the recording can be started in the GUI or by a
  digital input. The resulting point cloud can be downloaded through the
  browser.
- Compact streaming was added over TCP port 2115. UDP is not supported for
  this format on this device, and only one streaming format can be enabled at
  a time.
- Motor synchronization can use PTP clock synchronization or a wired index
  signal. Synchronization is disabled by default; the receiver phase can set
  the rotation offset.
- System diagnosis can create a reduced diagnosis after an error or an
  extended file at Service level.

**Improvements.**

Robustness was improved for applications that move or swivel the device.

**Known issues.**

Certain combinations of partial scan configurations and first- or last-echo
filtering could cause a fatal device error. This was fixed in V1.7.0. A
Chrome scan-view issue was also fixed in V1.7.0.

## Firmware V1.5.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Particle Filter, Distance Filter, updated scan-data viewer, and a prompt to change default passwords.

**New features.**

- Particle Filter removes isolated small-object or noise echoes, such as
  rain or dust, based on distance steps from neighboring beam angles.
- Distance Filter limits scans to a configured range; out-of-range echoes
  receive distance and RSSI values of zero.
- The scan viewer adds 3D and split views.
- The interface prompts users to change passwords that are still at their
  defaults.

**Incompatibilities.**

Customer passwords from firmware earlier than 1.5.0 are reset to defaults
because of updated password handling. The Glare Detection Filter was removed
and replaced by Particle Filter.

**Known issues.**

The fatal-error scan configuration and Chrome scan-view issues from V1.6.0
also apply to this release; both are fixed in V1.7.0.

## Firmware V1.4.0

**Compatible with:** LRS4581R

**New features:** Contamination Indication, PTP, IMU secondary data, and controls for the web server and CoLaScan/AutoIP.

**New features.**

- Contamination Indication monitors 12 sectors around 360 degrees. Thresholds,
  response time, and weather-protection cover can be configured. Monitoring
  is available by GUI and telegram; evaluation is inactive by default.
- PTP synchronization can be enabled through the web interface or the
  `TSCRole` CoLa parameter.
- IMU secondary data can be read or sent as events.
- The web server can be disabled from connection settings. `EnableColaScan`
  can disable CoLaScan/AutoIP and prevent opening port 30178.

**Improvements.**

- Loading factory defaults now requires the Service user level.
- The 2D scan-view update interval now adapts to the rotation and filter
  settings. Previously, visualization could become slow, particularly with
  the median filter enabled.
- The connection-options page now groups settings into separate panels for
  legacy CoLa A/B, CoLa 2, and the web-server port. Each panel also includes
  security settings for disabling the related ports.
- The unused Expert Mode has been removed.

**Bug fixes and incompatibilities.**

- The default CoLa dialect for the UDP port has changed from CoLa A to CoLa B.
- All application parameters are now accessible to SOPAS ET for export and
  import through `.sopas` files. Previously, some application parameters
  could not be stored in parameter exports.
- CoLa A event output is disabled by default from V1.4.0. At the highest
  performance settings with all features enabled, loss-free CoLa ASCII
  output cannot be guaranteed; compatibility handling can also affect other
  CoLa1 ports. Port 2111 still supports polling device parameters, while
  event streaming uses ports 2112 (CoLa B) and 2122 (CoLa 2).
- For compatibility, `EtherCoLaAEventsEnable` can enable CoLa A events.
  Changing it requires explicitly saving parameters permanently and cycling
  power. Data loss depends on resolution and device configuration, and
  enabling this setting can also affect other CoLa ports.

**Known issues.**

Firmware V1.4.0 has a known fatal-error issue for certain partial scan
configurations with first- or last-echo filtering. Firmware V1.7.0 fixes this
issue.

For feature availability and parameter details, use the documentation for the
device and firmware version.

# LRS4000 Web GUI (SOPASair): Screens and Settings

> Walk through the LRS4000 SOPASair web interface for status, configuration, data output, applications, cybersecurity, and diagnostics.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/graphical-user-interface/

# SOPASair Walkthrough

SOPASair is the built-in web interface of the LRS4000. It runs directly on
the sensor, so no software installation is needed. Open `http://<sensor-ip>/`
in a browser on the same network as the sensor. The factory default address
is `192.168.0.1`.

You can view status and settings without logging in. To change settings,
log in with the **Authorized Client** user level using the user icon in the
top bar.

![SOPASair Home dashboard showing LRS4581R status, live measurement data, I/O states, and detection history](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-home-overview.png)
*The SOPASair Home dashboard: device status, live scan view, input and output states, and detection history at a glance.*

## Home

The Home page summarizes the sensor's state.

**Status** shows separate indicators for the device, connection,
measurement, field evaluation, and data output. Because each state is
reported independently, measurement can be running while external data
output is switched off.

![LRS4581R device and application status](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-status.png)
*Device and application status indicators.*

**Device information** lists the model, part number, serial number, firmware
version, system time, and the time of the last save. Click **Find device**
to make the sensor LEDs blink, so you can identify the unit on site.

![LRS4581R device information](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-device-information.png)
*Device identity and installed firmware version.*

## Configuration

The Configuration menu contains the measurement, filter, network, and I/O
settings. For the matching REST parameters and value ranges, see the
[LRS4000 OpenAPI reference](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/api-rest-openapi/).

### Basic Settings

**Configuration > Basic settings** defines how the sensor scans. Select a
scan configuration to set the scan rate and angular resolution. The page
also shows the angular range, interlaced mode, and maximum scanning range,
and lets you adjust sensitivity, the status LED, and the measurement state.

![LRS4581R basic settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-basic-settings.png)
*Scan configuration and measurement settings. The values shown are an example configuration.*

**Date and system time** shows the device clock and its synchronization
source. **Apply computer time** sets the sensor clock to your computer's
time. For network-based time sources, see
[Time synchronization](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/time-synchronization/).

![LRS4581R date and system time](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-date-time.png)
*Device clock and time synchronization settings.*

**Motor synchronization** aligns the rotation of several scanners to avoid
mutual interference. Select the synchronization source here when you
integrate multiple sensors. See [Motor synchronization](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/motor-synchronization/)
for setup details.

![LRS4581R motor synchronization](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-motor-synchronization.png)
*Motor synchronization source.*

### Filter

**Configuration > Filter** combines the echo, particle, median, and mean
filters. The echo filter selects all, first, or last echoes. Expand each
of the other filters to set its threshold, width, or averaging parameters.
See [Filter details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/) for how each filter
affects the measurement data.

![LRS4581R filter settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-filters.png)
*Echo, particle, median, and mean filters.*

### Contamination Indication

**Configuration > Contamination indication** monitors the front window for
dirt. The sector diagram shows the contamination state per sector, using
the color legend below it. You can configure whether a warning or error is
output, the sensitivity, the monitored sectors, and the response delay. See
[Contamination indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/contamination-indication/) for
the application background.

![LRS4581R contamination indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-contamination.png)
*Contamination status per sector and evaluation settings.*

### Connection Options

**Configuration > Connection options** contains the Ethernet settings:
addressing mode, IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, MAC address, and
link speed.

When you click **Apply**, the new network settings take effect immediately.
The browser loses its connection if the sensor moves to an address that your
computer cannot reach, so note the new address before applying the change.

![LRS4581R Ethernet settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-ethernet.png)
*Ethernet addressing and link settings.*

### Inputs and Outputs

**Configuration > Inputs and outputs** assigns each port as an input or an
output. For outputs, select the signal sources, inversion, logic, and
restart behavior. The connector diagram next to each port shows the
corresponding pin, and the status indicators show the current physical
state. Enable **Use encoder** if an external encoder is connected.

![LRS4581R input and output assignments](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-inputs-outputs.png)
*Port assignments with connector pin diagrams.*

## Application

The Application menu contains measurement-data output and the on-device
applications: field evaluation, 3D scan recording, and perpendicular
distance measurement.

### Data Output

**Application > Data output** selects the output format: Compact,
LMDscandata, or Deactivated. The page lists the protocols and ports on which
the data is available. See [Data streaming](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/) for
the transport options and parser requirements.

![LRS4581R measurement-data output](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-data-output.png)
*Output format, protocols, and ports.*

**Output data format** selects the optional content of each telegram:
device name, time stamp, encoder values, and RSSI. It also sets the output
interval and the distance scaling factor.

![LRS4581R output data format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-output-format.png)
*Optional telegram content, output interval, and scaling factor.*

**Output range** limits the output to a start and stop angle.

![LRS4581R output angular range](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-output-range.png)
*Start and stop angle of the output range.*

**Range filter** removes measurement points outside a distance window.

![LRS4581R distance filter](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-range-filter.png)
*Distance filter.*

### Field Evaluation

**Application > Field evaluation** monitors fields for objects and switches
outputs when a field is infringed. Each group combines fields, evaluations,
and outputs, and has its own activation source. **Resource requirements**
shows how much of the sensor's evaluation capacity is in use, and
**Detection list** shows recent detections.

![LRS4581R field evaluation groups](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-field-evaluation.png)
*An evaluation group with its field, evaluation, and output.*

**Teach-in** creates a field automatically from the current environment.
Set the distances in front of and behind the detected contour and the
minimum teach-in time, then start teach-in from the button or a digital
input.

![LRS4581R teach-in controls](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-teach-in.png)
*Teach-in parameters and start control.*

See [Field evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/) for a complete
commissioning procedure.

### 3D Scan Recording

**Application > 3D scan recording** combines 2D scans with the sensor's
rotation to build a 3D point cloud. The rotation comes from the internal
IMU or an external encoder. Start the recording with the button or an
input signal, and download the resulting point cloud when it is complete.

![LRS4581R 3D scan recording settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-scan-recording.png)
*3D scan recording with the internal IMU as rotation source.*

See [3D Scan Recording](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/3d-scan-recording/) for the REST workflow.

### Perpendicular Distance Measurement

**Application > Perpendicular distance measurement** reports the shortest
and furthest measuring points within a field, relative to a reference
plane. Use **Add group** to define a new measurement, and
**Result list for distance measurement** to view the results.

![LRS4581R perpendicular-distance application](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-perpendicular-distance.png)
*A perpendicular-distance measurement group.*

## Diagnostics

### Overview

**Diagnostics > Overview** combines status, device identity, operating
information, the current device status, and the message log. Expand
**Operating information** to see the number of power-on cycles, the
operating hours, and the time of the last parameterization.

![LRS4581R operating information](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-operating-information.png)
*Power-on count, operating hours, and last parameterization.*

The message table lists current and past events with their status number
and description. If you need support, use **Create diagnostic file** to
collect the device state in one file and send it to SICK. See
[Contact](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/contact/).

### Cybersecurity

**Diagnostics > Cybersecurity** shows the HTTPS certificate with its
fingerprint, serial number, issuer, and expiry date. Use
**Create certificate** to generate a new certificate. The **Hash calculator**
helps you verify file checksums. See
[HTTPS and certificates](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/https-and-certificates/) for the
complete certificate setup. For the variant-qualified service ports, see the
[LRS4000 network-services matrix](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cybersecurity/#lrs4000-lrs4581).

![LRS4581R cybersecurity certificate status](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-certificates.png)
*HTTPS certificate overview.*

### Data Recorder

**Diagnostics > Data recorder** explains how to install the SICK data
recorder on your computer and connect it to the sensor. Use the recorder
to capture measurement data for later analysis or support cases.

![LRS4581R recorder instructions](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-recorder.png)
*Installation and connection steps for the data recorder.*

### Detection History

**Diagnostics > Detection history** records field-evaluation detections.
Select the evaluations to include, then start the history. The
**Statistics** section counts the detections per evaluation, and the
**Detection list** shows each event with its time stamp. Use
**Reset detection history** to clear the counters.

![LRS4581R detection history](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/LRS4000/img/sopasair-detection-statistics.png)
*Detection counts per evaluation.*

# multiScan100 Overview

> Developer entry point for the SICK multiScan100 multi-layer 3D LiDAR family: setup, REST and CoLa interfaces, scan data, and device applications.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/

# multiScan100

The multiScan100 is a family of multi-layer 3D LiDAR sensors. Supported
variants include the multiScan136, multiScan165, and multiScan166. For a sensor and cable combination to get started, see the [Starter Kit](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/starter-kit/).

[Specifications and data sheet on sick.com](https://www.sick.com/de/en/search?text=multiScan100)

<div class="product-scans product-scans--combined">
  <picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="../assets/multiScan100/img/multiscan100-scan-layers.png"><img src="https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/multiscan100-scan-layers.gif" width="817" height="295" alt="multiScan136/166 on the left, measuring from −22.7° to +42.8°, and multiScan165 on the right, from −7.3° to +35.3°, with positive elevation upward"></picture>
  *multiScan136/166 (left; high-resolution layers 6 and 14 emphasized) and multiScan165 (right). Schematic infrared beams in blue; angles are positive upward, opposite to the DIN ISO output sign.*
</div>

Find firmware, EPLAN and CAD data, NVIDIA Isaac Sim models, and Milestone
XProtect plug-ins on the *Downloads* tab of your device variant's product page:
[search for multiScan100 on sick.com](https://www.sick.com/de/en/search?text=multiScan100).
Select the files for your device variant; see [Release Notes](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/release-notes/)
for firmware changes.

See [Licenses](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/licenses/) for software packages, included functions, and
license part numbers.

# API | REST | OpenAPI

<div class="tool-intro tool-intro--centered" markdown>

![OpenAPI](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/openapi-logo.png)

This page provides the searchable V2.5.0 REST reference and downloadable
OpenAPI description for the multiScan100 family. For REST concepts,
authentication, and request patterns, see
[REST API / OpenAPI](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/).

</div>

[multiScan100_2.5.0.yaml (Download)](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/openapi/multiScan100_2.5.0.yaml)

Always match the file to your device's actual firmware version. Function
availability can vary by variant and installed software package. The
`ScanDataFormat` enum also lists `3` LMDscandata and `4` NativeROS2; the
multiScan100 does not support these formats. Use `1` MSGPACK or `2` Compact.

### 1 - General 

#### [POST /checkCredentials](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#rest-post-checkcredentials)

Indicates whether authentication succeeded. For more details, see https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_scan_rest_client.

Build the JSON body from the request schema below.

**Try the request**

Protected requests need challenge-response authentication, so `curl` alone cannot send them; use the [Python script on the REST Interface page](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/#challenge-response-authentication).

**Request body**

**Required:** true

**Media type: `application/json`**

**Type:** object · **Nullable:** true

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**

`header`

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#schema-responseheader)

#### [POST /SetPassword](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#rest-post-setpassword)

Sets the password for the CoLa A/B interface only. In this example, the password for user level: Service (4) is set to - test - (integer value of the password hash - test -). For more details, see https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_scan_rest_client.

**JSON example**

```json
{
  "data": {
    "siUserLevel": 4,
    "udiNewPassword": 3410122659
  }
}
```

**Try the request**

Protected requests need challenge-response authentication, so `curl` alone cannot send them; use the [Python script on the REST Interface page](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/#challenge-response-authentication).

#### [GET /LFPmovingAveragingFilter](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#rest-get-lfpmovingaveragingfilter)

Returns/sets the mean filter settings. This filter smooths the distance value by calculating the arithmetic mean from the configured number of scans (2 to 4 scans). Points with zero distance are treated as missing values and are not taken into account for averaging. If all distances considered for averaging have the value 0, the result will be 0 as well.

**Try the request**

Copy this command into a terminal. In Windows PowerShell, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```bash
curl --request GET "http://192.168.0.1/api/LFPmovingAveragingFilter"
```

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**
| `header` |

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#schema-responseheader)

 |
| --- | --- |
| `data` |
| `bEnable` |

**Type:** boolean · **Default:** false

 |
| `uiAveragingDepth` |

**Type:** integer · **Default:** 3 · **Minimum:** 2 · **Maximum:** 4

 |

 |

### 11 - Webserver settings 

#### [POST /SetWebserverEnabled](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#rest-post-setwebserverenabled)

Sets the availability of the web server (reboot required). If disabled, the web-based GUI and the REST interface can no longer be used.

This function requires at least user level: Authorized Client.

```json
  }
}
```

#### [POST /SetOutput](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#rest-post-setoutput)

Sets the state of an individual output. The output source must first be set to "SOPAS command".

**Editable JSON template**

```json
{
  "data": {
    "Output": "<integer>",
    "Value": "<integer>"
  }
```

#### [GET /InertialMeasurementUnit](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#rest-get-inertialmeasurementunit)

Returns the current IMU data (e.g. acceleration and orientation). The data uses a coordinate system based on DIN 70000. The x-axis lies on the 90-degree beam of the 0-degree layer. The y-axis is perpendicular to the x-axis and lies in the 0-degree layer. The y-values increase in the counterclockwise rotation direction (right-handed system). The z-axis is perpendicular to the x-y plane, with positive values pointing toward the top of the scanner.

**Try the request**

Copy this command into a terminal. In Windows PowerShell, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```bash
curl --request GET "http://192.168.0.1/api/InertialMeasurementUnit"
```

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**
| `header` |

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/#schema-responseheader)

 |
| --- | --- |
| `data` |
| `Acceleration` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 3

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Default:** 0.0

 |
| `AngularVelocity` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 3

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Default:** 0.0

 |

### 15 - Data reduction

# multiScan100 API | CoLa Telegrams (CoLa A and CoLa B)

> multiScan100 CoLa telegram reference with sRN, sWN, sMN, and sEN commands, parameter structures, and CoLa A and CoLa B examples.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-cola-telegrams/

# API | CoLa Telegrams

This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the multiScan100. Use the
command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level
integrations without guessing the telegram structure. For connection
setup, framing, and log in, see
[CoLa Interface](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/cola-interface/).

Each telegram lists its request and response structure, examples, variable types, lengths, and CoLa A and CoLa B byte values.

Every entry uses the same layout, as in the first entry, [Log In](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#log-in-smn-setaccessmode): a telegram structure table with the variable type, length, and the values in CoLa A and CoLa B, followed by examples that you can copy.

Examples are grouped by protocol, with each telegram representation in a separate code block and its own copy button.

Categories follow the [multiScan100 REST API reference](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/)
where corresponding CoLa telegrams are available. Select a telegram to expand
its structure and examples. A direct link to a telegram opens it automatically.
The categories organize the reference; availability still depends on the
device variant, firmware, and installed software packages.

<section class="cola-category" markdown="1">

## General

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]

</summary>

The password hashes of the default passwords are documented in the operating instructions (PDF) of your device. Do not pass them on, and change the passwords during commissioning.

A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. Changed parameters will be reset to the previous state via a reboot unless the are saved. To save parameter changes the command "sMN mEEwriteall" must be send before log out.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description                            | Variable | Length | Additional details                             | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Method                                 | String   | 3      |                                                | `sMN`                   | `73 4D 4E`                               |
| Command       | User level                             | String   | 13     |                                                | `SetAccessMode`         | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| User level    | Select user level                      | Int_8    | 1      | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `2<br>3<br>4`           | `02<br>03<br>04`                         |
| Password      | Hash value for the selected user level | Uint_32  | 4      | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `<password hash>` | `<password hash>`                  |

**Example: sMN SetAccessMode**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}4{SPC}<password hash><ETX>
```

```text
sMN SetAccessMode 4 <password hash>
```


**Telegram structure: sAN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part     | Description   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                        | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                |
| ----------------- | ------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type      | Answer        | String   | 3      |                    | `sAN`           | `73 41 4E`                               |
| Command           | User level    | String   | 13     |                    | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| Change user level | Changed level | Bool_1   | 1      | Error:<br>Success: | `0<br>1`        | `00<br>01`                               |

**Example: sAN SetAccessMode**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sAN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
02 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 13 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 01 38
```

</details>

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Enable/ Disable CoLa User Levels [sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel]

</summary>

This command enables and disables a specific CoLa user level (Maintenance, Authorized Client).

**Telegram structure: sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

| Telegram part | Description                     | Variable | Length | Additional details                 | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Method                          | String   | 3      |                                    | `sMN`                   | `73 4D 4E`                                                       |
| Command       | Enable/ disable CoLa user level | String   | 21     |                                    | `EnableLegacyUserLevel` | `45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C` |
| User level    | -                               | Uint_8   | 1      | Maintenance:<br>Authorized Client: | `2<br>3`                | `02<br>03`                                                       |
| Status        | Enable/ disable                 | Bool_1   | 1      | Disable:<br>Enable:                | `0<br>1`                | `00<br>01`                                                       |

**Example: sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}EnableLegacyUserLevel{SPC}3{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel 3 1
```

```text
02 73 4D 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 33 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1D 73 4D 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 03 20 01 21
```

```text
73 4D 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 03 20 01
```


**Telegram structure: sAN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

| Telegram part | Description                     | Variable | Length | Additional details           | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Answer                          | String   | 3      |                              | `sAN`                   | `73 41 4E`                                                       |
| Command       | Enable/ disable CoLa user level | String   | 21     |                              | `EnableLegacyUserLevel` | `45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C` |
| Status code   | Confirmation                    | Bool_1   | 1      | unsuccessful:<br>successful: | `0<br>1`                | `00<br>01`                                                       |

**Example: sAN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sAN{SPC}EnableLegacyUserLevel{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
02 73 41 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1B 73 41 4E 20 45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C 20 01 0E
```

</details>

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Load Factory Defaults [sMN mSCloadfacdef]

</summary>

The Factory-Reset (Load factory defaults) deletes the entire parametrization of the device. All parameters, settings and system applications will be set to default.

**Telegram structure: sMN mSCloadfacdef**

| Telegram part | Description           | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                        | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                |
| ------------- | --------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Method                | String   | 3      |                    | `sMN`           | `73 4D 4E`                               |
| Command       | Load factory defaults | String   | 13     |                    | `mSCloadfacdef` | `6D 53 43 6C 6F 61 64 66 61 63 64 65 66` |

**Example: sMN mSCloadfacdef**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}mSCloadfacdef<ETX>
```

```text
sMN mSCloadfacdef
```

## Basic Settings

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Read for Frequency and Angular Resolution [sRN LMPscancfg]

</summary>

Read the scanning frequency, angular resolution and aperture angle of the device. Values show the information of the values before any filters are applied. Therefore aperture angle is always showing the maximum, scanning frequency and angular resolution may also be static depending on device family.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part | Description                                   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                     | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command type  | Read                                          | String   | 3      |                    | `sRN`        | `73 52 4E`                      |
| Command       | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String   | 10     |                    | `LMPscancfg` | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |

**Example: sRN LMPscancfg**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRN{SPC}LMPscancfg<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sRN LMPscancfg<ETX>
```

```text
sRN LMPscancfg
```

```text
02 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0E 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 63
```

```text
73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67
```


**Telegram structure: sRA LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part      | Description                                   | Variable | Length | Additional details                                   | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command type       | Answer                                        | String   | 3      |                                                      | `sRA`                   | `73 52 41`                                  |
| Command            | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String   | 10     |                                                      | `LMPscancfg`            | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67`             |
| Scan frequency     | [1/100 Hz]                                    | Uint_32  | 4      | 20 Hz:                                               | `7D0h`                  | `00 00 07 D0`                               |
| Reserved           | -                                             | Int_16   | 2      | Always:                                              | `1`                     | `00 01`                                     |
| Angular resolution | [1/10000°]                                    | Uint_32  | 4      | 0.5°:<br>0.25° (interlaced):<br>0.125° (interlaced): | `1388h<br>9C4h<br>4E2h` | `00 00 13 88<br>00 00 09 C4<br>00 00 04 E2` |
| Start angle        | [1/10000°]                                    | Int_32   | 4      | Variant-dependent; example: -180 to +180 degrees     | `FFE488C0 ... 1B7740`   | `FF E4 88 C0 ... 00 1B 77 40`               |
| Stop angle         | [1/10000°]                                    | Int_32   | 4      | Variant-dependent; example: -180 to +180 degrees     | `FFE488C0 ... 1B7740`   | `FF E4 88 C0 ... 00 1B 77 40`               |

**Example: sRA LMPscancfg**

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]

</summary>

The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

**Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime**

| Telegram part | Description    | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                                | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                   |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command type  | Method         | String   | 3      |                    | `sMN`                                   | `73 4D 4E`                                  |
| Command       | Set time stamp | String   | 14     |                    | `LSPsetdatetime`                        | `4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65` |
| Year          |                | Uint_16  | 2      |                    | `+1970d … +2099d (07B2h … 0833h)`       | `07 B2 … 08 33`                             |
| Month         |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch)`                 | `01 … 0C`                                   |
| Day           |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh)`                 | `00 … 1F`                                   |
| Hour          |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+0d … +23d(00h … 17h)`                 | `00 … 17`                                   |
| Minute        |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)`                 | `00 … 3B`                                   |
| Second        |                | Uint_8   | 1      |                    | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)`                 | `00 … 3B`                                   |
| Microsecond   |                | Uint_32  | 4      |                    | `+0d … +999999d(00000000h … 000F423Fh)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F`                 |

**Example: sMN LSPsetdatetime**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}+2026{SPC}+10{SPC}+6{SPC}+9{SPC}+25{SPC}+28{SPC}+0<ETX>
```

```text
sMN LSPsetdatetime +2026 +10 +6 +9 +25 +28 +0
```

```text
02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 2B 32 30 32 36 20 2B 31 30 20 2B 36 20 2B 39 20 2B 32 35 20 2B 32 38 20 2B 30 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 EA 0A 06 09 19 1C 00 00 00 00 B1
```

```text
73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 EA 0A 06 09 19 1C 00 00 00 00
```


**Telegram structure: sAN LSPsetdatetime**

| Telegram part | Description    | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                         | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                   |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command type  | Answer         | String   | 3      |                    | `sAN`            | `73 41 4E`                                  |
| Command       | Set time stamp | String   | 14     |                    | `LSPsetdatetime` | `4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65` |
| Status code   | Code number    | Enum_8   | 1      | Success:           | `0`              | `00`                                        |

**Example: sAN LSPsetdatetime**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sAN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}0<ETX>
```

### Set Particle Filter [sWN LFPparticle]

</summary>

Filter out disturbances in the meausurement data caused by particles such as dust, snow flakes or similar .

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPparticle**

| Telegram part | Description              | Variable | Length | Additional details   | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                       | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                          |
| ------------- | ------------------------ | -------- | ------ | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Write                    | String   | 3      |                      | `sWN`          | `73 57 4E`                         |
| Command       | Set particle filter      | String   | 11     |                      | `LFPparticle`  | `4C 46 50 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65` |
| Status code   | Code number              | Bool_1   | 1      | Inactive:<br>Active: | `0<br>1`       | `00<br>01`                         |
| Threshold1)   | Particle threshold in mm | Uint_16  | 2      | (must be taken)      | `+500d (1F4h)` | `01 F4`                            |

Never change the threshold here, it is taken by the device to handle the particles.

**Example: sWN LFPparticle**

</summary>

| Status code   | Code number     | Enum_8   | 1      | First echo:<br>All echos:<br>Last echo: | `0<br>1<br>2`  | `00<br>01<br>02`                      |

### Set Moving Averaging Filter [sWN LFPmovingAveragingFilter]

</summary>

Enables the moving average filter

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPmovingAveragingFilter**

| Telegram part   | Description                 | Variable | Length | Additional details   | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                   | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                                 |

| Variable Data 1 | Moving averaging is enabled | Bool     | 1      | Off:<br>On:          | `0d (00h)<br>+1d (01h)`    | `00<br>01`                                                                |
| Variable Data 2 | averaging depth             | UInt     | 2      | Minimum:<br>Maximum: | `+2d (02h)<br>+4d (0Ah)`   | `00 02<br>00 04`                                                          |

### Set Ground Filter Thresholds [sWN groundFilterThresholds]

</summary>

Requires Authorized client.

**Telegram structure: sWN groundFilterThresholds**

| Telegram part    | Description                             | Variable | Length | Additional details           | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                 | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                           |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command type     | Write                                   | String   | 3      |                              | `sWN`                    | `73 57 4E`                                                          |
| Command          | groundFilterThresholds                  | String   | 22     |                              | `groundFilterThresholds` | `67 72 6F 75 6E 64 46 69 6C 74 65 72 54 68 72 65 73 68 6F 6C 64 73` |
| Minimum distance | Signed distance from ground plane in mm | Int_16   | 2      | -1000 to +1000; default -100 | `-100`                   | `FF 9C`                                                             |
| Maximum distance | Signed distance from ground plane in mm | Int_16   | 2      | -1000 to +1000; default +100 | `+100`                   | `00 64`                                                             |

### Set Contamination Indication Settings [sWN ContaminationConfig]

</summary>

Define how and under which conditions the device shall indicate a potential contamination of the optics cover to enable preventive cleaning.

**Telegram structure: sWN ContaminationConfig**

| Telegram part       | Description                                                                                | Variable | Length | Additional details                                                  | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                                                                    | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type        | Write                                                                                      | String   | 3      |                                                                     | `sWN`                                                                       | `73 57 4E`                                                                                |
| Command             |                                                                                            | String   | 19     |                                                                     | `ContaminationConfig`                                                       | `43 6F 6E 74 61 6D 69 6E 61 74 69 6F 6E 43 6F 6E 66 69 67`                                |
| Strategy            | Strategy code                                                                              | Enum_8   | 1      | No output:<br>All sectors contaminated:<br>One sector contaminated: | `0<br>1<br>2`                                                               | `00<br>01<br>02`                                                                          |
| Response time       | How fast (in seconds) the sensor reacts after a contamination                              | Uint_16  | 2      | Value range 3 ... 60<br>Default: 3                                  | `+3d … +60d (03h … 3Ch)`                                                    | `00 03 … 00 3C`                                                                           |
| Threshold warning   | Sensitivity                                                                                | Enum_8   | 1      | High:<br>Medium:<br>Low:                                            | `0<br>1<br>2`                                                               | `00<br>01<br>02`                                                                          |
| Sector preselection | Selection of either custom sectors or used weather protection hood                         | Enum_8   | 1      | All sectors:<br>Weather protection hood:<br>Custom sectors:         | `0<br>6<br>255d (FFh)`                                                      | `00<br>06<br>FF`                                                                          |
| Length              |                                                                                            | UInt_16  | 2      | Always:                                                             | `7`                                                                         | `07`                                                                                      |
| Custom sectors      | Enable/ disable individual sectors when custom sectors got selected in Sector preselection | Array    | 7      | Active: 1<br>Inactive: 0<br>Default value of all sectors is active  | `0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1` | `00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01` |
| Enable Warning      | Warning monitoring                                                                         | Bool_1   | 1      | Off (False):<br>On (True):                                          | `0<br>1`                                                                    | `00<br>01`                                                                                |
| Enable Error        | Error monitoring                                                                           | Bool_1   | 1      | Off (False):<br>On (True):                                          | `0<br>1`                                                                    | `00<br>01`                                                                                |

</summary>

**Telegram structure: sWN EtherCoLaScanMode**

**Telegram structure: sRA LIDportstate**

| Telegram part                                                            | Description                                                                      | Variable | Length | Additional details                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                          | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                             |
