| Status code                                                              | System counter (time in µs since power up max. 71min then starting from 0 again) | Uint_32  | 4      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `0 … FFFFFFFFh`                   | `00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF`           |

|                                                                          | ….                                                                               |          |        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |                                                                |                                                                    |
| ARRAY which defines the number of external or virtual ports*             | 0...n                                                                            | Uint_16  | 1      | Hex:<br>Not available:<br>Number of ports:                                                                                                                                                                              | `00 00 - FF FF<br>00<br>01 ... n` | `00 00 - FF FF`                       |
| State of the ports and count value in hex                                | External port state                                                              | Enum_8   | 1      | Output voltage low:(Relays open)<br>Output voltage high:(Relays closed)<br>Tri-state:<br>Input voltage high (level):Input voltage from low to high (edge)<br>Input voltage low (level):Input voltage high to low (edge) | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03<br>04`      | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03<br>04`          |
| State of the ports and count value in hex                                | External port counter                                                            | Uint_32  | 4      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `0 … FFFFFFFFh`                   | `00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF`           |
| Time                                                                     | States code                                                                      | Enum_16  | 1      | No time data:<br>Time data:                                                                                                                                                                                             | `00 00<br>00 01`                  | `00 00<br>00 01`                      |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Year                                                                             | Array    | 2      | E.g.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `1970`                            | `07 B2`                               |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Month                                                                            | Array    | 1      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `1 … 12`                          | `01 … 0C`                             |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Day                                                                              | Array    | 1      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `1 … 31`                          | `01 … 1F`                             |

| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Second                                                                           | Array    | 1      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `0 … 59`                          | `00 … 3B`                             |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Microsecond                                                                      | Array    | 4      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `0 … 999999`                      | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F`           |

Inputs/outputs: If the device has separate inputs and outputs (instead of general purpose ports) the ARRAY shall start with inputs followed by the outputs.

Virtual ports are ports that can be used to expand the number of ports but are not physically available. They just show up in the corresponding ethernet telegrams (like LIDportstate).

Tri-State: Port is neither input nor output; the port is set inactive in SOPAS

**Example: sRA LIDportstate**

### Read Port Configuration of All I/Os [sRN PortConfiguration]

</summary>

Read the configuration of the digital inputs and outputs.

**Telegram structure: sRN PortConfiguration**

| Telegram part | Description                | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                            | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                            |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Read                       | String   | 3      |                    | `sRN`               | `73 52 4E`                                           |
| Command       | Ask for port configuration | String   | 17     |                    | `PortConfiguration` | `50 6F 72 74 43 6F 6E 66 69 67 75 72 61 74 69 6F 6E` |

**Example: sRN PortConfiguration**

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Port Configuration [sWN PortConfiguration]

</summary>

Configuration of the given ports. Telegram structure represents the configuration of 1 port.

If the device has multiple ports, use the same structure.

**Telegram structure: sWN PortConfiguration**

| Telegram part   | Description                                                          | Variable   | Length       | Additional details                                     | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                           | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type    | Write                                                                | String     | 3            |                                                        | `sWN`                              | `73 57 4E`                                                 |
| Command         | Configuration of the given ports                                     | String     | 17           |                                                        | `PortConfiguration`                | `50 6F 72 74 43 6F 6E 66 69 67 75 72 61 74 69 6F 6E`       |
| Port Type       | Input or Output                                                      | Enum_8     | 1            | Input:<br>Output:                                      | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)`             | `00<br>01`                                                 |
| Name            | Name of the port                                                     | FlexString | 9<br>(0..32) | Default:                                               | `InOut1`                           | `00 06 49 6E 4F 75 74 31 00`                               |
| Input Settings  |                                                                      |            |              |                                                        |                                                                 |                                                                                         |
| Logic           | Logic of the input                                                   | Enum_8     | 1            | Active high:<br>Active low:                            | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)`             | `00<br>01`                                                 |
| Debounce        | Select debouncing time in ms                                         | Uint_16    | 2            | 0 to 10000 ms                                          | `0 ... 2710`                       | `00 00 ... 27 10`                                          |
| Sensitivity     | Input sensitivity                                                    | Enum_8     | 1            |                                                        | `1`                                | `01`                                                       |
| Reserved1       |                                                                      | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00 00`                                                    |
| Reserved2       |                                                                      | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00 00`                                                    |
| Output Settings |                                                                      |            |              |                                                        |                                                                 |                                                                                         |
| Logic           | Definition of the output logic                                       | Enum_8     | 1            | Active high:<br>Active low:                            | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)`             | `00<br>01`                                                 |
| Output Mode     | Set kind of mode for output pin                                      | Enum_8     | 1            | PNP:<br>NPN:<br>Push-Pull:                             | `0<br>1<br>2`                      | `00<br>01<br>02`                                           |
| Restart Type    | Defines type of restart to be used                                   | Enum_8     | 1            | Immediately:<br>Time:                                  | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)`             | `00<br>01`                                                 |
| Restart Time    | [Only with restart type = Time], time in ms                          | Uint_32    | 4            | (20 ms … 600,000 ms)                                   | `+20d … +600000d (C8h ... 927C0h)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 09 27 C0`                                |
| Restart Input   | [Only with restart type = Input], input for restart                  | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+1d ... +8d (1h ... 8h)`          | `00 00 … 00 08`                                            |
| Combination     | Combining multiple Events and/or Inputs                              | Enum_8     | 1            | AND:<br>OR:<br>XOR:                                    | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)<br>+2d (2h)` |                                                                                         |
| Reserved        | Reserved value 3                                                     | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00 00`                                                    |
| Reserved        | Reserved value 4                                                     | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00 00`                                                    |
|                 | Source                                                               |            |              |                                                        |                                                                 |                                                                                         |
| Source          | The source parameter are only existing if the port is set to OUTPUT! |            | 2            |                                                        | `+1d (1h)`                         | `00 01`                                                    |
| Source Name     | Name of the source option                                            | String     | 4            | DeviceNotReady:<br>Input1:<br>Input2:<br>SopasCommand: | `DRDY<br>IN01<br>IN02<br>SC01`     | `44 52 44 59<br>49 4E 30 31<br>49 4E 30 32<br>53 43 30 31` |
| Invert          | Invert the source signal                                             | Bool_1     | 1            | Not inverted:<br>Inverted:                             | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)`             | `00<br>01`                                                 |
| Reserved        | Reserved value 5                                                     | Uint_8     | 1            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00`                                                       |
| Reserved        | Reserved value 6                                                     | Uint_8     | 1            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00`                                                       |
| Reserved        |                                                                      |            |              |                                                        |                                                                 |                                                                                         |
| Reserved        | Reserved value 7                                                     | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00 00`                                                    |

| Reserved        | Reserved value 9                                                     | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00 00`                                                    |
| Reserved        | Reserved value 10                                                    | Uint_16    | 2            |                                                        | `+0d (0h)`                         | `00 00`                                                    |

### Configure Scan Output Angles [sWN LMPoutputRange]

</summary>

Select the scan output start and stop angles (manual pages 124-126). Angular resolution is taken from the scan configuration. This example uses 0.5 degree and -90 to +90 degrees.

Requires Authorized client.

**Telegram structure: sWN LMPoutputRange**

| Telegram part      | Description             | Variable | Length | Additional details                             | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                              | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                   |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Command type       | Write                   | String   | 3      |                                                | `sWN`                 | `73 57 4E`                                  |
| Command            | LMPoutputRange          | String   | 14     |                                                | `LMPoutputRange`      | `4C 4D 50 6F 75 74 70 75 74 52 61 6E 67 65` |
| Reserved           | Single output range     | Int_16   | 2      | Always 1                                       | `1`                   | `00 01`                                     |
| Angular resolution | Units of 1/10000 degree | Uint_32  | 4      | Read from scan configuration; not changed here | `1388 (0.5 degree)`   | `00 00 13 88`                               |
| Start angle        | Units of 1/10000 degree | Int_32   | 4      | -180 to +180 degrees                           | `FFE488C0 ... 1B7740` | `FF E4 88 C0 ... 00 1B 77 40`               |
| Stop angle         | Units of 1/10000 degree | Int_32   | 4      | -180 to +180 degrees                           | `FFE488C0 ... 1B7740` | `FF E4 88 C0 ... 00 1B 77 40`               |

**Example: sWN LMPoutputRange**

<section class="cola-category" markdown="1">

## Data Reduction

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Angle Range Filter [sWN LFPangleRangeFilter]

</summary>

The angle range Horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) limits in units of 1/10000 degree.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPangleRangeFilter**

| Telegram part   | Description                                                             | Variable | Length | Additional details                                               | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                                               | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type    | Write                                                                   | String   | 3      |                                                                  | `sWN`                                                  | `73 57 4E`                                                 |
| Command         | Horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) limits in units of 1/10000 degree | String   | 19     |                                                                  | `LFPangleRangeFilter`                                  | `4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |
| Variable Data 1 | Enables/Disables the filter                                             | Bool_1   | 1      | Off:<br>On:                                                      | `+0d<br>+1d`                                           | `00<br>01`                                                 |
| Variable Data 2 | ThetaStart                                                              | Int_32   | 4      | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40`                                |
| Variable Data 3 | ThetaStop                                                               | Int_32   | 4      | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40`                                |
| Variable Data 4 | PhiStart                                                                | Int_32   | 4      | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h)`     | `FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0`                                |
| Variable Data 5 | PhiStop                                                                 | Int_32   | 4      | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h)`     | `FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0`                                |
| Variable Data 6 | BeamIncrement                                                           | UInt_16  | 2      | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `1d…+20d`                                              | `00 01 … 00 14`                                            |

Explanation: Enable the angle range filter and set up theta (horizontal) start -90°, theta stop +90°, phi (vertical) start -90°, phi stop +90°, beam increment 1

**Example: sWN LFPangleRangeFilter**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWN{SPC}LFPangleRangeFilter{SPC}0{SPC}FFF24460{SPC}DBBA0{SPC}FFF24460{SPC}DBBA0{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
sWN LFPangleRangeFilter 0 FFF24460 DBBA0 FFF24460 DBBA0 1
```

```text
02 73 57 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 30 20 46 46 46 32 34 34 36 30 20 44 42 42 41 30 20 46 46 46 32 34 34 36 30 20 44 42 42 41 30 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 2B 73 57 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 00 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 00 01 2F
```


Enables and set up the interval filter. The interval filter reduce the scan output rate by a given factor.

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPintervalFilter**

| Telegram part   | Description                                                                          | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                                   | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Command         | Reduce the scan output rate by a given factor                                        | String   | 17     |                    | `LFPintervalFilter`                        | `4C 46 50 69 6E 74 65 72 76 61 6C 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |
| Variable data 1 | Enables/Disables the filter.                                                         | Bool     | 1      | Off:<br>On:        | `0d (00h)<br>+1d (01h)`                    | `00<br>01`                                           |
| Variable Data 2 | Only every nth scan is output where n is given by<br>the value of uiReductionFactor. | Uint_32  | 4      |                    | `1d…+50d<br>(00 00 00 01h … 00 00 00 32h)` | `00 00 00 01 … 00 00 00 32`                          |

Enables the interval filter an set up to the 3rd scan

On firmware 2.4.4.0R, the parameter block is a 2-byte version,
an 8-byte timestamp, and 48 one-byte result codes (58 bytes total).
Each result occupies one byte, with no additional reserved byte.

The timestamp unit is microseconds for both read replies (`sRA`) and events
(`sSN`), not milliseconds. For example, the event timestamp `65D2897B50D60`
is 1,791,278,785,564,000 microseconds, corresponding to
October 6, 2026, 09:26:25.564 UTC. Interpreting it as milliseconds would put
the date more than 56,000 years after 1970.

<section class="cola-category" markdown="1">

## Object Evaluation

These telegrams read and configure [Object Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/object-evaluation/). Object Evaluation is available from firmware 2.5.0 and requires the **3D Object Detection Advanced** package. Create the evaluations in SOPASair; the telegrams then read their state and change their contour, criteria, and group activation.

The `Get...` and `Set...` methods require the Authorized Client user level; without a log in, the device answers with `sFA 1`. The other telegrams need no log in. Changes are applied immediately but are lost on restart unless you save them with [sMN mEEwriteall](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#save-parameters-permanently-smn-meewriteall).

### Set Activation of Object Evaluation Group [sMN ActivateObjectEvaluationGroup]

</summary>

This telegram activates or deactivates object evaluation groups. It switches only groups whose activation type is Telegram. For a group with the activation type Always, the device confirms the telegram, but the group stays active. Check the result with [sRN ObjectEvaluationGroupState](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#read-object-evaluation-group-state-srn-objectevaluationgroupstate).

**Telegram structure: sMN ActivateObjectEvaluationGroup**

| Telegram part    | Description                                   | Variable | Length | Additional details       | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                        | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type     | Method                                        | String   | 3      |                          | `sMN`                           | `73 4D 4E`                                                                               |
| Command          | Activate / deactivate object evaluation group | String   | 29     |                          | `ActivateObjectEvaluationGroup` | `41 63 74 69 76 61 74 65 4F 62 6A 65 63 74 45 76 61 6C 75 61 74 69 6F 6E 47 72 6F 75 70` |
| Number of groups | Number of following group entries             | Uint_16  | 2      |                          | `1 ... +48`                     | `00 01 ... 00 30`                                                                        |
| Group number     | Group 1                                       | Uint_16  | 2      |                          | `1 ... +48`                     | `00 01 ... 00 30`                                                                        |
| Activation       | Activate / deactivate the group               | Bool_1   | 1      | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1`                        | `00<br>01`                                                                               |
| ..               |                                               |          |        |                          |                                                              |                                                                                                                       |
| Group number     | Last group                                    | Uint_16  | 2      |                          | `1 ... +48`                     | `00 01 ... 00 30`                                                                        |
| Activation       | Activate / deactivate the group               | Bool_1   | 1      | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1`                        | `00<br>01`                                                                               |

**Example: sMN ActivateObjectEvaluationGroup**

<summary markdown="block">

### Set Object Evaluation Configuration [sMN SetObjectEvaluationConfiguration]

</summary>

This telegram changes the name and the criteria of an existing object evaluation. Write all parameters; read the current configuration first and change only the values you need. The example sets evaluation 1 to moving objects of at least 200 mm width with a speed between 300 mm/s and 15000 mm/s.

Values outside the allowed range are rejected with `sFA 30`, and a name longer than 20 characters with `sFA 7`. A minimum that is greater than its maximum, for example for the size or speed, returns error code 2.

<section class="cola-category" markdown="1">

## Perpendicular Distance

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Request Perpendicular Distance Once [sRN perpendicularDistanceResult]

</summary>

This telegram can be used to request the perpendicular distance. The shortest and furthest measuring point in a range to a reference plane will be transmitted. A field and a reference plane must be defined in the user interface under Application > Perpendicular distance measurement.

**Telegram structure: sRN perpendicularDistanceResult**

### Request Perpendicular Distance Continuously on Event [sEN perpendicularDistanceResult]

</summary>

This telegram can be used to request the perpendicular distance continuously on event. The shortest and furthest measuring point in a range to a reference plane will be transmitted. A field and a reference plane must be defined in the user interface under Application > Perpendicular distance measurement.

**Telegram structure: sEN perpendicularDistanceResult**

| Telegram part | Description                   | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII)                                      | Values CoLa B (Binary)                                                                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------- | -------- | ------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command type  | Event                         | String   | 3      |                    | `sEN`                         | `73 45 4E`                                                                         |
| Command       | Perpendicular distance values | String   | 27     |                    | `perpendicularDistanceResult` | `70 65 72 70 65 6E 64 69 63 75 6C 61 72 44 69 73 74 61 6E 63 65 52 65 73 75 6C 74` |
| Start/ Stop   | -                             | Enum_8   | 1      | Stop:<br>Start:    | `0<br>1`                      | `00<br>01`                                                                         |

# multiScan100 Electrical Connection and Pin Assignment

> Wire a multiScan100 power, Ethernet, and digital I/O system plug to a controller using the documented M12 pin assignments.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/electrical-connection/

# Electrical Connection

Compatible with: multiScan100

To check whether the sensor still receives its minimum supply voltage at the end of a long cable, use the [Cable Dimensioning](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cable-dimensioning/) calculator.

## Power / 3 IOs 

System plug part number: 2116047

![System plug 2116047 with Ethernet and 5-pin power connectors](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical/system-plug-2116047.png){ width="320" }
*System plug 2116047 for power and three configurable digital I/Os.*

This system plug uses a male, 5-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![5-pin PWR connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/multiscan100-pwr-5.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">5-pin PWR connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR / 3 IOs** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 2 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 3 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 4 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 5 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |

## Power / 8 IOs 

System plug part number: 2130754

![System plug 2130754 with Ethernet and 12-pin power and I/O connectors](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical/system-plug-12-pin.png){ width="320" }
*System plug 2130754 with a 12-pin power and I/O connector.*

This system plug uses a male, 12-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![12-pin PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/multiscan100-pwr-12.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">12-pin PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR / 8 IOs** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 2 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 3 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 4 | `IN7/OUT7` | Configurable digital input 7 or output 7 |
| 5 | `IN8/OUT8` | Configurable digital input 8 or output 8 |
| 6 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |
| 7 | `IN4/OUT4` | Configurable digital input 4 or output 4 |
| 8 | `IN6/OUT6` | Configurable digital input 6 or output 6 |
| 9 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 10 | `IN5/OUT5` | Configurable digital input 5 or output 5 |
| 11 | — | Reserved; do not connect |
| 12 | — | Reserved; do not connect |

## Ethernet

The Ethernet connection uses a female, 4-pin, D-coded M12 connector.

![Ethernet connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/multiscan100-ethernet.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">Ethernet connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Ethernet** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `TX+` | Transmit + |
| 2 | `RX+` | Receive + |
| 3 | `TX-` | Transmit − |
| 4 | `RX-` | Receive − |

# multiScan100 Firmware Release Notes

> Changes, new features, improvements, bug fixes, and known issues in the multiScan100 firmware 2.x.x releases.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/release-notes/

# Release Notes

This page summarizes firmware changes for the multiScan100 product family
from firmware version 2.x.x. Check the release and device variant before
updating or using a feature.

## General Information

- Firmware 2.x.x is the standard firmware for all multiScan100 variants.
- multiScan100-S has a separate firmware file, which must be requested.
- A firmware update typically does not affect active parameter settings.
- Purchased licenses are not affected by firmware upgrades.
- Reboot the device after activating or deactivating licenses.

## Update Instructions

multiScan100 firmware can be updated through SOPAS ET, Sentio Creator, or the
web UI (SOPASair) with an `.spk` software package. For the steps, see
[Firmware Update](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/).

**Update via SOPASair.**

Firmware updates through SOPASair in a web browser are supported from version
2.4.1. Use the signed `.spk.signed` package. Start the update from the device
menu or from the link on the displayed firmware version.

## Firmware 2.5.0

**Release date:** 22 October 2026

**Effective from:** SN2644xxxx

**3D Object Evaluation / 3D Object Tracking.**

- New [3D Object Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/object-evaluation/)
  functionality using tracked object characteristics.
- Filtering by stationary or moving objects, object size, speed, direction of
  movement, and age.
- A detailed description is available in the online help in SOPASair.
- Available within the **3D Object Detection Advanced Package**.

![SOPASair light-mode 3D Object Evaluation view with tracked objects and their characteristics](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/firmware-250-object-evaluation-light.png)
*Firmware 2.5.0: tracked objects and their characteristics in the SOPASair 3D Object Evaluation view.*

**Optimization of Motor Parameters.**

- Improved motor control for increased robustness and stability.
- Improved measurement data availability under challenging operating conditions.

**GUI.**

- New **Dark Mode**.
- Updated GUI for 3D Object Evaluation.
- Updated error and notification messages.
- General usability improvements.

![SOPASair Dark Mode showing the 3D Object Evaluation view](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/firmware-250-object-evaluation-dark.png)
*Firmware 2.5.0: SOPASair Dark Mode with the 3D Object Evaluation view.*

## Firmware 2.4.4

**Release date:** 5 May 2026. Firmware 2.4.3 was not released.

**New features.**

- Firmware 2.4.4 is available for multiScan165S. The previous firmware for
  that variant is 2.3.0.
- Ground Filter and Perpendicular Distance are available as non-safety-related
  add-ons for multiScan165S with Safe 3D Object Detection
  (part number 1151596). See the current multiScan165S operating
  instructions for details.

**Optimization.**

The FPGA version was updated for production optimization. Firmware 2.4.4 is
functionally identical to 2.4.2.

**Known issues.**

Contamination-indication sectors may not be saved permanently and can be lost
after a reboot.

As a workaround, import an appropriate sensor configuration after reboot and
verify the sector setup. Use the REST `/ContaminationConfig` endpoint or the
CoLa A/B `sWN ContaminationConfig` telegram for parameterization.

## Firmware 2.4.2

**Release date:** 20 October 2025

**New features.**

Firmware 2.4.2 adds support for multiScan166. Earlier firmware versions do not
support multiScan166.

## Firmware 2.4.1

**Release date:** 20 October 2025

**New features.**

**Ground Filter.**

The Ground Filter provides upper and lower ground-threshold values. In
applications with moving objects, it can reduce false field-evaluation
triggers caused by the ground. When configured correctly, it is intended to
retain detection of small objects such as forklift tines. The filter can be
used indoors and outdoors. It affects both field evaluation and Perpendicular
Distance.

**Perpendicular Distance.**

For an object inside a configured box-shaped field, Perpendicular Distance
can output the object's minimum and maximum distance to an axis (X, Y, or Z).
Use `sRN perpendicularDistanceResult` for a one-time request and
`sEN perpendicularDistanceResult` for event-based output.

**Firmware update via web GUI.**

Firmware can be updated through the web GUI without SOPAS ET, using the
signed `.spk.signed` package.

**Parameter import and export.**

The firmware adds parameter import and export through the web GUI.

**GUI optimization and feature enhancements.**

- The multiScan-S is now shown with a yellow ring in the GUI. Previously,
  it was not visually distinguishable from other variants.
- Field contours uploaded by telegram are transferred directly to the web
  UI.
- The Cybersecurity overview shows that the Maintenance and Authorized
  Client user levels are disabled by default. They can be enabled in the GUI
  after logging in at the Service user level.
- HTTPS is supported for multiScan100 GUI components.
- Full-screen mode can be selected by adding `?fullscreen_mode=` to the scan
  view URL.
- The web update file dialog allows only signed `.spk` files.
- The scan-layer filter has a redesigned interface that makes enabled and
  disabled layers easier to identify. Each layer can be deactivated
  individually with a click.
- The distance filter displays minimum- and maximum-distance spheres to show
  the selected area.
- An Undo button was added next to Save.
- The Fullscreen button was moved from the top line next to split view to the
  device menu.
- The DHCP fallback mode was changed to Static IP.
- The `GetFieldEvaluationContour` telegram was implemented.

**Temperature improvements.**

The temperature range was extended from +50 °C to +60 °C when the device is
mounted with standard bracket 2130373. The device does not shut off when its
temperature exceeds the configured limits.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Firmware 2.4.1:** usage condition and mission time.</p>

| Usage condition | Mission time |
| --- | --- |
| Continuous use at 25 °C | 42 years |
| Continuous use rarely above 30 °C | 37.5 years |
| 55% of the time up to 30 °C, 35% up to 40 °C, and 10% up to 50 °C | 20 years |
| 70% of the time up to 30 °C and 30% up to 50 °C | 18 years |
| 80% of the time up to 30 °C and 20% up to 60 °C | 13.4 years |
| Continuous use at 50 °C | 8 years |

When a configured temperature range is exceeded, an output can be switched.
Use these telegrams for temperature warnings:

- Read current device temperature alarm status:
  `sRN temperatureAlarmStatus`
- Set device temperature alarm configuration:
  `sWN temperatureAlarmConfiguration`
- Read device temperature alarm configuration:
  `sRN temperatureAlarmConfiguration`

**Bug fixes.**

- Harmonized sensor behavior with other LiDAR sensors.
- Fixed diagnostic dumps not downloading through the GUI.
- Fixed measurement data sometimes not appearing in the UI after a browser
  refresh.
- Fixed an error when creating fields with X/Y extents greater than 100 m.
- Fixed missing layer selection in the Object Detection scheme.
- Fixed the queue-overflow error not resetting when streaming was stopped
  while the error was active.

## Firmware 2.3.0

**Release date:** 2 December 2024

**New features.**

- **High-resolution layers in 3D Object Detection:** Choose among 14
  one-degree scan layers or either of two high-resolution layers (2D scan
  layers 6 or 14). A field can be configured multiple times with different
  sources. multiScan165 does not have high-resolution layers.
- **Detection History:** The 3D Object Detection software adds a page for
  reviewing field-infringement history and logs of current field status.
- **REST firmware update:** Firmware updates can be performed using REST.
- **Online Help:** Existing help was updated with new content and guidance.
- **I/O application:** Adds a warning when I/O ports cannot be created and
  removes `FieldEvaluationAppState` from the source list.
- **CoLa1 password handling:** ROM passwords were removed; only RAM
  passwords are permitted.
- **Third-party components:** Updated to newer versions.
- **GUI changes:** Input configuration is visible when Port 1 is set to
  Input; the start page can show field evaluation or measurement data; the
  Field Evaluation Scan GUI can receive scan layers (for multiScan136, both
  one-degree and high-resolution layers); and the I/O status display was
  redesigned.

**Bug fixes and improvements.**

- IMU errors, including missing data delivery, now generate an error
  notification.
- Fixed mounting position not being written when set in the SOPAS ET device
  window.
- More than 20 sources can now be connected to a single output. Previously,
  exceeding 20 sources produced an error.
- PTP is no longer shown in the selection list when no PTP license is
  available.
- Switching between streaming and field-evaluation views is disabled when
  either required license is missing.
- System Diagnosis displays the sensor's local time when configured, instead
  of UTC.
- Corrected the translation of “No echo” to “Ignore missing echo.”
- Duplicated evaluations now appear immediately in the GUI without
  reloading the browser. Previously, duplicated fields were not displayed
  and could not be deleted.
- Fixed the maximum-range circle being tilted; it is positioned in the
  scanner's zero-degree layer.
- Fixed the preset mounting position not being displayed correctly.
- The frame count displayed for field-evaluation response time now reflects
  the scanning frequency correctly. Previously, a 50 ms response time could
  incorrectly be shown as three frames.
- Online Help no longer overlaps the settings area.
- Opening Object Detection and rapidly clicking **+** no longer produces
  `Access Denied (/api/EvaluationGroupMapping)`.
- White points are visible in Echo View.
- Fixed CoLa 2 reading and writing of Port Configuration and Source List.
- Fixed deserialization of Compact azimuth angles above pi.
- Cleaned up different API interfaces.

**Known issues.**

**Hardware.**

At startup, the motor may not begin rotating immediately and a **Motor
Stalled** error may appear in the error log. The sensorless motor driver
cannot measure the current frequency at startup. It retries its start sequence,
which may take up to six seconds; after ten seconds, software resets the driver
module.

**Firmware.**

- `DoDiagnosis` increases system load and can adversely affect measurement
  operation, potentially causing additional errors.
- While the GUI creates a diagnostic file, the device LED can remain green
  and the status can show **READY** even though 3D Object Detection and field
  evaluation are blocked. Normal operation resumes when file generation is
  complete.
- Ports configured as inputs with a 5-pin system plug do not work with
  **Active Low**.

**Application and UI.**

- In the **Upper Z limit** field, the cursor can jump vertically when the
  field is empty; this does not occur when it contains text.
- Device-name assignment can produce an error.
- A soft reset triggered through the UI can cause web-server error messages.
- Creating fields with an X/Y extent greater than 100 m can cause an error
  and prevent field evaluation from working.
- The queue-overflow error is not reset when streaming stops while the error
  is active.
- Layer selection is missing in the Object Detection scheme.
- Duplicating evaluations can fail after a group and evaluation are created,
  one evaluation is duplicated, and the original is deleted. Adding a new
  evaluation with ID 1 allows duplication again.

## Firmware 2.2.2

**Compatible with:** multiScan100; **Release date:** 19 August 2024

**New features.**

**Licensed 3D Object Detection for multiScan165.**

The licensed SensorApp was already available for multiScan136. For
multiScan165, it supports collision avoidance and area monitoring, with up
to 48 configurable fields. The evaluation uses real elevation angles based
on each sensor's production calibration data. It improves evaluation of object
position and size for multiScan136 and multiScan165, using all 16 layers for
multiScan165.

More simultaneously active fields require more processing and increase
system load. Excessive load can cause performance problems or system errors.
Deactivating other features, such as the GUI, measurement-data output, and
filters, can reduce load and allow more fields to be active.

- Additional GUI languages were added.
- An internal recorder can record and play back data on the device; a
  separate recorder tool is required.
- `sRN FieldEvaluationGroupState` reads evaluation-group state:
  `0` = not configured, `1` = active, `2` = inactive.
- Online Help was updated.
- Scan-GUI visualization was optimized, including use of scanner-specific
  elevation angles.
- The GUI now warns when an object is too small compared with the layer
  distance.
- Support for multiScan165 was added.

**Fixes, improvements, and changes.**

- Improved port selection in 3D Object Detection; ports already in use are
  no longer selectable.
- Improved resource monitoring in 3D Object Detection. Warnings indicate
  potential high load and help identify which functions use resources;
  creating additional fields no longer produces an error message, only
  warnings.
- Applied performance optimizations.
- Improved the GUI structure.
- Aligned contamination-indication and warning-LED behavior.
- Improved 3D Object Detection field visualization.
- Fields can now be duplicated more than four consecutive times, and group
  deletion works correctly.
- Applying the current system time now assigns the required internal
  variables correctly, preventing an incorrect system-time display.
- Mounting settings are visible without an IMU license.
- Improved contamination-indication timing and error handling.
- Field points deleted in the 3D Object Detection table view are now also
  removed from the graphical view, so both views show the same values.
- Corrected display of umlauts in the Input/Output window.
- Reduced the internally blocked `169.254.x.x` IP address range.
- The **Reset and maintain communication interface** button now performs
  the reset correctly.
- System timestamps, including IMU, 3D Object Detection, and scan timestamps,
  are in UTC.
- The interval filter now starts at `2`.
- Removed the sensitivity setting from Inputs/Outputs (edge/level).
- When more than three echoes are measured, the last echo is used instead of
  the third.
- An application-state error now changes the device state to error.
- Queue-overflow errors are shown only when data loss occurs.

**Known issues.**

- More than 100 field points can produce a duplicate error message.
- In Object Detection, quickly clicking **+** after opening the page can
  produce `Access Denied (/api/EvaluationGroupMapping)`.
- Duplicating fields may not work correctly. Press **F5** to refresh the
  browser as a workaround.
- GUI CPU usage can increase over time. If the GUI freezes, close and reopen
  the browser.
- Connecting more than 20 sources to an output produces an error.
- The change-password dialog may not disappear.
- An incorrect error message is shown if polygon points exceed 100 m.
- The queue-overflow error is not reset when streaming stops while the error
  is active.

**Firmware hash.**

The published SHA-256 hash for the firmware file is:

`110a4eb514b7ec868ecd97f2fc40ec8418dd5e5f56a7e48a099d649e3a84e2b6`

Compare a downloaded file's SHA-256 fingerprint with the value published by
SICK to check that the file has not been corrupted or manipulated.

**Chrome 128 scan-view issue.**

During tests with the Chrome 128 beta, measurement data was not displayed in
the 2D and 3D SOPASair visualizations. SOPAS ET was not affected. Microsoft
Edge was also affected because it uses the same software base.

Workarounds are to update the sensor to the latest firmware, use Firefox, use
SOPAS ET, or use Chrome Portable version 127 or earlier. Firmware 2.2.2
contains a fix for this issue.

# multiScan100 Web Interface (SOPASair)

> Navigate the multiScan100 SOPASair web interface to configure scan output, filters, field evaluation, and device settings.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/graphical-user-interface/

# SOPASair Walkthrough

SOPASair is the built-in web interface of the multiScan100 for
parameterization, service, and diagnostics. It runs directly on the sensor,
so no software installation is needed. Connect the sensor to the same
network as your computer and open `http://<sensor-ip>/` in a browser. The
factory default address is `192.168.0.1`.

You can view status and settings without logging in. To change settings,
log in with the **Authorized Client** user level using the user icon in the
top bar.

![SOPASair Home dashboard showing multiScan165 status, 3D live view with field evaluation, I/O states, and detection history](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-home-overview.png)
*The SOPASair Home dashboard: device status, 3D live view with field evaluation, input and output states, and detection history at a glance.*

## Home

The Home page summarizes the sensor's state. It is a good place to start
before you change any settings.

**Status** shows separate indicators for the device, connection,
measurement, field evaluation, and data output. Because each state is
reported independently, the sensor can be measuring while no data is sent
to an external receiver.

![multiScan165 device and application status](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-status.png)
*Device and application status indicators.*

**Device information** lists the model, part number, serial number, firmware
version, system time, and the time of the last save. Check the firmware
version before you use a firmware-specific API example. Click
**Find device** to make the sensor LEDs blink, so you can identify the unit
on site.

![multiScan165 device information](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-device-information.png)
*Device identity and installed firmware version.*

## Configuration

The Configuration menu contains the measurement, filter, mounting, network,
and I/O settings. For the matching REST parameters, value ranges, and
variant-specific limits, see the
[multiScan100 OpenAPI reference](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/).

### Basic Settings

**Configuration > Basic settings** contains interlaced mode, the status LED,
and the measurement state.

![multiScan165 basic settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-basic-settings.png)
*Interlaced mode, LED, and measurement settings.*

**Date and system time** shows the device clock and its synchronization
source. **Apply computer time** sets the sensor clock to your computer's
time. For network-based time sources, see
[Time synchronization](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/time-synchronization/).

![multiScan165 date and system time](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-date-time.png)
*Device clock and time synchronization settings.*

### Filter

**Configuration > Filter** combines the fog, echo, particle, and
moving-average filters. The echo filter selects all, first, or last echoes,
and the moving-average filter sets the averaging depth. See
[Filter details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/) to choose the right
filters for your application.

![multiScan165 filter settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-filters.png)
*Fog, echo, particle, and moving-average filters.*

### Mounting

**Configuration > Mounting** describes how the sensor is installed. Select a
preset mounting position or enter the orientation angles and position
offsets. **Adjust fields to mounting position** moves existing fields to
match the new mounting, and **Accept IMU data** takes the orientation from
the internal IMU.

![multiScan165 mounting position](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-mounting.png)
*Mounting position, orientation, and offsets.*

The **Inertial measuring unit (IMU)** panel shows the current orientation
and acceleration. Because the IMU is not calibrated, use its values as a
starting point for the mounting orientation, not as a precise measurement.

![multiScan165 live IMU readings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-imu.png)
*IMU orientation and acceleration.*

### Contamination Indication

**Configuration > Contamination indication** monitors the front window for
dirt. The sector diagram shows the contamination state per sector, using
the color legend below it. You can configure whether a warning or error is
output, the sensitivity, the monitored sectors, the handling of blocked
sectors, and the response delay. See
[Contamination indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/contamination-indication/) for
the application background.

![multiScan165 contamination indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-contamination.png)
*Contamination status per sector and evaluation settings.*

### Connection Options

**Configuration > Connection options** contains the Ethernet settings:
addressing mode, IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, MAC address, and
link speed.

When you click **Apply**, the new network settings take effect immediately.
The browser loses its connection if the sensor moves to an address that your
computer cannot reach, so note the new address before applying the change.

![multiScan165 Ethernet settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-ethernet.png)
*Ethernet addressing and link settings.*

### Inputs and Outputs

**Configuration > Inputs and outputs** assigns each port a name and a
direction. For outputs, select the signal source, inversion, logic, and
restart behavior. The connector diagram next to each port shows the
corresponding pin. The status panels below show the current input and
output states, and **Reset counters** clears the output switching counters.

![multiScan165 input and output assignments](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-inputs-outputs.png)
*Port assignments with connector pin diagrams.*

## Application

The Application menu contains measurement-data output and field
evaluation. Some variants offer additional functions. For example, the
multiScan165S with Safe 3D Object Detection adds a ground filter and
perpendicular distance measurement as non-safety-related functions.

### Data Output

**Application > Data output** selects the measurement-data format, MSGPACK
or Compact, and the UDP destination address and port. Start or stop the
data stream from the same panel. See
[Data streaming](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/) to choose a receiver and
parser.

![multiScan165 measurement-data output](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-data-output.png)
*Output format, UDP destination, and stream control.*

IMU data is streamed separately, with its own destination address, port,
and start/stop control.

![multiScan165 IMU output](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-imu-output.png)
*IMU data output.*

**Data reduction** limits the output by scan layer, angular range, and
output interval. **Range filter** removes points outside a cuboid area or a
distance window. If layers or points are missing from the received data,
check these settings together with the output format.

![multiScan165 data reduction](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-data-reduction.png)
*Scan-layer, angular-range, and interval reduction.*

![multiScan165 range filters](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-range-filter.png)
*Cuboid-area and distance filters.*

### Field Evaluation

**Application > Field evaluation** monitors fields for objects and switches
outputs when a field is infringed. Each group combines fields, evaluations,
and outputs, and has its own activation source. **Resource requirements**
shows how much of the sensor's evaluation capacity is in use, and
**Detection list** shows recent detections.

![multiScan165 field evaluation groups](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-field-evaluation.png)
*Evaluation groups with their activation sources.*

See [Field evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/) for a complete
commissioning procedure and API support.

### Perpendicular Distance Measurement

Where supported by the device variant and software package, perpendicular
distance measurement evaluates points within a field relative to a reference
line. The results include minimum and maximum perpendicular distances and
the positions of the corresponding measuring points.

See [Perpendicular Distance Measurement](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/perpendicular-distance-measurement/)
for configuration steps and result interfaces.

### Object Evaluation

Object Evaluation provides object properties such as size, speed, and
direction for decisions based on object criteria rather than only field
infringements. It is available from multiScan100 firmware 2.5.0; check the
device variant and installed software package for support.

See [Object Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/object-evaluation/)
for an introduction and application example.

## Diagnostics

### Overview

**Diagnostics > Overview** combines status, device information, operating
information, the current device status, and the message log. Expand
**Operating information** to see the number of power-on cycles, the
operating hours, and the time of the last parameterization.

![multiScan165 operating information](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-operating-information.png)
*Power-on count, operating hours, and last parameterization.*

The message table lists current and past events with their status, number,
time, description, and counter. **Current device status** shows only the
messages that are still active. If you need support, use
**Create diagnostic file** to collect the device state in one file and send
it to SICK. See [Contact](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/contact/).

### Cybersecurity

**Diagnostics > Cybersecurity** shows the HTTPS certificates and the
**Services and protocols** table. The table lists each service with its
purpose and port, so you can enable only the services your integration
needs. See [HTTPS and certificates](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/https-and-certificates/)
for the complete certificate setup.

![multiScan165 services and protocols](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-services-protocols.png)
*Services and protocols with their ports.*

The service list is specific to the device and firmware shown. For the
multiScan165 port reference and the separately configurable measurement-data
ports, see the [Cybersecurity network-services matrix](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cybersecurity/#multiscan100-multiscan165).

### Data Recorder

**Diagnostics > Data recorder** explains how to install the SICK data
recorder on your computer and connect it to the sensor. Use the recorder
to capture measurement data for later analysis or support cases.

![multiScan165 recorder instructions](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-recorder.png)
*Installation and connection steps for the data recorder.*

### Detection History

**Diagnostics > Detection history** records field-evaluation detections.
Select the evaluations to include, then start the history. The
**Statistics** section counts the detections per evaluation, and the
**Detection list** shows each event with its time stamp. Use
**Reset detection history** to clear the counters.

![multiScan165 detection history](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan100/img/sopasair-detection-statistics.png)
*Detection counts per evaluation.*

# multiScan200 Overview

> Developer entry point for the SICK multiScan200 3D LiDAR family (multiScan270): web GUI, REST API, CoLa telegrams, native ROS 2, and firmware release notes.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/

# multiScan200

The multiScan200 is a compact 3D LiDAR sensor family with high detection reliability in harsh environments. The first variant is the multiScan270.

[Specifications and data sheet on sick.com](https://www.sick.com/de/en/search?text=multiScan200)

<div class="product-scans product-scans--single">
  <picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="../assets/multiScan200/img/multiscan270-scan-layers.png"><img src="https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/multiscan270-scan-layers.gif" width="392" height="239" alt="multiScan270 with up to 192 scan layers and labelled physical elevation limits of −22.5° downward and +22.5° upward"></picture>
  *multiScan270: up to 192 layers, 45° vertical and 360° horizontal coverage, depending on configuration. Schematic infrared beams in blue; angles are positive upward.*
</div>

On sick.com, open your device variant's download area for firmware, EPLAN and CAD data,
and available NVIDIA Isaac Sim models and Milestone XProtect plug-ins.
See [Release Notes](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/release-notes/) for firmware changes.

#### [GET /InertialMeasurementUnit](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-rest-openapi/#rest-get-inertialmeasurementunit)

Returns the current IMU data (e.g. Acceleration, Orientation, ... ). The data is given in the following coordinate system which is based on the DIN70000 system. The x-axis lies on the 90-degree-beam of the 0-degree-layer. The y-axis is perpendicular to the x-axis and lies in the 0-degree-layer. The y-values are rising in the counterclockwise rotation direction (right-handed system). The z-axis is perpendicular to the x-y-plane and the scanner top points to rising z-values.

**Try the request**

Copy this command into a terminal. In Windows PowerShell, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```bash
curl --request GET "http://192.168.0.1/api/InertialMeasurementUnit"
```

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**
| `header` |

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-rest-openapi/#schema-responseheader)

 |
| --- | --- |
| `data` |
| `Acceleration` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 3

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Default:** 0.0

 |
| `AngularVelocity` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 3

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Default:** 0.0

 |
| `Orientation` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 4

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Default:** 0.0

 |
| `TimeStamp` |

**Type:** integer

# multiScan200 API | CoLa Telegrams (CoLa A and CoLa B)

> multiScan200 CoLa telegram reference with sRN, sWN, sMN, and sEN commands, parameter structures, and CoLa A and CoLa B examples.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-cola-telegrams/

# API | CoLa Telegrams

This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the multiScan200. Use the command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level integrations without guessing the telegram structure.

Examples are grouped by protocol, with each telegram representation in a separate code block and its own copy button.

Categories follow the [multiScan200 REST API reference](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-rest-openapi/)
where corresponding CoLa telegrams are available. Select a telegram to expand
its structure and examples. A direct link to a telegram opens it automatically.
The categories organize the reference; availability still depends on the
device variant, firmware, and installed software packages.

<section class="cola-category" markdown="1">

## General

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]

</summary>

The password hashes of the default passwords are documented in the operating instructions (PDF) of your device. Do not pass them on, and change the passwords during commissioning.

A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. On delivery, only the Service user level is enabled; until a Service user enables Maintenance or Authorized client, the device answers a log in with these levels with `sAN SetAccessMode 0` (see [User Levels](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/)). Changed parameters will be reset to the previous state via a reboot unless they are saved. To save parameter changes the command "sMN mEEwriteall" must be sent before log out.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | User level | String | 13 | | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| User level | Select user level | Int_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `2<br>3<br>4` | `02<br>03<br>04` |
| Password | Hash value for the selected user level | Uint_32 | 4 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `<password hash>` | `<password hash>` |

**Example: sMN SetAccessMode - Log in as “Authorized client”**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}3{SPC}<password hash><ETX>
```

```text
sMN SetAccessMode 3 <password hash>
```


**Telegram structure: sAN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sAN` | `73 41 4E` |
| Command | User level | String | 13 | | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| Change user level | Changed level | Bool_1 | 1 | Error:<br>Success: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sAN SetAccessMode**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sAN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
02 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 13 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 01 38
```

</details>

### Enable or Disable CoLa User Levels [sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel]

</summary>

This command enables and disables a specific CoLa user level (Maintenance, Authorized Client).

**Telegram structure: sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Enable/ disable CoLa user level | String | 21 | | `EnableLegacyUserLevel` | `45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C` |
| User level | - | Uint_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized Client: | `2<br>3` | `02<br>03` |
| Status | Enable/ disable | Bool_1 | 1 | Disable:<br>Enable: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel - Enable Authorized client**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}EnableLegacyUserLevel{SPC}3{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel 3 1
```

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Change Password [sMN SetPassword]

</summary>

Change the log in password of a user level. If you are logged in with a higher user level, you can also set the password of lower user levels.

The password is sent as a hash value. To calculate it, log in to SOPASair as Service and open **Diagnosis > Cybersecurity > Hash calculator**. For example, the hash value of the password `testtest` is `1920E4C9`.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetPassword**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Set password request | String | 11 | | `SetPassword` | `53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64` |
| User level | User level that the password will be applied to | Int_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `2<br>3<br>4` | `02<br>03<br>04` |
| Password | Hash value of the new password | Uint_32 | 4 | | `<Hash value>` | |

**Example: sMN SetPassword - Set the Authorized client password to "testtest"**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}SetPassword{SPC}3{SPC}1920E4C9<ETX>
```

```text
sMN SetPassword 3 1920E4C9
```

```text
02 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64 20 33 20 31 39 32 30 45 34 43 39 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 15 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64 20 03 19 20 E4 C9 1A
```

```text
73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64 20 03 19 20 E4 C9
```


**Telegram structure: sAN SetPassword**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sAN` | `73 41 4E` |
| Command | Set password requested | String | 11 | | `SetPassword` | `53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64` |
| Success | Confirmation | Int_8 | 1 | Failed:<br>Success: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sAN SetPassword**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sAN{SPC}SetPassword{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
02 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 50 61 73 73 77 6F 72 64 20 01 00
```

</details>

### Set Scan Configuration [sMN mCLsetscancfglist]

</summary>

Select the scan configuration (field of view, scanning frequency, and angular resolution) by its number. Scan configurations 10 to 12 use interlace mode: they achieve a higher angular resolution by combining scans that are shifted to each other. The supported scan configurations are listed in the parameter table below. Read the active scan configuration with `sRN PerformanceProfileNumber`. To set it, use [`sWN PerformanceProfileNumber`](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-cola-telegrams/#set-performance-profile-swn-performanceprofilenumber).

In CoLa A, a number without a sign is hexadecimal: send scan configuration 10 as `+10` or `A`, not as `10`.

### Set Device Time [sMN LSPsetdatetime]

</summary>

Set the device time: year, month, day, hour, minute, second, and microsecond. In CoLa A, write decimal values with a leading `+`; values without a sign are hexadecimal.

The device has no real-time clock. After a power cycle, the time must be set again, or use NTP or PTP.

Required user level: Authorized client.

**Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Set time stamp | String | 14 | | `LSPsetdatetime` | `4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65` |
| Year | | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+1970d …+2099d (07B2h… 0833h)` | `07 B2 … 08 33` |
| Month | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch)` | `01 … 0C` |
| Day | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh)` | `00 … 1F` |
| Hour | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +23d(00h … 17h)` | `00 … 17` |
| Minute | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)` | `00 … 3B` |
| Second | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)` | `00 … 3B` |
| Microsecond | | Uint_32 | 4 | | `+0d …+999999d(00000000h …000F423Fh)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F` |

**Example: sMN LSPsetdatetime**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}+2026{SPC}+10{SPC}+1{SPC}+16{SPC}+52{SPC}+1{SPC}0<ETX>
```

```text
sMN LSPsetdatetime +2026 +10 +1 +16 +52 +1 0
```

```text
02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 2B 32 30 32 36 20 2B 31 30 20 2B 31 20 2B 31 36 20 2B 35 32 20 2B 31 20 30 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 EA 0A 01 10 34 01 00 00 00 00 9F
```

```text
73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 EA 0A 01 10 34 01 00 00 00 00
```

## Filter

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Particle Filter [sWN particleFilter]

</summary>

Configure the particle filter. A point is a particle if fewer than the minimum number of neighbors in its 8-connected neighborhood, over all echoes, are within the distance threshold. See [Filter Details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/#particle-filter).

Required user level: Authorized client.

**Telegram structure: sWN particleFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write request | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Variable name | Particle filter | String | 14 | | `particleFilter` | `70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |
| enable | If true a detected particle is filtered out (aka distance set to zero) and subsequent echoes are moved up. Otherwise, the point is flagged in the properties channel. | Bool_1 | 1 | False:<br>True: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| minNumberOfNeighbors | If a measurement has less points in its 8-connected neighborhood over all echoes within the distance threshold, this measurement is considered as particle. | Uint_16 | 2 | Max: 8 | `+1` | `00 01` |
| distanceThreshold | Distance threshold value. For a given measurement all points in the 8-connected neighborhood over all three echoes are with a distance less than the distanceThreshold are counted. If the result is below the minNumberOfNeighbors, this measurement is considered as particle | Uint_16 | 2 | Max: 2000 | `+500` | `01 F4` |

**Example: sWN particleFilter - Disable the particle filter**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWN{SPC}particleFilter{SPC}0{SPC}+1{SPC}+500<ETX>
```

```text
sWN particleFilter 0 +1 +500
```

```text
02 73 57 4E 20 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 30 20 2B 31 20 2B 35 30 30 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 18 73 57 4E 20 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 00 00 01 01 F4 AA
```

```text
73 57 4E 20 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 00 00 01 01 F4
```


**Telegram structure: sWA particleFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
