## Contamination Indication

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Contamination Indication Settings [sWN ContaminationConfig]

</summary>

Define how and when the device signals a potential contamination of the optics cover, so that it can be cleaned in time. See [Contamination Indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/contamination-indication/).

Required user level: Authorized client.

**Telegram structure: sWN ContaminationConfig**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | | String | 19 | | `ContaminationConfig` | `43 6F 6E 74 61 6D 69 6E 61 74 69 6F 6E 43 6F 6E 66 69 67` |
| Strategy | Strategy code | Enum_8 | 1 | Inactive:<br>High available:<br>Sensitive: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Response time | How fast (in seconds) the sensor reacts after a contamination | Uint_16 | 2 | 3 … 60, default 3 | `+3d … +60d (3 … 3Ch)` | `00 03 … 00 3C` |
| Threshold warning | Sensitivity | Enum_8 | 1 | Low:<br>Medium:<br>High: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Cover | No cover, weather protection hood, or custom sectors | Enum_8 | 1 | No cover:<br>Weather protection hood:<br>Custom sectors: | `0<br>6<br>+255d (FFh)` | `00<br>06<br>FF` |
| Number of sectors | Number of the following sector values | Uint_16 | 2 | Always 12 | `C` | `00 0C` |
| Custom sector | Sector 1 … 12 is evaluated, one value per sector | Bool_1 | 1 | Inactive:<br>Active (default): | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Enable warning | Warning monitoring | Bool_1 | 1 | Off:<br>On: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Enable error | Error monitoring | Bool_1 | 1 | Off:<br>On: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sWN ContaminationConfig**

```text

```

</summary>

| IP address | Set values | Uint_8 | 1 | Third part of IP address | `0 …+255d (00 … FF)` | `00 … FF` |

### Read State of the Ports [sRN LIDportstate]

</summary>

Read the state and the change counter of all ports. The answer contains 8 internal (physical) ports and 8 external (virtual) ports. A tri-state port is neither input nor output; it is set inactive in the configuration.

**Telegram structure: sRN LIDportstate**

| Internal port state | Port 1 … 8, one state and one counter per port | Enum_8 | 1 | Output voltage low (relay open):<br>Output voltage high (relay closed):<br>Tri-state (port inactive):<br>Input voltage high (level) or low to high (edge):<br>Input voltage low (level) or high to low (edge): | `0<br>1<br>2<br>3<br>4` | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03<br>04` |

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Port Configuration [sWN PortConfiguration]

</summary>

Write the configuration of the digital inputs and outputs, with one record per port. The record has the same structure as in the answer of `sRN PortConfiguration`; read the current configuration first and change only the values you need.

**Telegram structure: sWN PortConfiguration**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Configuration of the given ports | String | 17 | | `PortConfiguration` | `50 6F 72 74 43 6F 6E 66 69 67 75 72 61 74 69 6F 6E` |
| Port type | Port 1 … 8, the following rows repeat for every port | Enum_8 | 1 | Input:<br>Output: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Port name length | Number of characters of the port name | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0 … 20` | `00 00 … 00 20` |
| Port name | Name of the port | String | Length | | `InOut1` | `49 6E 4F 75 74 31` |
| Input logic | Logic of the input | Bool_1 | 1 | Active high:<br>Active low: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Debouncing | Debouncing time in ms | Uint_16 | 2 | Maximum 10,000 ms | `0 … 2710` | `00 00 … 27 10` |
| Reserved | - | Enum_8 | 1 | | `1` | `01` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |
| Output logic | Logic of the output | Bool_1 | 1 | Active high:<br>Active low: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Output mode | PNP, NPN, or push-pull | Enum_8 | 1 | PNP:<br>NPN:<br>Push-pull: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Restart type | Restart behavior of the output after an event | Enum_8 | 1 | Immediately:<br>Time:<br>Input: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Restart time | Only with restart type Time, in ms | Uint_32 | 4 | 20 … 600,000 ms | `14 … 927C0` | `00 00 00 14 … 00 09 27 C0` |
| Restart input | Only with restart type Input, input used for the restart | Uint_16 | 2 | | `1 … 8` | `00 01 … 00 08` |
| Combination | Logic for combining several sources | Enum_8 | 1 | AND:<br>OR:<br>XOR: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |
| Number of sources | Number of combined sources; 0 for inputs | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0 … FFFF` | `00 00 … FF FF` |
| Source name | Repeats with the next two rows for every source | String | 4 | Device not ready:<br>Field evaluation xx:<br>SOPAS command xx:<br>Input xx: | `DRDY<br>FExx<br>SCxx<br>INxx` | `44 52 44 59<br>46 45 x x<br>53 43 x x<br>49 4E x x` |
| Source inverted | Invert the source signal | Bool_1 | 1 | Not inverted:<br>Inverted: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_8 | 1 | | `0` | `00` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_8 | 1 | | `0` | `00` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | - | Uint_16 | 2 | | `0` | `00 00` |

### Receive Output State by Event [sEN LIDoutputstate]

<section class="cola-category" markdown="1">

## Measurement Data Output

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Read IMU Data [sRN InertialMeasurementUnit]

</summary>

Read the latest IMU data. To receive the IMU data continuously as `sSN InertialMeasurementUnit` events, send `sEN InertialMeasurementUnit 1`; send `sEN InertialMeasurementUnit 0` to stop. For continuous IMU data at 100 Hz, prefer the Compact IMU output (telegram type 7).

Required user level: Authorized client.

**Telegram structure: sRN InertialMeasurementUnit**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Read IMU data | String | 23 | | `InertialMeasurementUnit` | `49 6E 65 72 74 69 61 6C 4D 65 61 73 75 72 65 6D 65 6E 74 55 6E 69 74` |

**Example: sRN InertialMeasurementUnit**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRN{SPC}InertialMeasurementUnit<ETX>
```

```text
sRN InertialMeasurementUnit
```

```text
02 73 52 4E 20 49 6E 65 72 74 69 61 6C 4D 65 61 73 75 72 65 6D 65 6E 74 55 6E 69 74 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1B 73 52 4E 20 49 6E 65 72 74 69 61 6C 4D 65 61 73 75 72 65 6D 65 6E 74 55 6E 69 74 03
```

```text
73 52 4E 20 49 6E 65 72 74 69 61 6C 4D 65 61 73 75 72 65 6D 65 6E 74 55 6E 69 74
```


**Telegram structure: sRA InertialMeasurementUnit**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sRA` | `73 52 41` |
| Command | Read IMU data | String | 23 | | `InertialMeasurementUnit` | `49 6E 65 72 74 69 61 6C 4D 65 61 73 75 72 65 6D 65 6E 74 55 6E 69 74` |
| Acceleration X | Acceleration along the X axis, including gravity | Float_32 | 4 | m/s² | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Acceleration Y | Acceleration along the Y axis, including gravity | Float_32 | 4 | m/s² | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Acceleration Z | Acceleration along the Z axis, including gravity | Float_32 | 4 | m/s² | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Angular velocity X | Rotation rate around the X axis | Float_32 | 4 | rad/s | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Angular velocity Y | Rotation rate around the Y axis | Float_32 | 4 | rad/s | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Angular velocity Z | Rotation rate around the Z axis | Float_32 | 4 | rad/s | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Orientation W | Orientation as quaternion | Float_32 | 4 | | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Orientation X | Orientation as quaternion | Float_32 | 4 | | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Orientation Y | Orientation as quaternion | Float_32 | 4 | | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Orientation Z | Orientation as quaternion | Float_32 | 4 | | `IEEE 754 float, hex` | `4 bytes` |
| Time stamp | Time of the measurement in µs since power-up | Uint_64 | 8 | µs | `0 … FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` | `8 bytes` |

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Angle Range Focus Filter [sWN angleRangeFocusFilter]

</summary>

Restricts streaming data output to a specified 3D field of view. The theta parameters define the azimuth range and the phi parameters define the elevation range. Beams outside these ranges are not transmitted. Within the selected range, subsampling can be applied to reduce data bandwidth. Additionally, a focus region can be defined where full resolution is preserved (no subsampling). This filter only affects raw data streaming and has no effect on object detection.

Required user level: Authorized client.

**Telegram structure: sWN angleRangeFocusFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write request | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Variable name | Restricts streaming data output to a specified 3D field of view. The theta parameters define the azimuth range and the phi parameters define the elevation range. Beams outside these ranges are not transmitted. Within the selected range, subsampling can be applied to reduce data bandwidth. Additionally, a focus region can be defined where full resolution is preserved (no subsampling). This filter only affects raw data streaming and has no effect on object detection. | String | 21 | | `angleRangeFocusFilter` | `61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 6F 63 75 73 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |
| enable | Enables/Disables the filter. | Bool_1 | 1 | False:<br>True: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| thetaStart | Lower boundary of the azimuth range. Columns outside this range are not transmitted. | Int_32 | 4 | | `-900000` | `FF F2 44 60` |
| thetaStop | Upper boundary of the azimuth range. Columns outside this range are not transmitted. | Int_32 | 4 | | `+900000` | `00 0D BB A0` |
| phiStart | Lower boundary of the elevation range. Layers outside this range are not transmitted. | Int_32 | 4 | | `-250000` | `FF FC 2F 70` |
| phiStop | Upper boundary of the elevation range. Layers outside this range are not transmitted. | Int_32 | 4 | | `+250000` | `00 03 D0 90` |
| thetaIndexIncrement | The 'thetaIndexIncrement' is used to sub-sample the slots within the selected theta angle range. With a 'thetaIndexIncrement' of n only every n'th slot from the selected angle range is serialized, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+1` | `00 01` |
| phiIndexIncrement | The 'phiIndexIncrement' is used to sub-sample the layers within the selected phi angle range. With a 'phiIndex-Increment' of n only every n'th layer from the selected angle range is serialized, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+1` | `00 01` |
| enable | Enables/Disables the focus region. In this region, the sub-sampling is not applied. | Bool_1 | 1 | False:<br>True: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| direction | Focus direction: selects whether the focus region spans the vertical or horizontal axis. | Enum_8 | 1 | | `0` | `00` |
| thetaStart | Lower boundary of the azimuth focus range | Int_32 | 4 | | `-450000` | `FF F9 22 30` |
| thetaStop | Upper boundary of the azimuth focus range | Int_32 | 4 | | `+450000` | `00 06 DD D0` |
| phiStart | Lower boundary of the elevation focus range | Int_32 | 4 | | `-100000` | `FF FE 79 60` |
| phiStop | Upper boundary of the elevation focus range | Int_32 | 4 | | `+100000` | `00 01 86 A0` |

**Example: sWN angleRangeFocusFilter - −90° … +90° × −25° … +25°, focus −45° … +45° × −10° … +10°**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWN{SPC}angleRangeFocusFilter{SPC}0{SPC}-900000{SPC}+900000{SPC}-250000{SPC}+250000{SPC}+1{SPC}+1{SPC}0{SPC}0{SPC}-450000{SPC}+450000{SPC}-100000{SPC}+100000<ETX>
```

```text
sWN angleRangeFocusFilter 0 -900000 +900000 -250000 +250000 +1 +1 0 0 -450000 +450000 -100000 +100000
```

```text
02 73 57 4E 20 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 6F 63 75 73 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 30 20 2D 39 30 30 30 30 30 20 2B 39 30 30 30 30 30 20 2D 32 35 30 30 30 30 20 2B 32 35 30 30 30 30 20 2B 31 20 2B 31 20 30 20 30 20 2D 34 35 30 30 30 30 20 2B 34 35 30 30 30 30 20 2D 31 30 30 30 30 30 20 2B 31 30 30 30 30 30 03
```

## Field Evaluation

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Activation of Evaluation Group [sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup]

</summary>

The telegram is intended to activate or deactivate groups via telegram. The group activation needs to be changed from "always" to "telegram" in advance.

**Telegram structure: sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Activate / deactivate evaluation group | String | 23 | | `ActivateEvaluationGroup` | `41 63 74 69 76 61 74 65 45 76 61 6C 75 61 74 69 6F 6E 47 72 6F 75 70` |
| Amount of evaluation groups to activate/ deactivate | Each array element contains two parameters: evaluation group number, and deactivation/ activation of evaluation group | Uint_16 | 2 | | `1d … 48d (1 … 30h)` | `00 01 … 00 30` |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 1 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `1` | `00 01` |
| Deactivation/ activation of evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 1 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 2 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `2` | `00 02` |
| Deactivation/ activation of evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 2 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | | | |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 48 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `48d (30h)` | `00 30` |
| Deactivation/ activation of evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 48 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example 1: sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup - Deactivate evaluation group 1**

### Set Field Evaluation Contour [sMN SetFieldEvaluationContour]

</summary>

This telegram describes how to change the polygon coordinates. A predefined polygon is required, setting up a polygon from scratch is not possible.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetFieldEvaluationContour**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Set the region of interest of an object detection evaluation | String | 25 | | `SetFieldEvaluationContour` | `53 65 74 46 69 65 6C 64 45 76 61 6C 75 61 74 69 6F 6E 43 6F 6E 74 6F 75 72` |
| Evaluation ID | Specific ID of the evaluation that is to be changed | UInt_16 | 2 | | `+1d ... +48d (1h ... 30h)` | `00 01 … 00 30` |
| Amount of polygon vertices | E. g. triangle = 3, square = 4 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+3d ... +100d (3h ... 64h)` | `00 03 ... 00 64` |
| Polygon vertex | Coordinates of first polygon vertex in mm | Dint_32 | 4 | X coordinate: | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |
| Polygon vertex | Coordinates of first polygon vertex in mm | Dint_32 | 4 | Y coordinate: | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |
| Polygon vertex | Coordinates of second polygon vertex in mm | Dint_32 | 4 | X coordinate: | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |
| Polygon vertex | Coordinates of second polygon vertex in mm | Dint_32 | 4 | Y coordinate: | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | | | |
| Polygon vertex | Coordinates of last polygon vertex in mm | Dint_32 | 4 | X coordinate: | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |
| Polygon vertex | Coordinates of last polygon vertex in mm | Dint_32 | 4 | Y coordinate: | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |
| Lower Z limit | Lower bound of extrusion in Z direction | Dint_32 | 4 | | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |
| Upper Z limit | Upper bound of extrusion in Z direction | Dint_32 | 4 | | `-100,000d ... +100,000d (FFFE7960h … 186A0h)` | `FF FE 79 60 … 00 01 86 A0` |

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Read Field Evaluation Result [sRN FieldEvaluationResult]

</summary>

This telegram returns the status information of all evaluations. Possible status codes:

- **Not configured** - This evaluation has not been configured.
- **Inactive** - This evaluation has been configured but is currently not evaluated.
- **Free** - The field is not infringed.
- **Infringed** - The field is infringed.
- **Detecting infringed** - An infringement has been detected in the field but the response time has not been reached yet.
- **Detecting free** - The field is no longer infringed but the time for the free state has not been reached yet.

**Telegram structure: sRN FieldEvaluationResult**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Info on field evaluation result | String | 21 | | `FieldEvaluationResult` | `46 69 65 6C 64 45 76 61 6C 75 61 74 69 6F 6E 52 65 73 75 6C 74` |

**Example: sRN FieldEvaluationResult**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRN{SPC}FieldEvaluationResult<ETX>
```

```text
sRN FieldEvaluationResult
```

```text
02 73 52 4E 20 46 69 65 6C 64 45 76 61 6C 75 61 74 69 6F 6E 52 65 73 75 6C 74 03
```

<summary markdown="block">

### Receive Field Evaluation Result by Event [sEN FieldEvaluationResult]

</summary>

This telegram returns the status information of all evaluations by subscribing to an event, using the same possible status codes as above. The device confirms the subscription with `sEA FieldEvaluationResult`. After that, it sends an `sSN FieldEvaluationResult` telegram each time an evaluation result changes, not cyclically. Send `sEN FieldEvaluationResult 0` to stop the event.

**Telegram structure: sEN FieldEvaluationResult**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Event | String | 3 | | `sEN` | `73 45 4E` |
| Command | Info on field evaluation result | String | 21 | | `FieldEvaluationResult` | `46 69 65 6C 64 45 76 61 6C 75 61 74 69 6F 6E 52 65 73 75 6C 74` |
| Reporting | Start/ stop | Enum_8 | 1 | Stop:<br>Start: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

## Error Codes [sFA]

If the device cannot execute a telegram, it answers with `sFA` and an error code, for example `sFA 3` (CoLa A) or `73 46 41 00 03` (CoLa B payload) for an unknown variable name.

| Error code | Description | Dec. | Hex. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Sopas_Ok` | No error | 0 | 0 |
| `Sopas_Error_METHODIN_ACCESSDENIED` | Wrong userlevel, access to method not allowed | 1 | 1 |
| `Sopas_Error_METHODIN_UNKNOWNINDEX` | Trying to access a method with an unknown Sopas index | 2 | 2 |
| `Sopas_Error_VARIABLE_UNKNOWNINDEX` | Trying to access a variable with an unknown Sopas index | 3 | 3 |
| `Sopas_Error_LOCALCONDITIONFAILED` | Local condition violated, e.g. giving a value that exceeds the minimum or maximum allowed value for this variable | 4 | 4 |
| `Sopas_Error_INVALID_DATA` | Invalid data given for variable, this errorcode is deprecated (is not used anymore). | 5 | 5 |
| `Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_ERROR` | An error with unknown reason occurred, this errorcode is deprecated. | 6 | 6 |
| `Sopas_Error_BUFFER_OVERFLOW` | The communication buffer was too small for the amount of data that should be serialised. | 7 | 7 |
| `Sopas_Error_BUFFER_UNDERFLOW` | More data was expected, the allocated buffer could not be filled. | 8 | 8 |
| `Sopas_Error_ERROR_UNKNOWN_TYPE` | The variable that shall be serialised has an unknown type. This can only happen when there are variables in the firmware of the device that do not exist in the released description of the device. This should never happen. | 9 | 9 |
| `Sopas_Error_VARIABLE_WRITE_ACCESSDENIED` | It is not allowed to write values to this variable. Probably the variable is defined as read-only. | 10 | A |
| `Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_CMD_FOR_NAMESERVER` | When using names instead of indices, a command was issued that the nameserver does not understand. | 11 | B |
| `Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_COLA_COMMAND` | The CoLa protocol specification does not define the given command, command is unknown. | 12 | C |
| `Sopas_Error_METHODIN_SERVER_BUSY` | It is not possible to issue more than one command at a time to an SRT device. | 13 | D |
| `Sopas_Error_FLEX_OUTOF_BOUNDS` | An array was accessed over its maximum length. | 14 | E |
| `Sopas_Error_EVENTREG_UNKNOWNINDEX` | The event you wanted to register for does not exist, the index is unknown. | 15 | F |
| `Sopas_Error_COLA_A_VALUE_OVERFLOW` | The value does not fit into the value field, it is too large. | 16 | 10 |
| `Sopas_Error_COLA_A_INVALIDCHARACTER` | Character is unknown, probably not alphanumeric. | 17 | 11 |
| `Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_MESSAGE` | Only when using SRTOS in the firmware and distributed variables this error can occur. It is an indication that no operating system message could be created. This happens when trying to GET a variable. | 18 | 12 |
| `Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_ANSWER_MESSAGE` | This is the same as `Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_MESSAGE` with the difference that it is thrown when trying to PUT a variable. | 19 | 13 |
| `Sopas_Error_INTERNAL` | Internal error in the firmware, probably a pointer to a parameter was null. | 20 | 14 |
| `Sopas_Error_HubAddressCorrupted` | The Sopas Hubaddress is either too short or too long. | 21 | 15 |
| `Sopas_Error_HubAddressDecoding` | The Sopas Hubaddress is invalid, it can not be decoded (Syntax). | 22 | 16 |
| `Sopas_Error_HubAddressAddressExceeded` | Too many hubs in the address | 23 | 17 |
| `Sopas_Error_HubAddressBlankExpected` | When parsing a HubAddress an expected blank was not found. The HubAddress is not valid. | 24 | 18 |
| - | An asynchronous method call was made although the device was built with “AsyncMethodsSuppressed”. This is an internal error that should never happen in a released device. | 25 | 19 |
| - | Device was built with „ComplexArraysSuppressed“ because the compiler does not allow recursions. But now a complex array was found. This is an internal error that should never happen in a released device. | 26 | 1A |

# multiScan200 Electrical Connection and Pin Assignment

> Wire a multiScan270 power, Gigabit Ethernet, and digital I/O system plug to a controller using the documented M12 pin assignments.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/electrical-connection/

# Electrical Connection

Compatible with: multiScan200

To check whether the sensor still receives its minimum supply voltage at the end of a long cable, use the [Cable Dimensioning](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cable-dimensioning/) calculator.

## Power / 8 IOs 

System plug part numbers: 2155106, 2148845

The PWR and I/O connection uses a male, 12-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/multiscan200-pwr.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR / 8 IOs** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 2 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 3 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 4 | `IN7/OUT7` | Configurable digital input 7 or output 7 |
| 5 | `IN8/OUT8` | Configurable digital input 8 or output 8 |
| 6 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |
| 7 | `IN4/OUT4` | Configurable digital input 4 or output 4 |
| 8 | `IN6/OUT6` | Configurable digital input 6 or output 6 |
| 9 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 10 | `IN5/OUT5` | Configurable digital input 5 or output 5 |
| 11 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 12 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |

**Always wire both supply pins 9 and 12 and both ground pins 2 and 11.** This is
a requirement in the multiScan270 operating instructions, not an optional
parallel connection.

## Ethernet

The Ethernet connection uses a female, 8-pin, X-coded M12 connector.

![Ethernet connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/multiscan200-ethernet.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">Ethernet connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Ethernet** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `TRD0_P` | Transmit/receive pair 0 + |
| 2 | `TRD0_N` | Transmit/receive pair 0 − |
| 3 | `TRD1_P` | Transmit/receive pair 1 + |
| 4 | `TRD1_N` | Transmit/receive pair 1 − |
| 5 | `TRD3_P` | Transmit/receive pair 3 + |
| 6 | `TRD3_N` | Transmit/receive pair 3 − |
| 7 | `TRD2_N` | Transmit/receive pair 2 − |
| 8 | `TRD2_P` | Transmit/receive pair 2 + |

The X-coded Gigabit Ethernet interface requires all four data pairs. A
four-wire D-coded connection is unsuitable.

# multiScan200 Web GUI (SOPASair): All Screens and Settings

> Walkthrough of every multiScan200 SOPASair web interface screen, captured on a multiScan270: configuration, data output, contamination indication, and diagnostics.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/graphical-user-interface/

# SOPASair Walkthrough

This page describes the multiScan200 web interface and the settings in each view. Use it to commission the sensor before you automate the configuration through the API. To try the interface without a device, open it in the [Virtual Sensor Lab](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/simulation/virtual-sensor-lab/).

## Home

The Home page gives you the current device status, network identity, firmware version, and an overview of the sensor's operating state. It is usually the first screen you see after logging in and is the quickest place to confirm that the unit is online and healthy before you start changing configuration or application settings.

![Home](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-home.png)
*Home page overview on a live multiScan270 device.*

The status bar at the top shows the LED indicator, the device connection status
and the measurement status. The toolbar next to it holds **Save permanently**,
the login panel, the language switch and the global help (**?**). The help
includes a **Getting started** tour that walks through the most important
commissioning steps.

Changes take effect immediately but are held in volatile memory. Click
**Save permanently** in the toolbar to store the parameter set in the device
and in the cloning memory of the system plug. Unsaved changes are lost at the
next power cycle.

For a monitoring display without configuration access, open
`http://192.168.0.1/#/?fullscreen=`.

The LEDs are only an additional visual aid. Switching them off in the web
interface does not affect diagnostics over Ethernet or the digital I/Os.

## Configuration

Choose the scan configuration and the core measurement behaviour. Resolution, frequency, and range trade off against each other.

The live scan on the left updates as you change the configuration, which is the quickest way to judge a setting.

### Basic Settings

Basic Settings controls the scan configuration used by the sensor. The settings
are shown on the right; the live scan on the left shows the effect of the
selected frequency, angular resolution, and other settings immediately. Use
this view to check coverage and measurement behaviour while commissioning.

![Basic settings tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-basic-settings-tile.png)
*Basic settings tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

The multiScan270 offers the following scan configurations. The vertical field of
view is always 45° (about +22.5° to −22.5°). Configurations 10 to 12 reach their
horizontal resolution in interlaced mode, where consecutive scans are offset in
angle and combined. The ambient-light image is passively captured by the same
receiver used for LiDAR, synchronized with the laser measurement, and has the
same scan frequency and horizontal resolution as the configured laser
measurement.

<p class="table-caption">multiScan270 scan configurations, angular resolutions, layer counts, ambient-image dimensions, and scan frequencies.</p>

| No. | Use case                    | FoV (H) | Resolution (H × V) | Layers | Ambient image (pixels, columns × rows) | Frequency            |
| --- | --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------ | ------ | -------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| 1   | Default                     | 276°    | 0.47° × 0.47°      | 96     | 592 × 96                               | 20 Hz                |
| 2   | Less bandwidth, more range  | 276°    | 0.47° × 0.94°      | 48     | 592 × 48                               | 20 Hz                |
| 3   | Highest vertical resolution | 276°    | 0.47° × 0.23°      | 192    | 592 × 192                              | 20 Hz                |
| 4   | Full 360° view              | 360°    | 0.47° × 0.47°      | 96     | 773 × 96                               | 10 Hz                |
| 10  | High horizontal resolution  | 276°    | 0.23° × 0.47°      | 96     | 1184 × 96                              | 20 Hz, 2× interlaced |
| 11  | High H and V resolution     | 276°    | 0.23° × 0.23°      | 192    | 1184 × 192                             | 20 Hz, 2× interlaced |
| 12  | Highest H and V resolution  | 276°    | 0.12° × 0.23°      | 192    | 2369 × 192                             | 20 Hz, 4× interlaced |
| 20  | Up to +55 °C                | 190°    | 0.47° × 0.47°      | 96     | 408 × 96                               | 20 Hz                |
| 21  | Up to +60 °C                | 120°    | 0.47° × 0.47°      | 96     | 285 × 96                               | 20 Hz                |

- **Configurations 20 and 21** reduce the horizontal field of view so that the
  device can operate at higher ambient temperatures (up to +55 °C and +60 °C).
- **Ambient image:** a passive, narrow-band image around 905 nm from the LiDAR
  receiver, not a camera image. Brightness can differ from what you see; for
  example, LED-lit areas may look dark. The table shows the image size that
  matches the point cloud. The maximum image size is 592 × 192 px
  (configurations 1 to 3), 773 × 192 (4), 1184 × 192 (10 and 11),
  2369 × 192 (12), 408 × 192 (20), and 285 × 192 (21).
- **Interlaced configurations (10 to 12):** 10 and 11 combine 2 scans (about
  100 ms at 20 Hz), 12 combines 4 (about 200 ms). This is the acquisition
  span, not the output latency. Because the points of one frame are captured
  at different times, moving objects can appear offset; for moving scenes,
  validate the result or use a non-interlaced configuration. The mean filter
  has no effect, and the particle filter should be checked because it compares
  measurements at different angles.
- **Small objects** must be hit repeatedly for reliable measurement. Objects
  below the minimum object size may need a stationary sensor and target.

![Date and system time tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-date-and-system-time-tile.png)
*Date and system time tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

**Date and system time**

The time base can be set using various methods:

- Explicitly setting the time with date, time
- Transferring the time from the computer used
- Via an external NTP server (Network Time Protocol) that is accessible in the network.
- Via an external PTP (Precision Time Protocol) master that is accessible in the network.

NTP uses UDP port 123 and PTP uses UDP ports 319/320. Both are inactive by
default. Use PTP when point clouds must be fused with other sensors, because it
gives the tightest synchronisation. For background and setup, see
[Time synchronization](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/time-synchronization/).

### Filter

Clean up the scan before it leaves the sensor by suppressing extra echoes, artefacts and airborne particles.

![Filter settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-filter-tile.png)
*Example filter settings in the multiScan270 web interface. Select parameters according to the requirements of each application.*

Filters can be combined freely. Active filters run one after another, each on
the result of the previous one, in this order: echo filter, particle filter,
interval filter, blooming filter, angle-range filter. Keep in mind:

- Filters apply to both measurement data output and field evaluation. Filtered
  values cannot be converted back into the original measurements.
- Each active filter adds processing time and therefore output latency. The
  particle filter adds a delay of one scan.
- Field evaluation always uses a single echo. If the echo filter is set to
  **All echoes**, field evaluation uses the first echo.
- In interlaced scan configurations (10 to 12), the precision mode has no
  effect, and the particle filter compares measurements from different angular
  positions. Check that it still works as intended in your application.

The signal path through the filters:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    echo([Echo]) --> core[Measurement core]
    core --> echofilter[Echo filter]
    echofilter --> particle[Particle filter]
    particle --> interval[Interval filter]
    interval --> blooming[Blooming filter]
    blooming --> angle[Angle-range filter]
    angle --> output[Measurement data output]
    angle --> fieldeval[Field evaluation]
```

*Filter processing order for measurement data output and field evaluation.*

The precision mode is the multiScan200 version of the mean filter.

For detailed behavior and examples, see [Filter details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/).

### Inertial Measuring Unit (IMU)

Use the IMU view to inspect the sensor's current orientation and acceleration.

![Mounting settings / IMU](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-mounting-settings.png)
*Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.*

![IMU tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-imu-tile.png)
*Inertial measuring unit (IMU) tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

The IMU view displays the yaw, pitch, and roll angles in degrees, together with the measured acceleration on the X, Y, and Z axes in meters per second squared.

The IMU samples at 100 Hz. It sits at X = −17 mm and Y = +23.5 mm relative to
the optical origin, so apply this offset when you fuse IMU data with the point
cloud. IMU data is streamed separately in Compact format on TCP port 2117, or as
the `imu` topic over [Native ROS 2](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/#native-ros-2).

Orientation follows DIN ISO 8855 with a right-handed coordinate system. X is the
main viewing direction, and Z points to the top of the device. Measurement data
is always output in the device coordinate system. Mounting settings describe the
sensor pose in the world coordinate system; without them, both systems are
identical.

### Contamination Indication

Monitor the optics cover for dirt and get a warning before measurement quality drops.

![Contamination indication tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-contamination-indication-tile.png)
*Contamination indication tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

A contamination warning makes LED2/LED4 flash yellow while LED1/LED3 stay green.
A contamination error makes LED1/LED3 flash red and LED2/LED4 flash yellow. The
contamination state is also available as secondary data, so a host can react
before measurement quality drops.

If the measurement data shows anomalies, clean the optics cover first:

1. If possible, disconnect the power supply.
2. Clean the optics cover with a clean, damp, lint-free cloth and a mild,
   antistatic plastic cleaner. Do not use pointed objects.
3. Remove dust from the housing with a soft brush.

If the optics cover is scratched or damaged, take the device out of operation
and have it repaired by SICK.

### Connection Options

Give the sensor its permanent Ethernet identity so it fits your network.

![Ethernet tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-ethernet-tile.png)
*Ethernet tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

The factory default IP address is `192.168.0.1`. The Ethernet link runs at
1 Gbit/s. Keep this in mind for high-resolution scan configurations.

- After changing the static IP address, restart the device so that Native ROS 2
  topics are published correctly.
- The addressing mode, IP address, subnet mask, default gateway and device name
  are also cloned to the system plug when you save permanently. A replacement
  device on the same system plug starts with the same network identity.

### Inputs and Outputs

Configure the multifunction I/O ports and map field-evaluation results and device states to physical outputs.

![Port configuration](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-port-config.png)
*Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.*

![System plug tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-configuration-port-config-system-plug-tile.png)
*System plug tile on the port configuration page, captured live from a multiScan270.*

The device has up to eight multifunction ports, depending on the mounted system
plug. Each port can be configured as an input, with a debounce time, or as an
output in push-pull, NPN, or PNP mode. For the electrical values, see the
product page on [sick.com](https://www.sick.com).

## Application

### Data Output

Decide what measurement data leaves the sensor and how it is streamed to your system.

![Measurement data output tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-application-data-output-measurement-data-output-tile.png)
*Measurement data output tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

![Data reduction tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-application-data-output-data-reduction-tile.png)
*Data reduction tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

![Angular range filter tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-application-data-output-angular-range-filter-tile.png)
*Angular range filter tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

For detailed filter behavior, see [Filter details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/).

![Scan data structure with slots and layers](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/data-structure-slots-and-layers.png)
*Scan data structure: at each horizontal angle step (slot M−1, M, M+1, …), the sensor measures one vertical column with layers 1 to N. The scan configuration sets the number of layers and the angle between slots.*

The device streams measurement data in these ways:

<p class="table-caption">Measurement and IMU data outputs, transports, and payloads on the multiScan270.</p>

| Output       | Transport                | Content                                                         |
| ------------ | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Compact      | TCP 2115 (outgoing)      | Distance and RSSI, optional ambient light (telegram type 6)     |
| Compact      | TCP 2116 (outgoing)      | Ambient light only (telegram type 3)                            |
| Compact IMU  | TCP 2117 (outgoing)      | IMU data at 100 Hz (telegram type 7)                            |
| Native ROS 2 | DDS over UDP 7400–65399  | `PointCloud2`, `LaserScan`, `ambient_light` and `imu` topics    |

All outputs are disabled by default. Compact uses TCP to avoid data loss.
Measurement data output responds within
100 ms or less, plus network delay from cables and switches. For each echo,
the device also outputs a relative signal strength indicator (RSSI).
Its representation depends on the output format: Compact carries an unsigned
16-bit value, while Native ROS 2 `PointCloud2` intensity is normalized to
0.0–1.0 and identifies reflectors through the properties bit mask.
Native ROS 2 `LaserScan` and `MultiEchoLaserScan` intensity uses 0.0–1.0 for
natural targets and 1.05 for detected reflectors. Do not use intensity alone
to determine whether a measurement is valid. See
[RSSI values](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/compact-format/#rssi-values) and
[Native ROS 2 topics](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/#published-topics)
for the format-specific details.

For Native ROS 2, use CycloneDDS as the ROS middleware and subscribe only to the
topics you need, because subscribed topics are published even when they contain
no points. Parameterisation still runs over REST or CoLa. See
[Compact format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/compact-format/) and
[Native ROS 2](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/#native-ros-2).

### Field Evaluation

Configure monitored volumes and let the sensor evaluate incoming 3D scan
points on the device.

![Field evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-application-field-evaluation.png)
*Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.*

![Field evaluation tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-application-field-evaluation-field-evaluation-tile.png)
*Field evaluation tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

Define a field's polygonal contour and its lower and upper Z limits to form
a monitored volume in the sensor coordinate system. The sensor evaluates
points inside that volume using the configured detection criteria.
Evaluation groups organize the fields and control their activation; results
can be combined with logic and mapped to outputs.

- Up to 48 fields can be configured, and up to 20 can be active at the same
  time.
- A group is activated by digital inputs, by telegram, or is always active. Each
  field in a group has its own evaluation settings.
- The result can be linked to a switching output and combined with other signals
  using logic such as AND, OR and XOR.
- Typical uses are collision protection, object protection and access
  monitoring.

Evaluation runs after every scan cycle, and the field status is output within
175 ms or less. The latency also depends on where and when an object enters the
field relative to the laser position, and on the number of active fields, the
digital outputs, the filters and measurement data streaming.

Only points that fall inside an active field add system load, but many active
fields can still cause performance problems. If you need more fields at once,
reduce the load by disabling the GUI live view, unused data outputs or filters.
Test with your actual application.

For programmatic access, see
[Field evaluation and distance API](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/).

## Diagnostics

### Overview

![Operating information tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-diagnosis-overview-operating-information-tile.png)
*Operating information tile, captured live from a multiScan270.*

The device logs events continuously. Logging cannot be switched off; when the
log memory is full, the oldest entries are overwritten. Download the diagnostic
file from **Diagnostics** and attach it to any support request, together with
the type code and serial number from the type label.

<p class="table-caption">Common device and web-interface symptoms and recommended diagnostic actions.</p>

| Symptom                          | Action                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Both LEDs flash red              | Device error. Read the error code in the web interface and fix the cause.                 |
| All LEDs flash red               | The device may not detect the system plug. Check that it is mounted, clean and dry.       |
| All LEDs stay red at start-up    | Check the power supply; it may not deliver enough current or voltage for motor start.     |
| All LEDs are off                 | Check the power supply, and check whether the LEDs were switched off in the interface.    |
| The loading screen stays on      | Reconnect. If that does not help, restart the device.                                     |
| The web interface does not open  | Check the IP addresses of the device and network adapter, for example with device search. |
| Measurement data shows anomalies | Clean the optics cover.                                                                   |

### Cybersecurity

![Cybersecurity](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/multiScan200/img/sopasair-diagnosis-cyber-security-measures.png)
*Live capture from a multiScan270's web interface.*

Enable and disable network services here. Disable every service you do not
need.

<p class="table-caption">Network services, device ports, and default activation states on the multiScan270.</p>

| Service           | Purpose              | Protocol and port (device) | Default  |
| ----------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------- | -------- |
| HTTP/REST         | Configuration, data  | TCP 80                     | Enabled  |
| HTTPS             | Configuration, data  | TCP 443                    | Enabled  |
| SOPAS (CoLa 2)    | Configuration, data  | TCP 2122                   | Disabled |
| SOPAS (CoLa A/B)  | Configuration, data  | TCP 2111/2112              | Disabled |
| NTP               | Time synchronisation | UDP 123                    | Inactive |
| PTP               | Time synchronisation | UDP 319/320                | Inactive |
| UDP device search | Device discovery     | UDP 30718                  | Enabled  |
| Compact           | Measurement data     | TCP 2115/2116              | Disabled |
| Compact IMU       | IMU data             | TCP 2117                   | Disabled |
| Native ROS 2      | Measurement data     | UDP 7400–65399             | Disabled |

For the full multiScan270 network-services matrix, including interfaces,
communication direction, and peer ports, see
[Cybersecurity: multiScan270 network services](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cybersecurity/#multiscan270-network-services-and-ports).

Change the default passwords at first commissioning. Only the **Service** user
level is active on delivery; see [User levels](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/).
SICK provides firmware updates to fix known vulnerabilities, but the device has
no automatic update. Check for updates regularly; see
[Firmware update](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/) and
[SICK PSIRT](https://www.sick.com/psirt) for security advisories.

# picoScan100

The picoScan100 is a compact 2D LiDAR sensor with one scan plane and a 276° scan range. It comes in two variants: the picoScan120 and the picoScan150. For a sensor and cable combination to get started, see the [Starter Kit](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/starter-kit/).

[Specifications and data sheet on sick.com](https://www.sick.com/de/en/search?text=picoScan100)

This operation uploads a file or uses a non-JSON body. Use the request media type and upload fields below.

**Request body**

**Media type: `multipart/form-data`**

`datei`

**Type:** string · **Format:** binary

Json-File

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

#### [POST /SetPassword](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-rest-post-setpassword)

Sets the password for the CoLa A/B interface only. In this example the password for user level: Service (4) is set to - test - (integer value of the password hash - test -). For more details see  https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_scan_rest_client.

```json

    "siUserLevel": "<integer>",
```

#### [GET /LFPmovingAveragingFilter](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-rest-get-lfpmovingaveragingfilter)

Returns/sets the mean filter settings. This filter smooths the distance value by calculating the arithmetic mean from the configured number of scans (2..4 scans). Points with zero distance are treated as missing values and are not taken into account for averaging. If all distances considered for averaging have the value 0, the result will be 0 as well.

**Try the request**

Copy this command into a terminal. In Windows PowerShell, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```bash
curl --request GET "http://192.168.0.1/api/LFPmovingAveragingFilter"
```

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**
| `header` |

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-schema-responseheader)

 |
| --- | --- |
| `data` |
| `bEnable` |

**Type:** boolean · **Default:** false

 |
| `uiAveragingDepth` |

**Type:** integer · **Format:** uint16 · **Default:** 3 · **Minimum:** 2 · **Maximum:** 4

 |

 |

#### [GET /InertialMeasurementUnit](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-rest-get-inertialmeasurementunit)

Returns the current IMU data (e.g. Acceleration, Orientation, ... ). The data is given in the following coordinate system which is based on the DIN70000 system. The x-axis lies on the 90-degree-beam of the 0-degree-layer. The y-axis is perpendicular to the x-axis and lies in the 0-degree-layer. The y-values are rising in the counterclockwise rotation direction (right-handed system). The z-axis is perpendicular to the x-y-plane and the scanner top points to rising z-values.

**Try the request**

Copy this command into a terminal. In Windows PowerShell, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```bash
curl --request GET "http://192.168.0.1/api/InertialMeasurementUnit"
```

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**
| `header` |

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-schema-responseheader)

 |
| --- | --- |
| `data` |
| `Acceleration` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 3

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Format:** float · **Default:** 0.0

 |
| `AngularVelocity` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 3

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Format:** float · **Default:** 0.0

 |
| `Orientation` |

**Default:**

```
[]
```

**Type:** array · **Minimum items:** 0 · **Maximum items:** 4

**Items:**

**Type:** number · **Format:** float · **Default:** 0.0

 |
| `TimeStamp` |

**Type:** integer · **Format:** uint64

 |

 |

### 13 - Data Reduction 

#### [GET /LFPangleRangeFilter](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-rest-get-lfpanglerangefilter)

Returns/sets the angle range filter settings. The filter restricts the output scan to a specified angle range. Filtered measurement values are set to 0. If the content of a complete data segment is set to 0, this segment is not output anymore.

#### [GET /MergeSaving](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-rest-get-mergesaving)

Returns/sets the status for saving the merged scans. As soon as a scan merge is completed, the point cloud is available for download on port 80 (192.168.0.1/cloud.pcd). Curl: http:///cloud.pcd -o cloud.pcd. Only the most recently created point cloud is available for download. The point cloud is ready for download when MergeSaving changes from 1 (Saving in progress) to 0 (Saving not active).

**Try the request**

Copy this command into a terminal. In Windows PowerShell, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```bash
curl --request GET "http://192.168.0.1/api/MergeSaving"
```

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**
| `header` |

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-schema-responseheader)

 |
| --- | --- |
| `data` |

`MergeSaving`

**Type:** boolean · **Default:** false

This operation uploads a file or uses a non-JSON body. Use the request media type and upload fields below.

**Request body**

**Media type: `multipart/form-data`**

`datei`

**Type:** string · **Format:** binary

Json-File

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

#### [POST /SetPassword](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan120-rest-post-setpassword)

Sets the password for the CoLa A/B interface only. In this example the password for user level: Service (4) is set to - test - (integer value of the password hash - test -). For more details see  https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_scan_rest_client.

**JSON example**

```json
{
  "data": {
    "siUserLevel": 4,
    "udiNewPassword": 3410122659
  }
}
```

**Try the request**

Protected requests need challenge-response authentication, so `curl` alone cannot send them; use the [Python script on the REST Interface page](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/#challenge-response-authentication).

**Request body**

**Required:** true

**Media type: `application/json`**

`data`

```
  "udiNewPassword": 3410122659
}
```

### 6 - Filter 

#### [GET /LFPparticle](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan120-rest-get-lfpparticle)

Returns/sets the particle filter settings. Filters out disturbances in the measurement data caused by particles such as dust, snowflakes, or similar. Configure the minimal threshold of the required distance step (mm) between the echo to be filtered and the echoes of surrounding beam angles.

**Try the request**

Copy this command into a terminal. In Windows PowerShell, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```bash
curl --request GET "http://192.168.0.1/api/LFPparticle"
```

**Responses**

**Status `200`**

**Media type: `application/json`**
| `header` |

**Fields:** [ResponseHeader](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan120-schema-responseheader)

 |
| --- | --- |
| `data` |
| `bEnable` |

**Type:** boolean · **Default:** false

 |
| `uiThreshold` |

**Type:** integer · **Format:** uint16 · **Default:** 500 · **Minimum:** 20 · **Maximum:** 5000

 |

 |

#### [POST /LFPparticle](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan120-rest-post-lfpparticle)

Returns/sets the particle filter settings. Filters out disturbances in the measurement data caused by particles such as dust, snowflakes, or similar. Configure the minimal threshold of the required distance step (mm) between the echo to be filtered and the echoes of surrounding beam angles.

# picoScan100 API | CoLa Telegrams (CoLa A and CoLa B)

> Complete picoScan100 CoLa telegram reference with sRN, sWN, sMN, and sEN commands, parameter structures, and CoLa A and CoLa B examples.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-cola-telegrams/

# API | CoLa Telegrams

This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the picoScan100. Use the command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level integrations without guessing the telegram structure.

Examples are grouped by protocol, with each telegram representation in a separate code block and its own copy button.

Categories follow the [picoScan150 REST API reference](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/#picoscan150-rest-api)
where corresponding CoLa telegrams are available. Select a telegram to expand
its structure and examples. A direct link to a telegram opens it automatically.
The categories organize the reference; they do not imply that every telegram
is supported by every picoScan variant.

<section class="cola-category" markdown="1">

## General

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]

</summary>

The password hashes of the default passwords are documented in the operating instructions (PDF) of your device. Do not pass them on, and change the passwords during commissioning.

A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. Changed parameters will be reset to the previous state via a reboot unless they are saved. To save parameter changes the command "sMN mEEwriteall" must be sent before log out.

**Telegram structure: sMN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | User level | String | 13 | | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| User level | Select user level | Int_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `2<br>3<br>4` | `02<br>03<br>04` |
| Password | Hash value for the selected user level | Uint_32 | 4 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized client:<br>Service: | `<password hash>` | `<password hash>` |

**Example: sMN SetAccessMode - Log in as “Authorized client”**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}3{SPC}<password hash><ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sMN SetAccessMode 3 <password hash><ETX>
```

```text
sMN SetAccessMode 3 <password hash>
```


**Telegram structure: sAN SetAccessMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sAN` | `73 41 4E` |
| Command | User level | String | 13 | | `SetAccessMode` | `53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65` |
| Change user level | Changed level | Bool_1 | 1 | Error:<br>Success: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sAN SetAccessMode**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sAN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
02 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 13 73 41 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 01 38
```

</details>

### Enable/ Disable CoLa User Levels [sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel]

</summary>

This command enables and disables a specific CoLa user level (Maintenance, Authorized Client).

**Telegram structure: sMN EnableLegacyUserLevel**

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Command | Enable/ disable CoLa user level | String | 21 | | `EnableLegacyUserLevel` | `45 6E 61 62 6C 65 4C 65 67 61 63 79 55 73 65 72 4C 65 76 65 6C` |
| User level | - | Uint_8 | 1 | Maintenance:<br>Authorized Client: | `2<br>3` | `02<br>03` |
| Status | Enable/ disable | Bool_1 | 1 | Disable:<br>Enable: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

### Read Checksum [sRN LFTchecksum]

</summary>

This command includes the MD5 checksum of multiple software parts to verify their integrity. The checksums help to ensure files have not been corrupted or altered. They are also important for cybersecurity because they detect unauthorized modifications.

**Telegram structure: sRN LFTchecksum**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | MD5 checksum | String | 11 | | `LFTchecksum` | `4C 46 54 63 68 65 63 6B 73 75 6D` |

**Example: sRN LFTchecksum**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRN{SPC}LFTchecksum<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sRN LFTchecksum<ETX>
```

```text
sRN LFTchecksum
```

```text
02 73 52 4E 20 4C 46 54 63 68 65 63 6B 73 75 6D 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0F 73 52 4E 20 4C 46 54 63 68 65 63 6B 73 75 6D 1C
```

```text
73 52 4E 20 4C 46 54 63 68 65 63 6B 73 75 6D
```

<summary markdown="block">

### Set to Run [sMN Run]

</summary>

### Read for Frequency and Angular Resolution [sRN LMPscancfg]

</summary>

Read the scanning frequency, angular resolution and aperture angle of the device. Values show the information of the values before any filters are applied. Therefore aperture angle is always showing the maximum, scanning frequency and angular resolution may also be static depending on device family.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String | 10 | | `LMPscancfg` | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |

**Example: sRN LMPscancfg**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sRN{SPC}LMPscancfg<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sRN LMPscancfg<ETX>
```

```text
sRN LMPscancfg
```

```text
02 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0E 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 63
```

```text
73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67
```


**Telegram structure: sRA LMPscancfg**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sRA` | `73 52 41` |
| Command | Info of scan frequency and angular resolution | String | 10 | | `LMPscancfg` | `4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67` |
| Scan frequency | [1/100 Hz] | Uint_32 | 4 | 15 Hz ... 50 Hz:<br>(depends on Dynamic Sensing Profile ) | `5DCh ... 1388h` | `05 DC ... 13 88` |
| Reserved | - | Int_16 | 2 | Always: | `1` | `00 01` |
| Angular resolution | [1/10000°] | Uint_32 | 4 | 0.1° ... 1°:<br>(depends on Dynamic Sensing Profile ) | `3E8h … 2710h` | `03 E8 ... 27 10` |
| Start angle | [1/10000°] | Int_32 | 4 | -48° ... 228° | `FFF8AD00h … 22CA40h` | `FF F8 AD 00h … 00 22 CA 40h` |
| Stop angle | [1/10000°] | Int_32 | 4 | -48° ... 228° | `FFF8AD00h … 22CA40h` | `FF F8 AD 00h … 00 22 CA 40h` |

**Example: sRA LMPscancfg - 30 Hz scan frequency, 0.1° angular resolution, -138° start angle, +138° stop angle**

<summary markdown="block">

### Autostart Measurement [sWN LMPautostartmeas]

</summary>

This parameter defines whether the scanner will start to rotate directly and measure when powering up or remain in idle mode. The changed setting (saved with the command sMN mEEWriteall, ) will be then be active with the next power-up cycle.

In case autostart is deactivated, the sensor will remain in idle mode with the laser switched off and a motor speed depending on the Dynamic Sensing Profile .

**Telegram structure: sWN LMPautostartmeas**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Autostart measurement | String | 16 | | `LMPautostartmeas` | `4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73` |
| Status code | Activate / Deactivate Autostart | Bool_1 | 1 | Autostart off:<br>Autostart on: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sWN LMPautostartmeas 1**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWN{SPC}LMPautostartmeas{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sWN LMPautostartmeas 1<ETX>
```

```text
sWN LMPautostartmeas 1
```

```text
02 73 57 4E 20 4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73 20 31 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 16 73 57 4E 20 4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73 20 01 4F
```

```text
73 57 4E 20 4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73 20 01
```


**Telegram structure: sWA LMDautostartmeas**

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]

</summary>

The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

**Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Method | String | 3 | | `sMN` | `73 4D 4E` |
| Command | Set time stamp | String | 14 | | `LSPsetdatetime` | `4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65` |
| Year | | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+1970d … +2099d (07B2h … 0833h)` | `07 B2 … 08 33` |
| Month | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch)` | `01 … 0C` |
| Day | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh)` | `00 … 1F` |
| Hour | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +23d(00h … 17h)` | `00 … 17` |
| Minute | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)` | `00 … 3B` |
| Second | | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh)` | `00 … 3B` |
| Microsecond | | Uint_32 | 4 | | `+0d … +999999d(00000000h … 000F423Fh)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F` |

**Example 1: sMN LSPsetdatetime Date: 17.02.2009; Time: 16:34**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}7D9{SPC}2{SPC}11{SPC}10{SPC}22{SPC}0{SPC}0<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sMN LSPsetdatetime 7D9 2 11 10 22 0 0<ETX>
```

```text
sMN LSPsetdatetime 7D9 2 11 10 22 0 0
```

```text
02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 37 44 39 20 32 20 31 31 20 31 30 20 32 32 20 30 20 30 03
```


**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 D9 02 11 10 22 00 00 00 00 00 A3
```

```text
73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 D9 02 11 10 22 00 00 00 00 00
```


**Example 2: sMN LSPsetdatetime Date: 26.01.2010; Time: 10:35**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}+2010{SPC}+01{SPC}+26{SPC}+10{SPC}+35{SPC}0{SPC}0<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sMN LSPsetdatetime +2010 +01 +26 +10 +35 0 0<ETX>
```


## Filter

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Particle Filter [sWN LFPparticle]

</summary>

Filter out disturbances in the meausurement data caused by particles such as dust, snow flakes or similar .

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPparticle**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |

## Contamination Indication

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Contamination Indication Settings [sWN ContaminationConfig]

</summary>

Define how and under which conditions the device shall indicate a potential contamination of the optics cover to enable preventive cleaning.

**Telegram structure: sWN ContaminationConfig**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | | String | 19 | | `ContaminationConfig` | `43 6F 6E 74 61 6D 69 6E 61 74 69 6F 6E 43 6F 6E 66 69 67` |
| Strategy | Strategy code | Enum_8 | 1 | No output:<br>All sectors contaminated:<br>One sector contaminated: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Response time | How fast (in seconds) the sensor reacts after a contamination | Uint_16 | 2 | Value range 3 ... 60<br>Default: 3 | `+3d … +60d (03h … 3Ch)` | `00 03 … 00 3C` |
| Threshold warning | Sensitivity | Enum_8 | 1 | High:<br>Medium:<br>Low: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Sector preselection | Selection of either custom sectors or used weather protection hood | Enum_8 | 1 | All sectors:<br>Weather protection hood:<br>Custom sectors: | `0<br>6<br>255d (FFh)` | `00<br>06<br>FF` |
| Length | | UInt_16 | 2 | Always: | `7` | `00 07` |
| Custom sectors | Enable/ disable individual sectors when custom sectors got selected in Sector preselection | Array | 7 | Active: 1<br>Inactive: 0<br>Default value of all sectors is active | `0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1<br>0 ... 1` | `00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01<br>00 ... 01` |
| Enable Warning | Warning monitoring | Bool_1 | 1 | Off (False):<br>On (True): | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Enable Error | Error monitoring | Bool_1 | 1 | Off (False):<br>On (True): | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sWN ContaminationConfig One sector contaminated, response time 60 seconds, sensitivity low, weather protection hood, enable warning, enable error**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWN{SPC}ContaminationConfig{SPC}2{SPC}3C{SPC}2{SPC}6{SPC}7{SPC}1{SPC}1{SPC}1{SPC}1{SPC}1{SPC}1{SPC}1{SPC}1{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sWN ContaminationConfig 2 3C 2 6 7 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1<ETX>
```

### Read State of the Ports [sRN LIDportstate]

</summary>

LIDportstate has to be available additionally or as successor of the LIDoutputstate telegram.

Valid for all sensors with Ethernet and ports (inputs / outputs).

**Telegram structure: sRN LIDportstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |


```text
73 52 4E 20 4C 49 44 70 6F 72 74 73 74 61 74 65
```


**Telegram structure: sRA LIDportstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Answer | String | 3 | | `sRA` | `73 52 41` |
| Command | Port state | String | 12 | | `LIDportstate` | `4C 49 44 70 6F 72 74 73 74 61 74 65` |
| Status code | Version number | Uint_16 | 2 | Current version: | `0 … FFFFh<br>0` | `00 01 … FF FF` |
| Status code | System counter (time in µs since power up max. 71min then starting from 0 again) | Uint_32 | 4 | | `0 … FFFFFFFFh` | `00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF` |
| ARRAY which defines the number of internal ports* | 0...n | Uint_16 | 2 | Hex:<br>Not available:<br>Number of ports: | `0000 - FFFF<br>00<br>01 ... n` | `00 00 - FF FF` |
| State of the ports and count value in hex | Internal port state | Enum_8 | 1 | Output voltage low:(Relays open)<br>Output voltage high:(Relays closed)<br>Tri-state:<br>Input voltage high (level):Input voltage from low to high (edge)<br>Input voltage low (level):Input voltage high to low (edge) | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03<br>04` | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03<br>04` |
| State of the ports and count value in hex | Internal port counter | Uint_32 | 4 | | `0 … FFFFFFFFh` | `00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF` |
| | ….. | | | | | |
| ARRAY which defines the number of external or virtual ports* | 0...n | Uint_16 | 1 | Hex:<br>Not available:<br>Number of ports: | `00 00 - FF FF<br>00<br>01 ... n` | `00 00 - FF FF` |
| State of the ports and count value in hex | External port state | Enum_8 | 1 | Output voltage low:(Relays open)<br>Output voltage high:(Relays closed)<br>Tri-state:<br>Input voltage high (level):Input voltage from low to high (edge)<br>Input voltage low (level):Input voltage high to low (edge) | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03<br>04` | `00<br>01<br>02<br>03<br>04` |
| State of the ports and count value in hex | External port counter | Uint_32 | 4 | | `0 … FFFFFFFFh` | `00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF` |
| Time | States code | Enum_16 | 1 | No time data:<br>Time data: | `00 00<br>00 01` | `00 00<br>00 01` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Year | Array | 2 | E.g. | `1970` | `07 B2` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Month | Array | 1 | | `1 … 12` | `01 … 0C` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Day | Array | 1 | | `1 … 31` | `01 … 1F` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Hour | Array | 1 | | `0 … 23` | `00 … 17` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Minute | Array | 1 | | `0 … 59` | `00 … 3B` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Second | Array | 1 | | `0 … 59` | `00 … 3B` |
| Time Block (sensor time from the last change of min. one of the outputs) | Microsecond | Array | 4 | | `0 … 999999` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F` |

Inputs/outputs: If the device has separate inputs and outputs (instead of general purpose ports) the ARRAY shall start with inputs followed by the outputs.

Virtual ports are ports that can be used to expand the number of ports but are not physically available. They just show up in the corresponding ethernet telegrams (like LIDportstate).

Tri-State: Port is neither input nor output; the port is set inactive in SOPAS

**Example: sRA LIDportstate**

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Port Configuration [sWN PortConfiguration]

</summary>

Configuration of the given ports. Telegram structure represents the configuration of 1 port.

If the device has multiple ports, use the same structure.

**Telegram structure: sWN PortConfiguration**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Configuration of the given ports | String | 17 | | `PortConfiguration` | `50 6F 72 74 43 6F 6E 66 69 67 75 72 61 74 69 6F 6E` |
| Port Type | Input or Output | Enum_8 | 1 | Input:<br>Output: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Name | Name of the port | FlexString | 9<br>(0..32) | Default: | `InOut1` | `00 06 49 6E 4F 75 74 31 00` |
| Input Settings | | | | | | |
| Logic | Logic of the input | Enum_8 | 1 | Active high:<br>Active low: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Debounce | Select debouncing time in ms | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d ... +255d (0h … FFh)` | `00 … FF` |
| Reserved | - | Enum_8 | 1 | Always: | `+0d (0h)` | `00` |
| Reserved1 | | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Reserved2 | | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Output Settings | | | | | | |
| Logic | Definition of the output logic | Enum_8 | 1 | Active high:<br>Active low: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Output Mode | Set kind of mode for output pin | Enum_8 | 1 | PNP:<br>NPN:<br>Push-Pull: | `0<br>1<br>2` | `00<br>01<br>02` |
| Restart Type | Defines type of restart to be used | Enum_8 | 1 | Immediately:<br>Time: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Restart Time | [Only with restart type = Time], time in ms | Uint_32 | 4 | (20 ms … 600,000 ms) | `+20d … +600000d (C8h ... 927C0h)` | `00 00 00 00 … 00 09 27 C0` |
| Restart Input | [Only with restart type = Input], input for restart | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+1d ... +8d (1h ... 8h)` | `00 00 … 00 08` |
| Combination | Combining multiple Events and/or Inputs | Enum_8 | 1 | AND:<br>OR:<br>XOR: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)<br>+2d (2h)` | |
| Reserved | Reserved value 3 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 4 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| | Source | | | | | |
| Source | The source parameter are only existing if the port is set to OUTPUT! | | 2 | | `+1d (1h)` | `00 01` |
| Source Name | Name of the source option | String | 4 | DeviceNotReady:<br>Input1:<br>Input2:<br>SopasCommand: | `DRDY<br>IN01<br>IN02<br>SC01` | `44 52 44 59<br>49 4E 30 31<br>49 4E 30 32<br>53 43 30 31` |
| Invert | Invert the source signal | Bool_1 | 1 | Not inverted:<br>Inverted: | `+0d (0h)<br>+1d (1h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 5 | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 6 | Uint_8 | 1 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00` |
| Reserved | | | | | | |
| Reserved | Reserved value 7 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 8 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 9 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |
| Reserved | Reserved value 10 | Uint_16 | 2 | | `+0d (0h)` | `00 00` |

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Read State of the Inputs [sRN LIDinputstate]

</summary>

Use sEN LIDinputstate 1 to receive a telegram each time an input signal (e.g. by trigger) changes.

**Telegram structure: sRN LIDinputstate**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Input state | String | 14 | | `LIDinputstate` | `4C 49 44 69 6E 70 75 74 73 74 61 74 65` |

**Example: sRN LIDinputstate**
