<summary markdown="block">

### Poll One Telegram [sRN LMDscandata]

</summary>

Asking the device for the measurement values of the last valid scan. The device will respond, even if currently no measurement data is created (e.g. due to standby or log in).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot-up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

**Telegram structure: sRN LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Read | String | 3 | | `sRN` | `73 52 4E` |
| Command | Only one telegram | String | 11 | | `LMDscandata` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61` |

**Example: sRN LMDscandata**

```text
<STX>sRN{SPC}LMDscandata<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sRN LMDscandata<ETX>
```

```text
sRN LMDscandata
```

<summary markdown="block">

### Send Data Permanently [sEN LMDscandata]

</summary>

Start/ stop continuous retrievement of measurement data from device. Data will be transmitted as configured as soon as measurement data is generated by the device. No data is generated when there is an active log in, the laser is shut off (e.g. in Standby mode), the motor is stopped or in case of certain error modes (e.g. Device not ready).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot-up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

**Telegram structure: sEN LMDscandata**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Event | String | 3 | | `sEN` | `73 45 4E` |
| Command | Data telegram | String | 11 | | `LMDscandata` | `4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61` |
| Measurement | Start/stop | Enum_8 | 1 | Stop:<br>Start: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

**Example: sEN LMDscandata**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sEN{SPC}LMDscandata{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sEN LMDscandata 1<ETX>
```

```text
sEN LMDscandata 1
```

```text

```

LMDscandata - reserved values

Valid distance measurement values are values starting from 16d upwards; everything below has the following meaning:

| DIST | RSSI | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0d | 0d | Invalid measurement value; caused by very low remission (extremely dark object), object distance not within measurement range (too close or too far away) or selected filter settings at device |
| 1d - 15d | 0d | Reserved, currently not in use |
| ≥16d | >0h | Valid measurement values |
| ≥16d | 254d | Reflector detected |
| ≥16d | 255d | Reserved |

Higher measurement values will be given out with a zero, that means no measurement value detected.

## Data Reduction

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Angle Range Filter [sWN LFPangleRangeFilter]

</summary>

The angle range filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

**Telegram structure: sWN LFPangleRangeFilter**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad | String | 19 | | `LFPangleRangeFilter` | `4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72` |
| Variable Data 1 | Enables/Disables the filter | Bool_1 | 1 | Off:<br>On: | `+0d<br>+1d` | `00<br>01` |
| Variable Data 2 | ThetaStart | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40` |
| Variable Data 3 | ThetaStop | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h)` | `FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40` |
| Variable Data 4 | PhiStart | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h)` | `FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0` |
| Variable Data 5 | PhiStop | Real | 4 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `-900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h)` | `FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0` |
| Variable Data 6 | BeamIncrement | UInt_16 | 2 | No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) | `1d…+20d` | `00 01 … 00 14` |

Explanation: Enable the angle range filter and set up theta (horizontal) start -90°, theta stop +90°, phi (vertical) start -90°, phi stop +90°, beam increment 1

**Example: sWN LFPangleRangeFilter**

**CoLa A (ASCII)**

```text
<STX>sWN{SPC}LFPangleRangeFilter{SPC}1{SPC}-900000{SPC}+900000{SPC}-900000{SPC}+900000{SPC}1<ETX>
```

```text
<STX>sWN LFPangleRangeFilter 1 -900000 +900000 -900000 +900000 1<ETX>
```

```text
sWN LFPangleRangeFilter 1 -900000 +900000 -900000 +900000 1
```



**CoLa B (binary)**

```text
02 02 02 02 00 00 00 2B 73 57 4E 20 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 20 01 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 FF F2 44 60 00 0D BB A0 00 01 2E
```

| Variable data 1 | Enables/Disables the filter. | Bool | 1 | Off:<br>On: | `0d (00h)<br>+1d (01h)` | `00<br>01` |
| Variable Data 2 | Only every nth scan is output where n is given by<br>the value of uiReductionFactor. | Uint_32 | 4 | | `1d…+50d<br>(00 00 00 01h … 00 00 00 32h)` | `00 00 00 01 … 00 00 00 32` |

Enables the interval filter an set up to the 3rd scan

### Set Activation of Evaluation Group [sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup]

</summary>

The telegram is intended to activate or deactivate groups via telegram. The group activation needs to be changed from always to telegram in advance.

**Telegram structure: sMN ActivateEvaluationGroup**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Amount of evaluation groups to activate/ deactivate | Array | Uint_16 | 2 | Each array element contains two parameters:Evaluation group numberDeactivation / activation of evaluation group | `1d ... 48d (1 ... 30h)` | `00 01 … 00 30` |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 1 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `1` | `00 01` |
| Deactivation / activation of evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 1 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |
| Evaluation group number | Evaluation group 2 | UInt_16 | 2 | | `2` | `00 02` |
| Activate/ deactivate evaluation group | Activate / deactivate evaluation group 2 | Bool_1 | 1 | Deactivate:<br>Activate: | `0<br>1` | `00<br>01` |

## Cybersecurity

<details class="cola-telegram" markdown="1">
<summary markdown="block">

### Set Device Search Mode [sWN EtherCoLaScanMode]

</summary>

This command configures the Auto IP functionalities (Device search by SICK Enginnering Tools) and the changeability of the IP address. The functionality can reduces the number of open ports to a minimum.

**Telegram structure: sWN EtherCoLaScanMode**

| Telegram part | Description | Variable | Length | Additional details | Values CoLa A (ASCII) | Values CoLa B (Binary) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command type | Write | String | 3 | | `sWN` | `73 57 4E` |
| Command | Set CoLa Scan / AutoIP search settings | String | 17 | | `EtherCoLaScanMode` | `45 74 68 65 72 43 6F 4C 61 53 63 61 6E 4D 6F 64 65` |

# picoScan100 Electrical Connection and Pin Assignment

> Wire a picoScan150 power, Ethernet, and digital I/O system plug to a controller using the documented M12 pin assignments.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/electrical-connection/

# Electrical Connection

Compatible with: picoScan100

To check whether the sensor still receives its minimum supply voltage at the end of a long cable, use the [Cable Dimensioning](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cable-dimensioning/) calculator.

## Power / 3 IOs 

System plug part number: 2116047

![System plug 2116047 with Ethernet and 5-pin power connectors](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical/system-plug-2116047.png){ width="320" }
*System plug 2116047 for power and three configurable digital I/Os.*

This system plug uses a male, 5-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![5-pin PWR connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/picoscan100-pwr-5.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">5-pin PWR connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR / 3 IOs** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 2 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 3 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 4 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 5 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |

## Power / 6 IOs 

System plug part number: 2130754

![System plug 2130754 with Ethernet and 12-pin power and I/O connectors](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical/system-plug-12-pin.png){ width="320" }
*System plug 2130754 with a 12-pin power and I/O connector.*

This system plug uses a male, 12-pin, A-coded M12 connector.

![12-pin PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/picoscan100-pwr-12.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">12-pin PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR / 6 IOs** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 2 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 3 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 4 | — | Reserved; do not connect |
| 5 | — | Reserved; do not connect |
| 6 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |
| 7 | `IN4/OUT4` | Configurable digital input 4 or output 4 |
| 8 | `IN6/OUT6` | Configurable digital input 6 or output 6 |
| 9 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 10 | `IN5/OUT5` | Configurable digital input 5 or output 5 |
| 11 | — | Reserved; do not connect |
| 12 | — | Reserved; do not connect |

## Power / 6 IOs (TiM-Compatible) 

System plug part number: 2130871

![TiM-compatible system plug 2130871 with Ethernet and 12-pin power and I/O connectors](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical/system-plug-12-pin.png){ width="320" }
*System plug 2130871 uses the same housing as 2130754, with a TiM-compatible pin assignment.*

This system plug also uses a male, 12-pin connector, but its assignment differs
from system plug 2130754. It uses a TiM-compatible pin assignment.

![12-pin PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/picoscan100-pwr-12.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">12-pin PWR and I/O connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**PWR / 6 IOs (TiM-Compatible)** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `GND` | Supply return, 0 V |
| 2 | `Vs` | Supply, +9 V DC to +30 V DC |
| 3 | `IN1/OUT1` | Configurable digital input 1 or output 1 |
| 4 | `IN2/OUT2` | Configurable digital input 2 or output 2 |
| 5 | `IN3/OUT3` | Configurable digital input 3 or output 3 |
| 6 | `IN4/OUT4` | Configurable digital input 4 or output 4 |
| 7 | `IN5/OUT5` | Configurable digital input 5 or output 5 |
| 8 | `IN6/OUT6` | Configurable digital input 6 or output 6 |
| 9–12 | — | Reserved; do not connect |

## Ethernet

The Ethernet connection uses a female, 4-pin, D-coded M12 connector.

![Ethernet connector face with numbered pins](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/electrical-symbols/picoscan100-ethernet.png)
<p class="caption connector-caption">Ethernet connector face with numbered pins.</p>

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Ethernet** connector pin assignments and signal functions.</p>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `TX+` | Transmit + |
| 2 | `RX+` | Receive + |
| 3 | `TX-` | Transmit − |
| 4 | `RX-` | Receive − |

# picoScan100 Licenses and Part Numbers

> picoScan100 software licenses: streaming, field evaluation, teach-in, perpendicular distance, native ROS 2, and more, with part numbers and firmware availability.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/licenses/

# Licenses

The picoScan software packages below enable optional device functions. Activate a purchased license through the sensor's license-management workflow. The picoScan150 PRO variants (part numbers 1134610, used in the [Starter Kit](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/starter-kit/), and 1142273) are delivered with the native ROS 2 license (PICOSCAN ROSCONNECT) pre-installed; check the other licenses of your variant with its Product ID on sick.com.

## Measurement Data and Object Detection

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Measurement Data and Object Detection:** package, license, part number, and availability.</p>

| Package | License | Part number | Availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Measurement-data output | PICOSCAN STREAMING | 1134356 | Since product launch |
| 2D Object Detection | PICOSCAN 2D FIELD EVALUATION | 1134371 | Since firmware V1.3.0; S/N 2418 |
| 2D Object Detection | PICOSCAN FIELD INFRINGEMENT LOGGING | 1134370 | Since firmware V1.3.0; S/N 2418 |
| 2D Object Detection Advanced | PICOSCAN TEACH-IN | 1146090 | Since firmware V1.5.0; S/N 2445 |
| 2D Object Detection Advanced | PICOSCAN PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE | 1146093 | Since firmware V2.1.0; S/N 2517 |

2D Object Detection provides configurable fields, including island fields, and Ethernet control of field configurations. The Advanced functions require the 2D Object Detection package and add teach-in, reference-contour monitoring, and perpendicular distance measurement.

## Dynamic Sensing Profiles

Dynamic sensing profiles switch between preset scan configurations without restarting the sensor. They support application-specific operating modes, such as close-range positioning, wide-area navigation, and fast collision avoidance. These licenses are available only for Prime and Pro variants.

# picoScan100 Firmware Release Notes

> picoScan100 firmware release history from V1.0.2 to V2.3.3: new features, fixes, new CoLa telegrams and REST endpoints, and update instructions.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/release-notes/

# Release Notes

This page records picoScan100 firmware changes, fixes, and compatibility notes across releases. Use it to assess update impact and find the release information relevant to your installed firmware.

## General Information

V1.x.x/V2.x.x is standard firmware for all picoScan100 variants. Downgrades are not possible. A firmware update typically does not affect active parameter settings or purchased features / licenses for picoScan100 variants. Restart the device after activating or deactivating licenses.

## Update Instructions

**Recommended update path to V2.3.3.**

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Update Instructions:** current firmware, target firmware, recommended update tool / procedure, and firmware update file.</p>

| Current firmware | Target firmware | Recommended update tool / procedure | Firmware update file            |
| ---------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| V2.3.1           | V2.3.3          | SOPASair, web browser, or REST API  | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk.signed` |
| V2.2.1           | V2.3.3          | SOPASair, web browser, or REST API  | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk.signed` |
| V2.1.0           | V2.3.3          | SOPASair, web browser, or REST API  | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk`        |
| V2.0.0           | V2.3.3          | SOPAS ET                            | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk`        |
| V1.x.x           | V2.3.3          | SOPAS ET                            | `picoScan100_V2.3.3.spk`        |

After selecting a `.spk.signed` file, the upload process may take several seconds. Once the upload is complete, the **Install now** button becomes active and allows the update to begin. After a successful update, the device indicates completion by showing a green LED again. If the dialog becomes unresponsive, refresh the browser.

**Firmware update via SOPASair.**

Recommended for firmware versions `>= V2.1.0`. SOPASair offers the possibility of a firmware update via web browser.

**Headless firmware update via HTTP / REST.**

Possible with firmware versions `>= V1.4.0`. Follow [Firmware Update](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/#headless-via-the-rest-api) for the complete sequence with authentication. The OpenAPI description is available in the product download section.

**Firmware update via SOPAS ET.**

Recommended for firmware versions `<= V2.0.0`. Follow the [SOPAS ET steps](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/#sopas-et); the update can take up to 2 minutes.

## Firmware V2.3.3

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 31/2026; **Effective from:** S/N 2632xxxx

> Important note: Devices with serial numbers `>= 2632xxxx` can only be operated with firmware version V2.3.3 or later. Earlier firmware versions are not supported.

**Improvements and fixes.**

- Motor control has been improved for picoScan150 and picoScan120.

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** if the measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode. After a device reboot, the contamination indication output may initialize with an incorrect logical state when assigned to a digital output with inversion enabled. The output status is corrected once a new contamination event is detected.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load. This happens when the system diagnosis is called on a device where Particle filter, Moving average filter, and Streaming are active. Deactivate those filters before executing the system diagnosis.
- In very rare cases, device availability after startup is slightly delayed. In this case, the device is fully operational within 20 seconds.
- When changing input and output settings or importing configuration files, an occasional parameterization message can appear in the diagnostics overview: **Too many functions are active at the same time. Deactivate functions that are not required.** This message can be safely ignored because the error becomes inactive immediately.
- Native ROS 2 provides the ROS standard message type `MultiEchoLaserScan`. For this message type, scan profiles 1, 2, 4, and 11 are recommended.

## Firmware V2.3.1

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 22/2026; **Effective from:** S/N 2625xxxx

**New features.**

**Data output format LMDscandata configurable.**

The graphical user interface allows users to configure the content of the LMDscandata output format, for example disabling RSSI values to reduce network bandwidth.

**Data output format Compact configurable.**

The graphical user interface allows users to configure the content of the Compact output format, for example disabling RSSI values to reduce network bandwidth.

**3D point cloud capture and data export.**

For demonstration purposes, it is possible to swivel or move the scanner in a linear direction to capture a 3D point cloud of the surrounding environment using the encoder input or the integrated IMU of the picoScan150. The captured 3D point cloud is visualized in the Scan View GUI and can be exported as a `.pcd` file.

**Support for PoE system plug.**

This firmware version is required to operate the picoScan150 in combination with the newly developed PoE system plug variant.

**Support for new frontend.**

With this firmware version, picoScan150 and picoScan120 are prepared for compatibility with a new laser frontend as hardware change. The hardware change is planned for implementation in production at a later point in time. Firmware V2.3.1 or later is required to operate devices with the new hardware. Earlier firmware versions are not compatible with the new hardware.

**WebSocket events.**

Added WebSocket-based event subscription support, enabling real-time push notifications over a persistent `/apievents` connection. A single WebSocket link handles multiple event registrations, e.g. contamination, device status, field evaluation, temperature and other events.

**UDP multicast for IMU and encoder data.**

Added support for UDP multicast for both IMU and encoder data streams. The UDP destination address can now be configured as a multicast address.

**CoLa A/B port configurable.**

The CoLa A and CoLa B communication ports, default 2111 and 2112, can now be configured individually. This is useful for compatibility with other SICK LiDAR devices that support the LMDscandata output format.

**Support of Virtual Sensor Lab.**

The [Virtual Sensor Lab](https://devices.cloud.sick.com/) enables users to explore the graphical user interface without requiring a physical device. It also allows the creation of offline configuration files (`.json`) which can be exported and later imported into another device. Configuration files from physical devices can be loaded and viewed in the Virtual Sensor Lab. The web-based tool can set the system plug type, 5-pin or 12-pin. Import and export of `.sopas` files is not supported.

**Cybersecurity improvements.**

System plug variants can clone network parameters, and this firmware allows network parameter cloning to be disabled. The GUI Cyber Security page displays the encoder setup and can enable or disable encoder data streaming. Internal device dependencies were updated to address security vulnerabilities and align with cyber secure software development.

**Improvements and fixes.**

- The **Optimized for Robustness** sensitivity mode improves measurements on retroreflectors. It suppresses and filters blooming effects associated with these targets, making the measurement results more stable and robust.
- Reflector tagging is corrected for the 20 m to 30 m distance range. Previously, tags were inconsistent and some measurement points on retroreflectors were not marked as reflector returns. These points are now tagged reliably within the affected range.
- Environment teach-in results survive a device reboot and are included when a parameter file is downloaded from the device. This allows the recorded environment to be reused and simplifies configuration.
- Encoder processing no longer produces implausible values from incorrectly interpolated encoder data. The interpolation error that occurred in some cases has been corrected.
- The sectors selected for contamination indication are now retained reliably after a reboot. Previously, some sector selections were not saved correctly.
- The Native ROS 2 descriptions for **child frame** and **parent frame** are corrected; they were previously interchanged.
- Native ROS 2 now operates reliably with DHCP IP address servers.

**API changes and publications.**

For a complete reference, consult the OpenAPI description in the product
download section on [sick.com](https://www.sick.com/).

Session-token-based authentication now secures parameter-file upload, download, and import. A short-lived `X-Session-Token`, obtained at service level, creates, downloads, re-uploads, and restores a JSON parameter file.
New full-screen URLs are `http://<ip>/#/?fullscreen=` and `http://<ip>/#/?fullscreen_mode=`.
`http://<ip>/#/?scanview_fullscreen=` has been disabled.

The OpenAPI files are available for [picoScan120](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp684461) and [picoScan150](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp678507).

**Introduced telegrams / REST endpoints.**

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load when Particle filter, Moving average filter, and Streaming are active; deactivate those filters before running the diagnosis.
- Device availability may very rarely be delayed but becomes fully operational within 20 seconds.
- The occasional parameterization message **Too many functions are active at the same time. Deactivate functions that are not required.** can be ignored when it becomes inactive immediately.
- Native ROS 2 provides `MultiEchoLaserScan`, for which scan profiles 1, 2, 4, and 11 are recommended.

## Firmware V2.2.1

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 11/2026; **Effective from:** S/N 2612xxxx for picoScan150 and S/N 2613xxxx for picoScan120

**Improvements and fixes.**

This release includes minor GUI improvements and bug fixes.

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load when Particle filter, Moving average filter, and Streaming are active; deactivate those filters before running the diagnosis.
- Device availability may very rarely be delayed but becomes fully operational within 20 seconds.
- The occasional parameterization message **Too many functions are active at the same time. Deactivate functions that are not required.** can be ignored when it becomes inactive immediately.
- Native ROS 2 does not provide measurement data after DHCP fallback, so ensure that the DHCP server is available after boot.
- The Native ROS 2 GUI parameter descriptions for **child frame** and **parent frame** are interchanged.

## Firmware V2.2.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 03/2026; **Effective from:** not released for production

**New features.**

**Encoder input support.**

The device has a digital encoder input for recording incremental encoder signals. Configuration can be done via the user interface or telegram using the communication interface. The encoder input supports single-channel encoders (A) and dual-channel encoders (A/B) for direction determination. Recorded pulses are provided with a high-resolution timestamp using NTP / PTP and output either as a separate UDP stream or as part of LMDscandata. External reference signals can also be fed in, for example encoder Z signal or limit switch signals.

**Download and import of parameter files via SOPASair.**

The parameter set can be manually saved as a project file (`*.json`) on the computer via **Download / Import configuration file**. This is the generally recommended procedure. The project file can be transferred to another product and optionally password-protected. SOPAS ET is obsolete for transferring project files.

**Temperature alarm via digital output.**

The device can set a temperature alarm via digital output. The internal temperature is continuously monitored. If the set temperature is exceeded, a digital output is switched. Threshold settings can be applied via the communication interface.

**Checksum for device validation.**

The sensor can compute a checksum to verify critical device information, including device type, system plug, parameter setting, point of time of last save, calibration data, operating system and active licenses.

**Full screen mode button.**

The three-dot menu includes a full screen mode. When activated, it hides the main menu control bar. Press ESC to exit full screen.

**Improvements and fixes.**

- The GUI now offers **Native ROS 2** as a selectable data format. Communication uses DDS (Data Distribution Service) to transmit measurement data directly in ROS 2-compatible formats, without additional drivers and with minimal delay.
- Motor-controller settings have been optimized for device startup.
- The angle range filter can again be disabled for LMDscandata output. Previously, disabling the filter did not work.

**Cybersecurity improvements.**

**Signed firmware update support.**

This firmware forms the basis for signed firmware updates. Future firmware packages in `.spk.signed` format will be validated by the sensor before installation to help ensure that only authentic and tamper-proof software is installed.

**Behavioral changes.**

- The GUI provides an undo function for the last parameter change and includes minor visual improvements.
- Opening the device window in SOPAS ET now displays a generic start page with a link to the browser.
- The contamination-indication setting **Evaluation for blocked sectors** lets users choose whether blocked sectors are evaluated as heavy contamination. A sector can be blocked when the device is installed close to a wall or an object covers the optical hood. The setting is also available via CoLa A/B and REST.
- An IMU plausibility check detects missing or frozen data and creates an error-log entry when the data is implausible.
- **Reset and maintain communication interfaces** now preserves HTTPS certificates because they are part of the communication interface.

**API changes and publications.**

The OpenAPI files are available for [picoScan120](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp684461) and [picoScan150](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp678507).

## Firmware V2.1.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan120 and picoScan150; **Release date:** cw 16/2025; **Effective from:** S/N 2517xxxx for picoScan120 and picoScan150

**New features.**

**Perpendicular distance evaluation.**

Perpendicular Distance evaluation is part of the 2D Object Detection Advanced license package. It allows fields to be drawn and evaluates the minimum and maximum perpendicular distance between objects entering the field and a reference line.

A new device can be configured through the sales configurator with the 2D Object Detection Advanced package. On an existing device, activate license `1146093 PICOSCAN PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE` through License Manager.

**Reflector detection improvements.**

The reflector-detection algorithm has been improved, particularly for false positives in ambient light. Devices with serial numbers `> 2422xxxx`, which were more sensitive to false-positive reflector detection, benefit from this improvement. LMDscandata provides reflector information using RSSI value 254, and a reflector-detection filter handles double echoes from reflector targets. On picoScan120, the **optimized for reflector** mode improves measurement performance on reflector targets but can overlook very small, transparent, or mirroring objects.

**HTTPS.**

picoScan100 supports HTTPS, enabling secure and encrypted communication.

**Firmware update via SOPASair.**

SOPASair now offers firmware update capability. SOPAS ET is no longer needed for a firmware update for supported versions.

**Full screen scan view URL.**

For full-screen visualization of measurement data or 2D Object Detection:

```text
<IP>/#/?scanview_fullscreen=
```

Example:

```text
http://192.168.0.1/#/?scanview_fullscreen=
```

**Measurement data recording.**

Measurement and IMU data can be recorded and played back when used with additional recorder software.

Use the [Recorder software](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp681956).

**Improvements and fixes.**

- The 2D Object Detection history table has improved visualization. Configuration no longer becomes inconsistent when evaluations are deleted, renamed, or recreated with the same names.
- The GUI measurement tool can now measure the distance to the device center.
- SOPASair scan view provides separate show/hide controls for reflector and non-reflector scan points.
- The contamination-indication GUI element has been reworked to improve usability and fix bugs.
- LMDscandata now includes I/O states for better compatibility with products such as TiM and LMS1.
- The diagnostics overview identifies message categories with icons for Info, Warning, Error, and Fatal Error. It also displays message numbers and indicates whether a warning is active or inactive.
- Output counters no longer increment when an output is HIGH and a configuration change leaves its actual state unchanged. Resetting a counter now displays `-`, meaning zero, rather than incorrectly setting the value to `2`.
- `.sopas` files can now be imported regardless of the earlier firmware version for which they were created. A warning is displayed if information in the file does not match the target device's setup.
- Error handling has been optimized so that the message **Too many functions are active at the same time** appears less often during operation.
- The low-device-temperature warning is intended for temperatures of -5 °C or below, when motor startup may be delayed. The issue that occasionally caused this warning at higher temperatures has been fixed.
- The CoLa A/B user levels **Maintenance** and **Authorized Client** are disabled by default, matching the HTTP/REST interface behavior. They can be enabled in the GUI after logging in as **Service**. Updating from firmware earlier than V2.1.0 preserves previously enabled user levels; a factory reset restores the defaults, with **Maintenance** and **Authorized Client** disabled and **Service** enabled.
- Enabling the LMDscandata scan-range filter no longer causes the first output beam to have an incorrect distance value of `0`.
- The Teach-In setting **Start/Stop by Input Signal** is now saved permanently. Previously, rebooting or cycling power reset it to its default value.

**Behavioral changes.**

- Activating more than 20 fields exceeds the supported maximum and stops 2D Object Detection. From V2.1.0, the device status also changes to **device not ready**.
- During the **waiting for restart** output state, LED 1 is continuously yellow and LED 2 flashes green. This indicates that a restart is pending after a configured time or digital input.
- Devices shipped with firmware V2.1.0 use **Static IP** instead of **Repeat DHCP** as the DHCP fallback default. This change does not apply to devices updated in the field from V1.5.0 or lower.

**API changes and publications.**

The OpenAPI files are available for [picoScan120](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp684461) and [picoScan150](https://www.sick.com/de/en/downloads/media/swp678507).

Selected changes include `perpendicularDistanceResult`, which returns the perpendicular-distance feature's minimum distance, maximum distance, and timestamp, and `EtherCoLaScanMode`, which replaces `EnableColaScan` with the Enabled, Time-Limited, Restricted, and Disabled modes. Send `EthernetUpdate` after updating IP configuration to trigger reconfiguration. `changePassword` sets the REST interface password, `SetPassword` sets the CoLa A/B interface password, `EnableUserLevel` activates or deactivates the REST user level, and `EnableLegacyUserLevel` activates or deactivates the CoLa A/B user level. `EnableDetectionHistory` returns or sets detection history, `EvaluationsToLog` returns or sets the evaluations that are logged, and `ResetDetectionHistory` resets detection-history logs. `httpsStatus` returns HTTPS interface status, `certificateBundleInfo` returns information about the uploaded certificate bundle, `setCertificateBundleInfo` uploads a certificate bundle in PEM format through JSON, and `removeCertificateBundleInfo` removes the uploaded certificate bundle.

**Known issues.**

- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or the device is in stand-by mode.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load, and an error-log message can occur during a factory reset; both can be ignored as applicable.
- Device availability may very rarely be delayed but becomes fully operational within 20 seconds.
- There is a minimal chance of a fatal error after a firmware update; if it occurs, repeat the update. The update was successful if the device operates stably with a green LED for more than 10 minutes.
- The angle range filter cannot be disabled for LMDscandata; use start angle `-138°` and stop angle `138°`, or perform a factory reset, to output the full field of view.
- In SOPAS ET, 2D object-detection parameters can influence one another, so SOPASair is strongly recommended for parameterization.
- An invalid measurement point can appear at 0° in GUI Application > Data output, but this does not affect Compact or LMDscandata output.
- Some SOPASair notifications during and after a factory reset, firmware update, or reboot can be ignored.

## Firmware V2.0.0

- CoLa A/B remains active after `EtherAuxEnabled` is set to false, so a power cycle is required.
- The output counter does not show the correct number and must not be used to count **Device Not Ready** signals.
- Queue overflows can occur when Ethernet settings change but do not affect picoScan120 use.
- SOPAS ET can show several error messages and is not recommended; use SOPASair instead.
- The angle range filter cannot be disabled for LMDscandata; use start angle `-138°` and stop angle `138°`, or perform a factory reset.

## Firmware V1.3.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan150 only; **Release date:** cw 18/2024; **Effective from:** S/N 2418xxxx

**New features.**

**2D Object Detection.**

The new **Field Evaluation** application allows definition of up to 48 individual fields / evaluations.

Fields can be merged into groups, which can be activated by telegram or input signal. Telegrams and output signals can monitor field and application status. Maximum blanking size and detection time are individually configurable. Distance-dependent mode combines measuring points inside a field according to distance, while manipulation prevention triggers object detection if monitoring from the device to the field boundary is insufficient. **Ignore missing echo** treats a missing echo as a measuring point in the field. In Blanking mode, field evaluation reacts to all measurement points; in Reflector mode, it reacts only to points marked as reflectors. Detection history can store up to 200 entries, deleting the oldest entry when a new detection occurs.

**Contamination indication.**

The contamination indication evaluates 7 sectors regarding contamination levels. Results can be monitored in the GUI, via digital outputs or via telegram. Response time can be adjusted.

**New scan configuration.**

New scan configuration with 15 Hz scanning frequency and 1° angular resolution, profile number 11. This configuration can be used to retrofit, for example, TiM351 or TiM551.

**Improvements and fixes.**

- The 40 Hz / 0.125° scan configuration, profile 10, now provides all available echoes. Previously, it supported only one echo.
- The start and stop timestamps of each scan segment in Compact and MSGPACK output now match system time.
- The IMU streaming issue that occasionally paused data output for approximately 1 second has been fixed.
- The scan-range filter now limits LMDscandata output to the selected range instead of transmitting zero values outside it.
- LMDscandata now includes device-status and scanning-frequency information.
- The interval filter's default and minimum values have changed from 1 to 2.
- The `mResetCounter` telegram no longer resets an I/O port to its default state.
- GUI notifications have been added to improve the user experience.
- LED indication for the **RecoverableError** device state has been corrected.

**Known issues.**

- Object-detection output-reset behavior, detection-history refresh and consistency, and incorrect online help for **ignore missing echo**.
- Contamination indication segments show **clean** when measurement is stopped or in stand-by mode.
- The sector dropdown has no effect for **None** or **Weather protection hood**.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load.
- The LMDscandata angle range filter can output a first beam with distance `0` and cannot be disabled.
- An error-log entry during a factory reset can be ignored.

## Firmware V1.2.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan150 only; **Release date:** cw 09/2024; **Effective from:** S/N 2410xxxx

**New features.**

**Precision Time Protocol support.**

PTP is a synchronization mechanism for precise coordination of data acquisition across multiple LiDAR units or other clients in a network. By synchronizing internal clocks, PTP enables accurate timestamping of measurements, supporting spatial mapping and object detection. It minimizes latency and supports reliable data fusion in applications such as autonomous vehicles or industrial automation.

**Native ROS 2.**

Native ROS 2 is a digital add-on with license. The device offers native ROS 2 support using DDS to enable real-time communication and optimize interoperability with ROS 2 standards. To enable it:

Install the corresponding license through License Manager, disable MSGPACK, Compact, or LMDscandata data output, and enable Native ROS 2 with telegram `RosConnectEnable`.

**License Manager support.**

License Manager is integrated and available via:

```text
http://192.168.0.1/#/license
```

**Improvements and fixes.**

- Boot time has been optimized. The device is typically ready after 9.5 seconds, with the green LED on and data output available.
- All digital outputs now show the same electrical levels during device startup.
- Reflector detection has been improved for edge hits involving a second target. Retroreflectors can produce a measurement point at twice the actual distance; previously, this could cause the first target to be incorrectly classified as a reflector.
- The maximum input debounce time has increased to 1000 ms.
- The Compact-format scaling factor is now set correctly in the rare range-extension conditions that previously caused incorrect distance data.
- IMU data now uses the system timestamp and updates when system time is set by the user, an NTP server, or PTP.
- The picoScan sensor model in scan view has been updated.
- GUI refresh time after a reboot has been reduced to 10 seconds.
- The login dropdown now shows only enabled user levels, and the displayed angular resolution is no longer rounded.
- Visual and wording issues have been corrected, including the incorrect appearance of the distance-measuring tool.
- The redundant `SaveParameters` method has been removed. Use `mEEwriteall` to save parameters permanently.

**Known issues.**

- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load.
- In rare cases, IMU data streaming can pause for about 1 second before continuing with the latest data.
- A factory reset can trigger **IMU Queue Overflow**, which can be ignored.

## Firmware V1.1.0

**Compatible with:** picoScan150 only; **Release date:** cw 50/2023; **Effective from:** S/N 2350xxxx

**New features.**

**IMU support.**

IMU data is enabled with this release and available in Compact format. IMU type: [BOSCH BHI160B](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/smart-sensor-systems/bhi160b/).

**Cloning of communication parameters.**

Every system plug has cloning memory on board. Communication parameters such as IP address, subnet mask and gateway are stored automatically to the system plug when parameters are saved permanently. Parameters are loaded on boot up. This enables faster device exchange if the system plug remains in the application.

**Improvements and fixes.**

- Reflector detection at close range has improved. Typical detection ranges are `0.3 m <= x <= 25 m` for Core, `0.3 m <= x <= 60 m` for Prime, and `0.3 m <= x <= 120 m` for Pro.
- False-positive reflector flags no longer occur at target edges on devices calibrated in the production line. This improvement applies only to those calibrated devices.
- Measurement-core lockups in complex scenarios have been fixed. Previously, scenarios with many dynamic targets could occasionally cause a temporary device error.
- The angular error that depended on the selected dynamic sensing profile has been improved. This change applies only to devices calibrated in the production line.
- Boot-up time has been optimized to typically 11 seconds.
- Scan segments are no longer occasionally transmitted with a delay of one segment.
- The device now sends a response before executing a reboot or factory-defaults command. Previously, it rebooted immediately without answering the command.
- Ethernet-configuration input validation now prevents invalid configurations from being set.
- The static DHCP fallback IP address now works as expected.
- General GUI improvements include a better user experience in Microsoft Edge and Firefox.

**Known issues.**

- Incorrect distance data is possible in range-extension mode when using picoScan150 Pro-1 with Compact output, active range extension, scan profile 1, 2, 4, 5, or 7, and a highly reflective target at a distance greater than 65 m.
- In SOPASair, a browser tab can consume memory over time and produce an Out of memory error; restart the browser to recover.
- A file error can occur during system diagnosis under high load.
- In rare cases, IMU data streaming can time out for about 1 second.
- The IMU data-stream timestamp begins at boot and does not update with user-set time or an NTP server.

# picoScan100 Web GUI (SOPASair): All Screens and Settings

> Walkthrough of every picoScan100 SOPASair screen: basic settings, mounting, I/O, data output, field evaluation, contamination, and diagnostics.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/graphical-user-interface/

# SOPASair Walkthrough

This page describes the picoScan100 web interface and the settings in each view. Use it to commission the sensor before you automate the configuration through the API. To try the interface without a device, open it in the [Virtual Sensor Lab](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/simulation/virtual-sensor-lab/).

## Home

The Home page summarizes the sensor's state: device, connection, measurement,
field evaluation, and data-output status, device information with the
firmware version, the live scan, and the I/O states. Use it to confirm that the
sensor is online and healthy before you change settings.

![SOPASair Home page of a picoScan100](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-home.png)
*Live capture of the picoScan100 SOPASair Home page.*

## Configuration

Choose the scan configuration and the core measurement behavior. Resolution, frequency, and range trade off against each other.

*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

The live scan on the left updates as you change the configuration, which is the quickest way to judge a setting.

### Basic Settings

Basic Settings controls the scan configuration used by the sensor. The settings
are shown on the right; the live scan on the left shows the effect of the
selected frequency, angular resolution, and other settings immediately. Use
this view to check coverage and measurement behavior while commissioning.

**Coordinate System**

The device coordinate system uses one point as the origin and reference for all
laser beams and distance measurements. With no translation into a world
coordinate system, this point is also the world origin.

The horizontal beam angle is **theta** (`θ`). A beam at `θ = 0°` points along
the middle of the sensor's main viewing direction, making the scan symmetric
around the X axis. The vertical elevation angle is **phi** (`φ`) and is
measured from the X/Y plane. For a single-plane picoScan, `φ = 0°` when the
sensor is ideally mounted.

<div>
<img src="https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/configuration-coordinate-system-xy.png" alt="Device coordinate system: theta" style="width: 220px; height: 220px; object-fit: contain;">
*Horizontal beam angle <strong>theta</strong>.*
</div>
<div>
<img src="https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/configuration-coordinate-system-xz.png" alt="Device coordinate system: phi" style="width: 220px; height: 220px; object-fit: contain;">
*Vertical beam angle <strong>phi</strong>.*
</div>

Measurement data is always output in the device coordinate system. Transform it
into a world or application frame on the receiving system after accounting for
the sensor's mounting position and orientation. See
[3D point clouds with 2D LiDARs](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/3d-with-2d-lidars/) for an
example coordinate transform.

**Date and system time**

The time base can be set using various methods:

- Explicitly setting the date and time
- Transferring the time from the computer used
- Via an external NTP server (Network Time Protocol) that is accessible in the network. The technology uses UDP on port 123. This setting is recommended to ensure a correct time stamp in the detection history or error entries.
- Via an external PTP (Precision Time Protocol) master that is accessible in the network. The technology uses UDP on ports 319 and 320. This setting is recommended for precise synchronization requirements (e.g. between several devices).

**Dynamic Sensing Profiles**

LiDAR applications often need different sensor characteristics at different
times. An AMR may need the shortest response time in busy areas, a large
scanning range and good angular resolution in a warehouse, and the highest
close-range angular resolution while docking. Higher angular resolution
requires a lower scanning frequency, so choose the priority for each
application.

Dynamic Sensing Profiles allow the scan's core parameters to be changed during
operation without restarting the sensor. The Scan Data Configuration function
allows fast switching between profiles:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Basic Settings:** profile, frequency, angular resolution, and typical use.</p>

| Profile | Frequency | Angular resolution | Typical use |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 15 Hz | 0.5° | Object detection with large scanning ranges |
| 2 | 15 Hz | 0.33° | TiM series retrofit |
| 3 | 20 Hz | 0.1° | Fine positioning or environment maps |
| 4 | 20 Hz | 0.25° | Low-noise measurements; recommended for LiDAR-LOC |
| 5 | 25 Hz | 0.25° | LMS100 series retrofit |
| 6 | 30 Hz | 0.1° | Fine positioning or environment maps |
| 7 | 40 Hz | 0.25° | Fast object detection at a large scanning range |
| 8 | 50 Hz | 0.25° | Very fast object detection |
| 9 | 15 Hz | 0.05° | Highest angular resolution for static measurements |
| 10 | 40 Hz | 0.125° | High angular resolution and high scan rate |
| 11 | 15 Hz | 1° | TiM series retrofit |

Available profiles depend on the device variant and license; see
[Licenses](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/licenses/).

*How to change the device name.*
*How to change scanning frequency and angular resolution.*

### Filter

Clean up the scan before it leaves the sensor by suppressing extra echoes, artifacts and airborne particles.

![Filter settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-configuration-filter-tile.png)
*Example filter settings in the picoScan100 web interface. Select parameters according to the requirements of each application.*

If present, the filters are applied in the following order:

1. Fog filter
2. Echo filter
3. Particle filter
4. Moving average filter
5. Filters for data reduction and the region of interest filter

For detailed behavior and examples, see [Filter details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/).

### Inertial Measuring Unit (IMU)

Use the IMU view to inspect the sensor's current orientation and acceleration.

*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

The IMU view displays the yaw, pitch, and roll angles in degrees, together with the measured acceleration on the X, Y, and Z axes in meters per second squared. The orientation indicator provides a visual representation of the current sensor position.

Use these values as a guide when checking the sensor installation or interpreting the scan coordinate system.

### Contamination Indication

Monitor the optics cover for dirt and get a warning before measurement quality drops.

*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

The contamination status provides a live reading of Clean, Minor, Heavy, or Blocked. The segment wheel identifies where contamination is accumulating around the optics cover. Configure whether contamination triggers a warning, an error, or both, and adjust the sensitivity and outputs for the environment.

*How to receive contamination indication through event-driven CoLa.*

### Connection Options

Give the sensor its permanent Ethernet identity so it fits your network.

*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

Choose static addressing to enter a fixed IP address, or DHCP to have a server assign the address automatically, according to your application and network requirements. The IP address must be unique on your network. The subnet mask defines which addresses are local, for example `255.255.255.0`, and the default gateway provides access to other subnets. The MAC address and calculated speed are read-only values for reference and firewall rules.

1. Set the addressing mode to Static.
2. Enter the IP, subnet mask, and gateway for your network.
3. Press Apply.
4. Reconnect the browser at the new address.

Pressing Apply drops your current browser connection.

### Inputs and Outputs

Configure the multifunction I/O ports and map field-evaluation results and device states to physical outputs.

*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

Set each port as an input or an output and give it a name.
Bind an output to a source, such as a field-evaluation result or a device state.
Configure the logic (HIGH or LOW active), inversion, restart behavior, and status log.
The right panel shows the live status and counters for every port.

I/O is a simple way to connect a PLC when you do not want to parse the data stream.

*How to switch digital outputs by API.*

## Application

### Data Output

Decide what measurement data leaves the sensor and how it is streamed to your system.

*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

For data output, select Compact, MSGPACK, LMDscandata, or Native ROS 2 according to your application. For Compact or MSGPACK, configure serialization to include only the RSSI and properties layers your application needs. Reduce bandwidth at the source with an angular-range filter that retains one sector or an interval filter that reduces the number of scans sent per second.

![Compact measurement data output](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-compact.png)
*Compact outputs measurement data over UDP and provides separate controls for RSSI and properties serialization.*

*MSGPACK outputs measurement data over UDP to the configured destination address and port.*

![LMDscandata measurement data output](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-lmdscandata.png)
*LMDscandata provides CoLa ASCII and CoLa Binary TCP ports. Restart the sensor after changing a port.*

![Native ROS 2 measurement data output](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-native-ros2.png)
*Native ROS 2 configures the sensor and reference coordinate frames, namespace, and DDS domain ID.*

![IMU data output settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-imu.png)
*The IMU data output panel enables IMU streaming and configures the destination port and IP address.*

![Encoder data output settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-encoder.png)
*The Encoder data output panel enables encoder-data streaming and configures the destination port and IP address.*

![Data reduction settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-reduction.png)
*The Data reduction panel reduces the transmitted data with an interval filter and an angular range filter.*

For detailed filter behavior, see [Filter details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/).

For the Compact format, a segment that lies entirely outside the selected range
is omitted. A segment that is only partly within the range remains in the output
and its outside values are filled with `0`.

![Range filter settings](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-range-filter.png)

![Region of interest in the scan view](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-data-output-region-of-interest.png)
*The scan view shows the selected region of interest and the points detected within it.*

### Field Evaluation

Draw 2D fields in the sensor's scan plane. The sensor detects points inside them without an external computer.

*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

Each field belongs to an evaluation group that combines field geometry, logic, and output. A field state can drive a physical output (see [Inputs and outputs](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/graphical-user-interface/#inputs-and-outputs)) or appear in the detection list for your software. A group can remain active continuously or be switched by an input, for example to monitor a zone only while a machine is moving. Pan and zoom the scan view to check field coverage across the full aperture angle.

*Live capture of creating a detection field on a picoScan100.*

1. On the Field evaluation panel, click **Add group** to create an evaluation group.
2. The group opens an evaluation chain: Field → Evaluation → Output.
3. Click the Field node to define the field geometry: draw a contour, or use Teach-in to capture the current environment as the field.
4. Set the evaluation logic and wire the result to an output; the field then appears live in the 2D view.
5. Click the floppy-disk icon in the toolbar to save the configuration permanently (until you do, changes live in RAM and are lost on restart).

The [REST API](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/) can also create, change, and activate evaluation groups; see [Field Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/#configure-over-the-api).

- [How to draw fields and detect objects](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article?id=b3822c6c-a151-f011-877b-7c1e52272c21)
- [How to use a taught background for field evaluation](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article?id=cf43c5fc-4350-f011-b4cc-7c1e52272c21)

*How to configure a field for retro-reflectors only.*
*How to use a contour as a reference.*
*How to activate fields through HTTP.*
*How to read field evaluation state through HTTP.*
*How to receive field evaluation state via event-driven CoLa.*
*How to use the REST API client.*

### Perpendicular Distance Measurement

Each evaluation group measures the perpendicular distance from the sensor's
scan line to the nearest object inside a zone. Like [field evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/graphical-user-interface/#field-evaluation),
it runs on the sensor, but returns a distance rather than a
field-clear/field-infringed state; no raw-scan processing on a host is needed.

*Perpendicular distance measurement in SOPASair.*

The Max. blanking size setting ignores gaps smaller than the set width, and the Detection time setting sets how long an object must be present (in scans) before it counts.

1. On the Perpendicular distance measurement panel, click **Add group**.
2. Draw the zone the measurement applies to, the same way you draw a field.
3. Set Max. blanking size and Detection time under Object detection to
   match your target and required responsiveness.
4. Read the distance in the Result list for distance measurement, or wire it
   into your software over the [REST API](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/)
   or [WebSocket events](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/websocket-events/).
5. Click the floppy-disk icon to save the configuration permanently (until you do,
   changes live in RAM and are lost on restart).

![Result list for distance measurement](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-application-perpendicular-distance-result-list.png)
*The Result list shows the minimum and maximum distance and the coordinates of the measuring points for each evaluation.*

## Diagnostics

The health dashboard shows device, connection, measurement, and data-output status; the power-on counter, operating hours, temperature, and most recent parameterization; and a filterable event log with message severity, ID, time, and description. You can create and download a diagnostic file for SICK service; creating a new file overwrites the previous one.

![Diagnostics overview screen](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-diagnosis-overview.png)
*Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.*

# Asset Administration Shell (AAS) for SICK LiDAR Sensors

> Overview of the SICK Asset Administration Shell for LiDAR product part numbers and the product data it provides.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/asset-administration-shell/

# Asset Administration Shell

Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

The Asset Administration Shell (AAS) is the standardized digital twin of Industry 4.0. SICK publishes an AAS for each product part number at [aas.sick.com](https://aas.sick.com). Access requires a SICK ID login. The AAS describes the product type in a machine-readable format, which makes it useful for engineering tools and asset management systems.

## What to Expect

- **Nameplate:** manufacturer, product designation, order code, and markings such as CE and UKCA
- **Technical data:** product classification (ECLASS, ETIM) and key technical properties
- **Documents:** data sheet, operating instructions, dimensional drawing, and certificates
- **CAD data:** 3D models such as STEP files and the EPLAN macro
- **Contact information:** SICK sales and service contacts

The AAS describes the part number, not an individual device. Serial number, firmware version, configuration, status, and measurement data come from the device itself through the [REST API](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/), the [CoLa interface](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/cola-interface/), and the data streams.

## Link a Device to Its AAS

Each device is identified by its product ID
[`pid.sick.com/{P/N}/{S/N}`](https://pid.sick.com/), made of the part number
and the serial number from the type label. Both values can also be read from
the device over the REST API. The part number connects the device to its AAS.

# Verify LiDAR Firmware and Parameters with LFTchecksum (MD5)

> Use the LFTchecksum REST resource to verify firmware, calibration, and persisted parameters with MD5 digests, and understand RAM versus EEPROM state.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/checksums/

# Checksums

Compatible with: multiScan200 picoScan100

The `LFTchecksum` is a read-only REST resource that returns MD5 digests over four independent software and configuration areas of the device. It lets you verify at any time that nothing has changed since a known-good reference: detect unintended parameter changes, confirm a configuration file applied correctly, or check that a firmware update touched only the areas it should.

See the [multiScan200](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-rest-openapi/) or
[picoScan100](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/) REST API reference for the
endpoint definition.

## Reading It

No authentication required:

```http
GET /api/LFTchecksum
```

```json
{
  "header": { "status": 0, "message": "Ok" },
  "data": { "LFTchecksum": {
    "MD5SumOK":       true,
    "MD5LinuxRoot":   "8439a3f5bb209f3d51557d509169ec60",
    "MD5App":         "304f9a18302e2b635da2c2c220463119",
    "MD5Calibration": "bc5e5d5df638dc45c85937c8c67b59d7",
    "MD5Parameters":  "07f18c8032e24ac65ca0ed7c04be6a62"
  } }
}
```

## The Four Sub-Checksums

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**The Four Sub-Checksums:** field, covers, and changes when….</p>

| Field            | Covers                            | Changes when…                                                                          |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MD5LinuxRoot`   | Linux root filesystem (OS layer)  | A firmware update modifies the OS partition                                            |
| `MD5App`         | Application binary and libraries  | A firmware update installs a new application version                                   |
| `MD5Calibration` | Factory calibration data          | Calibration is recalculated/overwritten (factory service only)                         |
| `MD5Parameters`  | Persistent parameter set (EEPROM) | Parameters are persisted via `WriteEeprom`, or a config file is imported and persisted |
| `MD5SumOK`       | Overall integrity flag            | `false` if any of the four fails its internal verification                             |

## RAM vs. Persistent Storage

The device keeps two parameter states at once:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**RAM vs. Persistent Storage:** parameter state, storage location, persistence after reboot, and effect on `MD5Parameters`.</p>

| State          | Where          | Survives reboot?                                                                    | Reflected in `MD5Parameters`?             |
| -------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Working copy   | RAM            | No (a `RebootDevice` flushes RAM to EEPROM first, so it survives a software reboot) | No, until `WriteEeprom` or `RebootDevice` |
| Persisted copy | EEPROM / flash | Yes                                                                                 | Yes                                       |

**An unchanged `MD5Parameters` does not mean RAM is unchanged:** REST writes modify the working copy. Unlike `RebootDevice`, which persists RAM first, `SoftReset` and a hard power-cycle discard unsaved changes.

## When Does Each Sub-Checksum Change?

The following table shows the behavior of a picoScan150 (● = changed, - = unchanged):

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**When Does Each Sub-Checksum Change?** Scenario and resulting change of the LinuxRoot, app, calibration, and parameters checksums.</p>

| Scenario | LinuxRoot | App | Calibration | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Two consecutive reads, no operation | - | - | - | - |
| Change a parameter in RAM only (no `WriteEeprom`) | - | - | - | - |
| Change in RAM, then `SoftReset` | - | - | - | - |
| Change in RAM, then `RebootDevice` (persists first) | - | - | - | ● |
| Change + `WriteEeprom` | - | - | - | ● |
| `CreateParameterBackup` → `RestoreParameterBackup`, same file, no content change | - | - | - | - |
| `LoadApplicationDefaults` (destructive) | - | - | - | ● |
| Firmware upgrade | ● | ● | - | - |
| Firmware downgrade | ● | ● | - | - |

`MD5Calibration` does not change through normal end-user operations. A change there indicates a factory calibration update or an unexpected write to the calibration partition, so treat it as a red flag.

## A Practical Integrity Workflow

1. Record all four hashes from a known-good device (the reference).
2. After any change (a config push, a [restore](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/configuration-backup-and-restore/), a [firmware update](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/)), read `LFTchecksum` again.
3. Compare field by field: a firmware update should move `MD5LinuxRoot` + `MD5App` only; a persisted config change should move `MD5Parameters` only; `MD5Calibration` should never move.
4. Anything else is unexpected: investigate before putting the device back into service.

Compact and MSGPACK telegrams carry a CRC32 per packet (see [Compact Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/compact-format/#frame-layout)); CoLa B telegrams carry a 1-byte XOR checksum. The `LFTchecksum` covers the stored software and configuration, which complements these on-the-wire checks.

# Device State and Availability

> Check sensor availability with its status LEDs, a configurable digital output, or the REST and CoLa device-state interfaces.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/device-state/

# Device State

Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

The sensors provide several ways to check whether they are available and
ready to measure. Choose the local indication that suits the installation, or
read the state through REST or CoLa from a host application.

## Status LEDs

Status LEDs indicate the device state. On devices where the LEDs can be
switched off, they do not indicate anything while disabled. See the device
operating instructions for the meanings of the individual LED states.

## Digital Output: Device Not Ready

Use a digital output when an external controller or PLC needs a hardware
signal for device availability:

1. Open the sensor web interface and log in as **Service**.
2. Open **Inputs and Outputs**.
3. Select **Device not ready** as the source for the output that should signal
   the status.
4. Configure the restart time, switching logic, and electrical connection
   logic for the installation.

If contamination is expected and should be signaled separately, select
**Contamination indication** as an output source. See
[Contamination Indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/contamination-indication/)
for its configuration and behavior.

## Read State over REST or CoLa

Two state values are available. `SCdevicestate` gives a simple readiness
result; `DeviceStatus` (REST) / `DevSta` (CoLa A/B) provides more detail:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Simple readiness (`SCdevicestate`):** value and meaning.</p>

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Busy or logged in |
| `1` | Ready |
| `2` | Error |

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Detailed state (`DeviceStatus` / `DevSta`):** value and meaning.</p>

| Value | State | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Reserved | Reserved value. |
| `1` | Startup | The device is starting. |
| `2` | Service mode | A service action is in progress, such as a software update or comprehensive parameter exchange. This state does not indicate whether the device can operate normally. |
| `3` | Normal operation | Startup is complete and no errors or warnings have occurred. |
| `4` | Suspended operation | An internal or environmental condition prevents adequate measurement. |
| `5` | Service recommended | Measurement is operating as specified, but a service technician may need to address an issue. |
| `6` | Service required | Measured values are still available, but the issue may affect them; service is required. |
| `7` | Recoverable error | The device has a malfunction and measurement service is likely disrupted; service may be able to resolve it. |
| `8` | Fatal error | A fatal error has occurred; reset and reboot the device. |

For exact request and response formats, see the REST API references and the
CoLa listing sections:

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**References:** device, REST, `DevSta`, and `SCdevicestate`.</p>

| Device | REST | `DevSta` | `SCdevicestate` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LRS4000 | [OpenAPI](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/api-rest-openapi/) | – | [sRN SCdevicestate](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/api-cola-telegrams/#read-the-device-state-srn-scdevicestate) |
| multiScan100 | [OpenAPI](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-rest-openapi/) | [sRN DevSta](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#read-the-device-state-srn-devsta) | [sRN SCdevicestate](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#read-the-device-state-srn-scdevicestate) |
| multiScan200 | [OpenAPI](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-rest-openapi/) | [sRN DevSta](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-cola-telegrams/#read-device-state-srn-devsta) | [sRN SCdevicestate](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-cola-telegrams/#read-device-ready-state-srn-scdevicestate) |
| picoScan100 | [OpenAPI](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-rest-openapi/) | [sRN DevSta](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#read-the-device-state-srn-devsta), [sEN DevSta](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#receive-the-device-state-by-event-sen-devsta) | [sRN SCdevicestate](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#read-the-device-state-srn-scdevicestate), [sEN SCdevicestate](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/api-cola-telegrams/#receive-the-device-state-by-event-sen-scdevicestate) |
