# ROS 2 Reversing Assistant with an Ambient-Light Image

> Level 3 multiScan270 project: publish SDK point clouds and ambient-light images over ROS 2 with Zenoh, receive field events, and select monitoring groups.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/beginner-projects/ros2-reversing-assistant-camera/

# ROS 2 Reversing Assistant with an Ambient-Light Image

Compatible with: multiScan200

<div class="tool-intro" markdown>

![ROS 2](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/integration-notes/ros2-logo.png)
This Level 3 project combines a multiScan270, an SDK-based ROS 2 wrapper,
asynchronous field status, and an ambient-light view in RViz or another
ROS-connected display.

</div>

## What You'll Learn

- How to wrap sick_perception_sdk data as ROS 2 topics over Zenoh.
- How to combine WebSocket field events with REST field-group selection.
- How to show the ambient-light image next to the point cloud in RViz.

## Application Background

A reversing assistant should show the area behind a vehicle and indicate
whether the selected monitoring field is occupied. The operator switches
between a close-range field for confined spaces and a wider monitoring field.
The display must show the **confirmed** group, not just the requested mode.

![Forklift reversing toward stacked material with an illustrative monitoring area and driver display](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/beginner-projects/multiscan270-reversing-camera-application.png)
*Application illustration: an obstacle warning and a view of the reversing area help the driver assess the situation.*

The multiScan270 provides a grayscale ambient-light image, not an RGB camera
stream. Publish it as a ROS image so a display can show it alongside the point
cloud and field status.

![Example grayscale multiScan ambient-light image showing railway tracks, trees, hills and overhead line poles](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/beginner-projects/multiscan270-ambient-light-example.png)
*Ambient-light image example supplied for this project. The same type of image can be streamed through a ROS Image topic to RViz or a vehicle display; this picture is illustrative, not a capture from the current live session.*

This prototype is a warning aid, not a safety function. Do not connect it to
braking, steering, or motion authorization. Missing data, inactive fields, and
disconnected communication must appear unavailable, never as a clear reversing area.

## Before You Start

- Use a supported ROS 2 installation with compatible `rmw_zenoh_cpp`, RViz,
  colcon, and C++17 build tools. The architecture does not require a particular
  ROS distribution; match compiler, Python, and runtime libraries to your installation.
- Use SDK 2.0.0 or a compatible newer release with the multiScan200 driver.
  Keep SDK build and dependency setup separate from the ROS workspace.
- Configure the two existing fields in **different TELEGRAM-controlled groups**.
  Follow [Field Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/#activate-and-monitor-a-group)
  rather than recreating the configuration procedure here. Record evaluation IDs,
  group IDs, and result-list positions separately; confirm which volume is near/wide.
- Enable ambient data in Compact type 6 without overwriting other output options.
  Check `compactTelegramType6Content` in the
  [multiScan200 REST reference](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/api-rest-openapi/).
- Use the [WebSocket Events](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/websocket-events/) registration
  pattern for `FieldEvaluationResult`; verify support on the target device.
  Offer compression, but do not require it when the server does not negotiate it.

![multiScan270 configuration view showing a point cloud and two monitoring volumes](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/beginner-projects/multiscan270-reversing-fields.png){ width="50%" }
*Configuration example: retain the existing field geometry and assign each monitoring volume to its own selectable group.*

![Field-group activation settings showing the designation Close Range, activation Telegram, and Initially active enabled](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/beginner-projects/multiscan270-field-group-activation.png){ width="50%" }
*Field-group example: name the group <strong>Close Range</strong> and select <strong>Telegram</strong> activation so the application can control it. <strong>Initially active</strong> defines its startup state; the screenshot shows it enabled. Configure the wide-range field in a separate group and verify both groups' startup states before selecting a mode.*

## Suggested Data Path

Unlike [native ROS 2 integration](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/#native-ros-2),
this approach receives Compact data through the host SDK and publishes ROS
messages itself. Zenoh transports those messages; it does not replace the
device's TCP, WebSocket, or REST interfaces.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    sensor["multiScan270"]
    sdk["SDK scan/image node"]
    events["Field status/control node"]
    ros["ROS 2 over Zenoh"]
    display["RViz or vehicle display"]
    sensor -->|"Compact TCP"| sdk
    sensor -->|"WebSocket events"| events
    events -->|"REST group selection"| sensor
    sensor -->|"REST contour read"| events
    sdk -->|"Point cloud + ambient image"| ros
    events -->|"Field status + colored contour markers"| ros
    ros --> display
```

*Reversing-assistant data path: the SDK publishes point clouds and ambient-light images, while a separate node handles field events and REST control. ROS 2 over Zenoh carries the data to RViz or a vehicle display.*

The wrapper publishes `points` (`PointCloud2`), `ambient_light` (`Image`),
`field_states` (both evaluations with validity/activity), `field_markers`
(`MarkerArray` volumes colored by live state), and `diagnostics`
under `/sick_multiscan200_node`. A `select_field_group` service selects
`near` or `wide`, verifies REST success and group readback, then waits for a
fresh event snapshot before declaring field results current.

## Check the Result

- RViz shows the point cloud and the ambient-light image.
- The field volumes are green while free and turn red when an object enters.
- Calling `select_field_group` switches between `near` and `wide`, and the
  group readback matches the selection.

## Example Solution

![RViz point cloud with the actual near field outlined in green and labeled FREE, and the farther field outlined in red and labeled INFRINGED](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/beginner-projects/multiscan270-rviz-field-states.png)
*RViz example: field volumes read through REST are overlaid on the SDK point cloud. Live field events color evaluation 1 green (FREE) and evaluation 2 red (INFRINGED); colors change with the reported state.*

Use the following **single prompt** to build the wrapper in your own workspace.
Its phases also separate the reusable scan/image wrapper from field control.

<details>
<summary>Expand the complete project prompt</summary>

```markdown
# Build an SDK-Based ROS 2 Reversing Assistant

Create an OS-neutral multiScan270 warning prototype. Use sick_perception_sdk
2.0.0 or a compatible newer release, not the sensor's native ROS publisher.
Use the installed ROS 2 distribution with matching rmw_zenoh_cpp and RViz;
do not require migration to a named distribution. Inspect the actual SDK
headers and device OpenAPI instead of guessing APIs or firmware capabilities.

## Phase 1: Workspace and Interfaces

Create a C++17 ament_cmake package sick_multiscan200_node for SDK reception
and custom ROS interfaces. Use a separate Python rclpy package
sick_multiscan200_events with an asyncio WebSocket/REST client so network
control never blocks scan callbacks. Deliver launch, YAML and RViz files.
Keep the SDK and ROS sources unchanged.

Parameters: sensor_address, scan_port (default 2115), frame_id (lidar),
mirror_image, publish_identity_tf (false), mapping_verified (false),
and separate near/wide evaluation IDs, group IDs and zero-based result indexes.
Validate all values. Require verified mapping before trusting field status
or enabling switching; do not infer group IDs from evaluation IDs.

Publish under /sick_multiscan200_node:
- points: sensor_msgs/PointCloud2
- ambient_light: sensor_msgs/Image
- field_states: custom FieldStateArray
- field_markers: visualization_msgs/MarkerArray
- diagnostics: diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray
- select_field_group: custom service, string mode -> success/message/group ID

Each FieldState includes evaluation_id, group_id, raw_state, valid, active,
and reason. Use reliable KeepLast(5) for scan/image and reliable
transient-local KeepLast(1) for status. Report scan/image/event health separately.

## Phase 2: SDK Point Cloud

Use sick::multiScan200::Driver and scanDataReceiver().setup(scan_port).
Attach an explicitly typed UnorganizedPointCloud callback plus a raw
MultiScan200Data callback; the SDK multiplexes them. Enable Cartesian
coordinates, intensity, time offsets, ring, layer and echo indexes.

Map SDK fields/offsets/types to PointCloud2, preserve meter scaling and
sensor acquisition time, and validate sizes, byte counts and endian order.
ROS PointField has no Int64/Uint64: reject them or numerically repack;
never relabel integer bytes as FLOAT64. Handle timestamp overflow explicitly.

## Phase 3: Ambient Image and RViz

Read type-6 ambientLightData and its actual metadata dimensions. Convert
column-major samples to row-major mono16, with step=width*2 and explicit
little-endian bytes. Mirror horizontally only when mirror_image is enabled.
Preserve sensor time and raw pixel values. Reject malformed/partial frames;
skip missing image data with a diagnostic, never synthesize an image.

Configure RViz PointCloud2 and Image displays, reliable QoS and fixed frame
lidar. Normalize only the displayed image. Do not use Camera without
CameraInfo or invent calibration. Leave map-to-sensor identity TF disabled;
moving vehicles require real mounting/localization transforms and clock sync.

## Phase 4: Field Events and Group Selection

Register FieldEvaluationResult at ws://<sensor_address>/apievents using
the documented event envelope. Handle both initial registration data and
subsequent events. Offer permessage-deflate, accept an uncompressed session,
and explicitly report unsupported registration or malformed data.

Preserve raw device states. Only a current FREE result for a confirmed
active group is clear; inactive, unknown, disconnected or pending is not.
Keep transition states as warnings. Reconnect with bounded backoff,
resubscribe and invalidate old results until a fresh snapshot arrives.
A quiet healthy subscription is not automatically stale.

The near/wide service touches only the two configured groups. Serialize
requests, mark status pending, check HTTP and device response headers and
every activation result, then verify target active/other inactive by readback.
Do not assume switching is atomic. Discard old in-flight results and obtain
a fresh subscription snapshot after switching. Monitor external group
changes even while field events continue arriving.

Read each evaluation's contour and configuration through the REST API,
using the documented authentication without storing credentials in the
workspace. Convert polygon coordinates and lower/upper Z limits from
millimeters to meters in the sensor frame. Publish the actual field volumes
as RViz markers, with green for FREE, red for INFRINGED, amber for transition
states, gray for inactive and a distinct unknown indication on invalid or
disconnected data. Show evaluation IDs and state labels. Never invent
geometry when access is denied; report the error and request authentication.

## Phase 5: Build and Run

Provide Windows and Linux build/environment instructions, a combined launch
file, YAML configuration and RViz layout. Match SDK/ROS compiler runtimes
(including /MD on Windows) and stop/join workers cleanly on shutdown.
Start a Zenoh router and use the same middleware/domain in all terminals.
Do not create/delete fields, write EEPROM or change network settings.
Keep verification scripts, captures and test reports local, outside the guide.
Explain clock synchronization, field-mapping and scene-orientation checks.
```

</details>

## Run and Display

After building the generated packages, activate ROS and your workspace in
every terminal. Select the same middleware and domain for all processes:

=== "Windows PowerShell"

    ```powershell
    $env:RMW_IMPLEMENTATION = "rmw_zenoh_cpp"
    $env:ROS_DOMAIN_ID = "187"
    ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd
    ```

=== "Linux"

    ```bash
    export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION="rmw_zenoh_cpp"
    export ROS_DOMAIN_ID="187"
    ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd
    ```

Use an available router endpoint and a domain appropriate for your system.
In another activated terminal, launch with your edited YAML path; the launch
file must load it for both nodes. In a third, open the generated RViz layout.
These relative paths assume the generated workspace is the working directory:

```bash
ros2 launch sick_multiscan200_node multiscan200.launch.py \
  config:="$PWD/src/sick_multiscan200_node/config/reversing_assistant.yaml"
rviz2 -d src/sick_multiscan200_node/rviz/reversing_assistant.rviz
```

On PowerShell, use native paths and its continuation syntax instead:

```powershell
ros2 launch sick_multiscan200_node multiscan200.launch.py `
  "config:=$PWD\src\sick_multiscan200_node\config\reversing_assistant.yaml"
rviz2 -d .\src\sick_multiscan200_node\rviz\reversing_assistant.rviz
```

The **Image** display subscribes to `/sick_multiscan200_node/ambient_light`.
A custom vehicle display can subscribe to that same topic. Keep **Fixed Frame**
at `lidar` for the stationary example; the ambient view is not a calibrated
overlay on the point cloud.

Inspect status and request a group using the generated interfaces:

```bash
ros2 topic echo --once /sick_multiscan200_node/field_states
ros2 service call /sick_multiscan200_node/select_field_group \
  sick_multiscan200_node/srv/SelectFieldGroup "{mode: near}"
```

```powershell
ros2 service call /sick_multiscan200_node/select_field_group `
  sick_multiscan200_node/srv/SelectFieldGroup "{mode: wide}"
```

Confirm the returned group and current field status. Before vehicle use,
check actual near/wide geometry, sensor clock synchronization and image
orientation with an asymmetric scene. Do not change a working installation
or persistent sensor settings merely to follow the example.

# Troubleshooting SICK LiDAR Sensors

> Fix common SICK LiDAR issues, look up error codes, and create a diagnostic file for SICK support.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/

# Troubleshooting

Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

Start here when a sensor does not connect, does not send data, or reports an error.

* [Common Issues](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/common-issues/): symptom and check tables for connection, configuration, and measurement data.
* [Diagnostics](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/diagnostics/): create a diagnostic file on the device and send it to SICK for analysis.
* [Error Codes](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/error-codes/): interpret reported errors and recommended actions.

## Get Support

Create a diagnostic file in SOPASair (**Diagnostics → Overview → Diagnostic file**) and send it to SICK with a description of the problem. See [Diagnostics](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/diagnostics/) and [Contact](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/contact/).

# Common SICK LiDAR Issues and Quick Fixes

> Symptom and check tables for SICK LiDAR connection, configuration, REST access, and measurement-data problems.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/common-issues/

# Common Issues

Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

Quick fixes for the problems you are most likely to encounter during commissioning and integration. Each row links to the page with the details.
Available settings, protocols, and menu paths vary by device family and firmware.
Use the relevant device guide and release notes to confirm support.

## Connection

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Connection:** symptom and check.</p>

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Sensor not reachable / ping fails | Computer and sensor in the same subnet; power and Ethernet connected ([Getting Started](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/getting-started/)) |
| IP address unknown | [Device Discovery](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/device-discovery/): SOPAS ET search, or ARP when device search is disabled |
| Lost connection after an IP change | Move the computer to the new subnet, or use device search to find the sensor |
| IP change through device search is rejected | The default IP change policy allows it only within 60 s after boot; reboot or log in ([IP Address Assignment](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/ip-address-assignment/#troubleshooting)) |
| Web UI does not load | Open `http://<ip>/` in Chrome, Edge, or Firefox; clear the cache; check that the web server is not disabled ([Cybersecurity](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/cybersecurity/#web-server)) |
| HTTPS refuses connections after a certificate upload | Read `httpsStatus` over HTTP on port 80, fix the certificate, and upload it again ([HTTPS & Certificates](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/https-and-certificates/#remove-the-bundle)) |

## Configuration

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Configuration:** symptom and check.</p>

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Cannot change settings in the web UI | Log in with an enabled [user level](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/); without login, the UI is read-only |
| REST response has `header.status` 4 (Access Denied) | The HTTP status is always `200`; check `header.status`. Fetch a new challenge for every `POST`, check the password and that the user level is enabled, and wait 30 s after five failed logins ([REST Interface](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/#status-codes-and-errors)) |
| REST file transfer returns 403 | Send a valid `X-Session-Token` header ([Backup & Restore](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/configuration-backup-and-restore/)) |
| Settings lost after power cycle | Persist with `WriteEeprom` or **Save permanently** ([REST Interface](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/#reading-vs-writing)) |
| CoLa `sFA` error response | Look up the [CoLa error code](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/cola-interface/#cola-error-codes) |
| Web UI shows an error ID | Look up the ID in the [Error Codes](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/error-codes/) list |
| Need to restore factory settings | [How to perform a factory reset](https://support.sick.com/sick-knowledgebase/article?id=e1f49414-a351-f011-877b-7c1e52263b55) |
| Firmware update stuck or fails | Do not power-cycle while `UpdateState` is `1`; allow 2-5 minutes for flash and reboot; on `3` (Error), check for the correct `.spk.signed` package ([Firmware Update](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/#error-handling)) |

## Measurement Data

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Measurement Data:** symptom and check.</p>

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| No UDP data arrives | Data output enabled and destination IP/port set to your computer; Windows network profile set to Private; firewall allows the UDP port ([Compact Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/compact-format/#transport)) |
| No TCP data on LRS4000 or multiScan200 | The sensor sends Compact over TCP only while a client is connected; connect to port `2115` ([Compact Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/compact-format/#transport)) |
| LMDscandata returns only zeros | The output format is not set to LMDscandata; `sRN LMDscandata` then answers without an error ([LMDscandata Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/lmdscandata-format/#receive-lmdscandata)) |
| Scan view empty | Measurement is active and data output is enabled in the device's web interface |
| CRC errors in your parser | Compact: CRC32 over the whole frame; MSGPACK: CRC32 over the MSGPACK buffer only ([MSGPACK Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/msgpack-format/#framing)) |
| Fewer points than expected | [Filters](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/) and scan range reduce or zero out points |
| No ROS 2 topics visible on a device with Native ROS 2 support | Cyclone DDS configured with the host interface IP; matching domain ID ([Native ROS 2](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/#native-ros-2)) |
| WebSocket closes with error 1002 on a device with WebSocket support | Check the negotiated extensions and firmware; use a client compatible with the negotiated mode ([WebSocket Events](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/websocket-events/#troubleshooting)) |
| Reduced range or warnings | Check [contamination indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/contamination-indication/) and clean the optics cover |

If the problem persists, create a [diagnostic file](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/diagnostics/) and contact SICK.

# Diagnostic File for SICK LiDAR Sensors

> Create a diagnostic file on a SICK LiDAR sensor in SOPASair and send it to your local SICK contact for analysis.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/diagnostics/

# Diagnostics

Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

If you cannot solve a problem with the [Troubleshooting](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/) tables or the
[Error Codes](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/error-codes/), create a diagnostic file on the device. The file
collects diagnostic data of the device in one ZIP archive. SICK uses it to
analyze the problem.

## SOPASair Diagnostics

Open the web interface of the device and go to **Diagnostics → Overview**. The
page shows the current device status, the message log, and the
**Diagnostic file** tile.

![SOPASair Diagnostics overview with the Diagnostic file tile](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/assets/picoScan100/img/sopasair-diagnosis-overview.png)
*SOPASair **Diagnostics → Overview** on a picoScan100: status, messages, and the **Diagnostic file** tile with **Create file** and **Download**.*

## Create and Send a Diagnostic File

1. Reproduce the problem, or create the file soon after it occurs.
2. Log in with the Service [user level](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/) or
   higher.
3. In the **Diagnostic file** tile, click **Create file**. A new file
   overwrites the previous one, and the previous file can no longer be
   downloaded.
4. Click **Download** and save the ZIP file on your computer.
5. Send the file to SICK through your local SICK contact for analysis. Add a
   short description of the problem, the part number, the serial number, and
   the firmware version. See [Contact](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/contact/) for the contact options.

You can also create the file over the REST API with `DoDiagnosisDump`. See the
REST API | OpenAPI page of your device for the available diagnostic endpoints.

The diagnostic file may contain information about your installation. Do not
post it in public forums.

## More Information

The operating instructions of your device describe the diagnostic functions,
the status LEDs, and the messages in more detail. Download them from the
*Downloads* tab of the product page on [sick.com](https://www.sick.com/), or
open the downloads section of your device guide:
[LRS4000](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/LRS4000/#downloads),
[multiScan100](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan100/#downloads),
[multiScan200](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/multiScan200/#downloads), or
[picoScan100](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/picoScan100/#downloads).

# Error Codes for SICK LiDAR Sensors

> General list of SICK customer error IDs with their meaning and the recommended action for SICK LiDAR sensors.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/troubleshooting/error-codes/

# Error Codes

Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

The device reports problems with a customer error ID. The web interface shows the ID together with a short description and a recommended action. The list below omits codes for functions that these devices do not have, such as CAN, cameras, and SensorApps. Not every remaining code applies to every device.

<p class="table-caption" markdown>**Error Codes:** error ID, description, and action.</p>

| Error ID | Description and action |
| --- | --- |
| 110 | The device is defective. Return the device after consulting your SICK contact. |
| 120 | Switch off the device and restart it after 20 seconds. If the error occurs repeatedly, contact your SICK contact. |
| 130 | The firmware update failed. Install the firmware again after 2 minutes. If that does not work, install the last working firmware. |
| 140 | The system plug is defective. Replace the system plug. |
| 205 | The firmware update failed. The device uses the last active firmware. Restart the firmware update after 2 minutes. |
| 210 | The device is not ready for operation. Wait, and restart the device if the error persists. |
| 211 | Object evaluation is not active in interlaced mode. Deactivate interlaced mode to use object evaluation. |
| 215 | Measurement data is missing. |
| 220 | The device temperature is not OK. Check the ambient operating temperature. If necessary, use a heater or ensure sufficient cooling. |
| 223 | The device temperature is too low. Check the ambient operating temperature. If necessary, use a heater. |
| 225 | The device temperature is too high. Check the ambient operating temperature. If necessary, ensure sufficient cooling. |
| 227 | The motor speed is not OK. Check the device for external mechanical influences. |
| 228 | Shock or vibration exceeds the specification. |
| 229 | Dazzling detected. |
| 230 | The device is contaminated and not ready for operation. Clean the optics cover. |
| 235 | The device is not ready for operation. Wait. If the error persists, contact your SICK contact. |
| 237 | The device is not ready for operation. A parameterization problem was detected. Restart the device. If that does not help, contact your SICK contact. |
| 239 | Internal communication error detected. Switch off the device and restart it after 20 seconds. |
| 240 | The device and the system plug are not connected correctly. Check the connection and clean it if necessary. If the error occurs repeatedly, contact your SICK contact. |
| 241 | New system plug detected. The available inputs and outputs may have changed. Check the input and output configuration and all functions that use inputs and outputs. |
| 250 | The inertial measurement unit (IMU) is faulty. Restart the device. If that does not help, return the device after consulting your SICK contact. |
| 505 | Fallback mode is active. Disconnect the device from the power supply for about 20 seconds and restart it. |
| 510 | The device is temporarily not receiving measurement data. |
| 511 | The rotation speed deviates from the target value but is within the tolerated range: (f ≥ 15 Hz and f < 19 Hz) or (f > 21 Hz and f ≤ 25 Hz). Measurement data is still output. |
| 520 | The heater cannot be switched on. Check the power supply and the cable length and cross-section. |
| 523 | The temperature is close to the lower temperature limit. |
| 525 | The temperature is close to the upper temperature limit. |
| 530 | The device is contaminated and has limited functionality. Clean the optics cover. |
| 540 | Check the communication connection and settings. |
| 543 | A data packet could not be sent because a previous packet was not transmitted completely. Possible causes are a slow network connection or delayed data processing on the receiver side. Receive the data in a separate thread and use sufficiently large buffers. |
| 545 | Communication with the external time server (PTP, NTP) is not possible. Check the network settings. |
| 547 | The synchronization signal is missing. Check the wiring and the settings of the sync primary. |
| 550 | No connection to the internal additional sensors. Wait, and restart the device if necessary. |
| 551 | Measurement data of the inertial measurement unit (IMU) is missing. |
| 560 | I/O problem detected. Check the wiring and the configuration of the inputs and outputs. |
| 562 | The system plug memory could not be read. The system plug is defective or contains no data. Save the parameter set permanently on the system plug. If the error persists, check how the system plug is mounted on the device and replace the system plug if necessary. |
| 563 | The system plug memory could not be written. Check how the system plug is mounted on the device. |
| 564 | The input voltage is too high. Check whether the device is damaged. |
| 565 | The input voltage is too low. Inputs and outputs no longer work. |
| 570 | Parameterization problem detected. Check the configured parameters. |
| 580 | The HTTPS settings are faulty. Check the certificate on the Cybersecurity page. |
| 581 | Error while processing the certificate. Restart the device. If that does not help, return the device after consulting your SICK contact. |
| 610 | Too many fields are active at the same time. Reduce the number of simultaneously active fields or adjust the field size. |
| 709 | System plug without Gigabit Ethernet detected. This can cause loss of measurement data. Use a Gigabit Ethernet system plug. |
| 710 | Customer-specific setting. |
| 715 | The laser is switched off automatically by a customer-specific setting. |
| 720 | The device parameters differ from those on the cloning plug. The parameters from the cloning plug are applied. |
| 810 | Service mode. |
| 905 | The application is not loaded or not activated. Check the firmware. |
| 907 | The operation could not be completed because licenses are missing. Activate the required licenses and repeat the operation. |
| 910 | Too many functions are active at the same time. Deactivate functions that are not needed. |
| 911 | Object tracking is overloaded, for example because the device is moving. Switch off the object tracking function. |
| 916 | The output data is invalid. Restart the device. |
| 918 | Application error: See Diagnostics in the user interface of the application or the product documentation. |
| 935 | One of the inputs used is not available or is used more than once. Check the functions that use ports as inputs. |
| 940 | The device is not ready for operation. Restart the device. If the error still occurs, reset the device to factory settings or change the parameterization. |
| 990 | Application error: The parameters are invalid. Check the configured parameters. If necessary, reset to factory settings. |
| 992 | The configuration was not applied because of an internal error. The device uses the last saved configuration. Configure the device again. If that does not work, restart the device. |

# Glossary: SICK LiDAR, CoLa, REST, and ROS Terms

> Definitions of the terms, abbreviations, and SICK-specific names used in this developer guide.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/glossary/

# Glossary

This glossary explains the terms, abbreviations, and SICK-specific names used in this guide. Where a term has its own page, the entry links to it. Glossary terms on other pages link to their entry here.

<div class="glossary-tables" markdown="1">

## A

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| AAS (Asset Administration Shell) | Standardized digital twin of a product with its data sheet, operating instructions, certificates, and CAD data. See [Asset Administration Shell](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/asset-administration-shell/). |
| Activation type | Setting of an evaluation group that defines when the group is evaluated: always, controlled by digital inputs, or controlled by a telegram. See [Field Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/#activate-and-monitor-a-group). |
| Ambient light image | Passive image captured through a LiDAR receiver. |
| AMR (autonomous mobile robot) | Mobile robot that navigates without fixed guidance. A typical application for LiDAR sensors. |
| Angle range filter | Filter that limits the output to a horizontal and vertical angle range. See [Filter Details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/#angle-range-filter). |
| API (application programming interface) | Interface through which programs access the sensor, for example REST or CoLa. |
| Authorized Client | User level for configuring the sensor in daily operation. See [User Levels](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/). |
| AutoIP | Method in which the sensor assigns itself an IP address when no DHCP server answers. |
| Azimuth | Horizontal angle of a beam (theta). |

## B

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Beam | One measurement direction of the sensor. Each beam can return one or more echoes. |
| Blanking | Detection mode of field evaluation: the field is infringed when an object at least as large as the minimum object size is inside the field. Smaller objects are ignored ("blanked"). |
| Blooming | False points that appear near highly reflective objects such as retroreflectors. |

## C

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Challenge-response authentication | Login method of the REST API. The client requests a one-time challenge and answers with a hash that includes the password; the password itself is not transmitted. See [REST Interface](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/). |
| Checksum | Value calculated over data to detect transmission errors or changes. CoLa B uses an XOR checksum, the Compact format CRC32, and the device reports MD5 checksums of its software and parameters. See [Checksums](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/checksums/). |
| CloudCompare | Open source software for viewing and processing 3D point clouds. See [CloudCompare](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/visualization/cloudcompare/). |
| CoLa (Command Language) | SICK protocol for monitoring, maintaining, and using sensors, including configuration and data requests. CoLa A uses ASCII text on TCP port 2111, CoLa B binary data on TCP port 2112, and CoLa 2 uses TCP port 2122. See [CoLa Interface](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/cola-interface/). |
| CoLa1 | Collective name for CoLa A and CoLa B. |
| Compact format | SICK binary format for measurement data over UDP or TCP, described by Kaitai Struct definitions. See [Compact Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/compact-format/). |
| Contamination indication | Function that detects dirt on the optics cover and reports warnings or errors. See [Contamination Indication](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/contamination-indication/). |
| Contour mode | Detection mode of field evaluation that compares the scan with a taught-in reference contour. |
| CRC32 | 32-bit cyclic redundancy check. Protects each Compact and MSGPACK telegram. |
| Cyclone DDS | DDS implementation specified as the ROS 2 middleware for native ROS 2. |

## D

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Data output | Application in SOPASair that configures which measurement data the sensor sends and in which format. |
| DDS (Data Distribution Service) | Publish-subscribe middleware used by ROS 2. Native ROS 2 runs a DDS participant on the sensor. |
| Device Not Ready | Device state that signals that the sensor does not work correctly. Can be output on a digital output (`DRDY`). |
| Device search | Discovery of sensors in the network through UDP broadcasts on port 30718. See [Device Discovery](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/device-discovery/). |
| DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) | Protocol with which a network server assigns IP addresses automatically. |
| Diagnostic file | File with log entries for in-depth analysis by SICK. Created in SOPASair under Diagnostics. |
| DIN 70000 | German standard for vehicle coordinate systems (x forward, y left, z up). The IMU coordinate system of the Compact format is based on it. See [Compact Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/compact-format/#type-2-imu). |
| Distance-dependent | Field evaluation parameter that decides, based on their axial separation, whether two objects are evaluated separately or merged. See [Field Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/#distance-dependent). |

## E

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Echo | Reflection of one laser pulse. One beam can return several echoes, for example from a raindrop and a wall behind it. |
| Echo filter | Filter that selects which echoes are output, for example the first, the last, or all echoes. See [Filter Details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/#echo-filter). |
| EEPROM | Non-volatile memory of the sensor. Changes are stored permanently only after `WriteEeprom` (REST) or `mEEwriteall` (CoLa). |
| Elevation | Vertical angle of a beam (phi). |
| Encoder | Sensor that measures the rotation or position of a moving axis. Encoder data can be combined with 2D LiDAR scans to build 3D point clouds. See [3D With 2D LiDARs](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/3d-with-2d-lidars/). |
| EPLAN | Electrical engineering software for designing schematics. SICK provides EPLAN macros as product data. See [Asset Administration Shell](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/asset-administration-shell/). |
| Evaluation | One detection field with its parameters. Up to 48 evaluations can be configured. |
| Evaluation group | Set of evaluations that is activated and deactivated together. |

## F

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Field evaluation | On-sensor application that checks whether objects are inside a defined field and reports `FREE` or `INFRINGED`. See [Field Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/). |
| Firmware | Software that runs on the sensor. See [Firmware Update](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/firmware-update/). |
| Fog filter | Filter that suppresses echoes caused by fog, particularly at close range. |
| Frame | One complete scan. A frame is split into segments for output. |

## H

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| HDDM<sup>+</sup> (High Definition Distance Measurement Plus) | SICK time-of-flight technology that combines returns from many laser pulses to calculate a distance value. See [LiDAR Basics](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/lidar-basics/#measuring-distance-with-light). |

## I

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| IGMP (Internet Group Management Protocol) | Protocol with which hosts join a multicast group. Switches with IGMP snooping forward multicast traffic only to ports with receivers. See [UDP Unicast / Multicast](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/udp-unicast-multicast/). |
| IMU (inertial measurement unit) | Built-in sensor that measures acceleration, angular velocity, and orientation. |
| Interlaced mode | Scan mode that combines several scans shifted relative to one another to increase angular resolution. |
| Interval filter | Filter that outputs only every n-th scan. |

## K

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Kaitai Struct | Language for describing binary formats. SICK publishes the Compact format as Kaitai Struct definitions (`.ksy`). |

## L

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Layer | One horizontal scan line at a fixed elevation angle. A multi-layer sensor provides several layers; a single-layer sensor provides one. |
| LiDAR (light detection and ranging) | Measurement principle that determines distances from the time-of-flight of laser pulses. |
| LMDscandata | CoLa telegram with measurement data. See [LMDscandata Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/lmdscandata-format/). |

## M

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Maintenance | User level for maintenance tasks. See [User Levels](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/). |
| Mean filter | Filter that averages the distance of each point over several scans, also called moving average filter. Some devices refer to this as high precision mode. See [Filter Details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/#moving-average-filter). |
| Minimum object size | Smallest object that infringes a field in blanking mode. |
| MIP (Milestone Integration Platform) | Platform for integrating applications and devices with Milestone XProtect video management software. Its software development kit (SDK) supports protocols, components, and plug-ins. See [Milestone XProtect Camera Plugin](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/milestones-camera/). |
| MessagePack (MSGPACK) | Compact binary serialization format for exchanging data between programming languages. See [MSGPACK Format](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/msgpack-format/). |
| Multi-echo | Ability of the sensor to measure several echoes per beam. |
| Multicast | Transmission of one data stream to a group of receivers. |

## N

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Native ROS 2 | Function with which the sensor publishes ROS 2 messages itself over DDS, without a host driver. See [ROS Integration](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/#native-ros-2). |
| NTP (Network Time Protocol) | Protocol for synchronizing the sensor clock with a time server. See [Time Synchronization](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/time-synchronization/). |

## O

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAPI | Machine-readable description of a REST API. SICK publishes OpenAPI files for its REST APIs. |

## P

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Particle filter | Filter that removes isolated points caused by dust, rain, or snow. See [Filter Details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/#particle-filter). |
| pcap | File format for recorded network traffic, created for example with Wireshark. See [Wireshark](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/recording/wireshark-pcap/). |
| PCD (Point Cloud Data) | File format of the Point Cloud Library for 3D point clouds. Viewers such as CloudCompare open it. See [CloudCompare](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/visualization/cloudcompare/). |
| Performance profile | See scan configuration. |
| Perpendicular distance measurement | On-device application that measures the distance of objects to a reference line. See [Perpendicular Distance Measurement](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/perpendicular-distance-measurement/). |
| PLC (programmable logic controller) | Industrial controller. See [PLC Integration](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/plc-integration/). |
| Point cloud | Set of 3D points calculated from the measured distances and angles. |
| PointCloud2 | ROS message type for point clouds. |
| Product ID | Globally unique identifier for SICK products that provides access to product-related information. It contains the part number (P/N) and, if available, the serial number (S/N). See [`pid.sick.com/{P/N}/{S/N}`](https://pid.sick.com/). |
| PSIRT (Product Security Incident Response Team) | SICK team that handles reports of security vulnerabilities. |
| PTP (Precision Time Protocol, IEEE 1588) | Protocol for precise time synchronization over Ethernet. |
| PWR (power) | Connector label for a sensor's power supply connection; some variants combine power and digital I/O. |

## Q

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Quaternion | Four values (w, x, y, z) that describe an orientation in 3D. The IMU reports its orientation as a quaternion. |

## R

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Reflector | Highly reflective target, such as a retroreflector. The sensor can mark points on reflectors. |
| Region of interest | Selected range of measured values used for further evaluation. In this guide, it limits an evaluation or a filter; for teach-in, a polygon bounds where the contour is learned. |
| Remission factor | Measure of the light reflected by a surface relative to a defined white reference surface, expressed as a percentage. A value of 100 % means the same return as the reference, not that all incident light is reflected. Retroreflectors can exceed 100 %. Sensor ranges are specified for a given remission factor, for example 10 %. |
| REST (Representational State Transfer) | HTTP-based interface of the sensor for reading and writing variables and calling methods. See [REST Interface](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/configuration/rest-interface/). |
| RMW (ROS middleware) | Layer that connects ROS 2 to a DDS implementation. |
| ROS (Robot Operating System) | Open source framework for robot software. See [ROS Integration](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/). |
| ROS bag | Recording of ROS messages in a file (`.bag` in ROS 1, `.db3` or `.mcap` in ROS 2). See [ROS Bag](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/recording/ros-bag-db3/). |
| RSSI (received signal strength indicator) | Measure of the strength of an echo. |

## S

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Scan configuration | Predefined combination of aperture angle, scanning frequency, and angular resolution, identified by a number. |
| Scan merger | On-device function that combines the 2D scans of a rotating sensor into one 3D point cloud. See [3D Scan Recording](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/3d-scan-recording/). |
| Scan range | Angle range covered by the sensor. |
| ScanSegmentAPI | SICK Python and C# libraries for receiving segmented scan data. Supported devices and features depend on the library version. |
| Segment | Part of a scan restricted to an azimuth (horizontal) and/or elevation (vertical) angle range. In the segmented output described in this guide, parts of a frame are sent as separate telegrams so they can be processed immediately. |
| Sensitivity mode | Receiver setting that trades scanning range against robustness to ambient light and noise. See [Filter Details](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/filter-details/#sensitivity-mode). |
| Service | Highest user level. See [User Levels](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/). |
| Session token | Token that authorizes binary file transfers, for example firmware updates and configuration backups. |
| sick_perception_sdk | SICK C++ SDK for configuring compatible sensors and receiving Compact data. See [Coding Tools & Examples](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/coding-tools-and-examples/). |
| sick_scan_xd | SICK driver for ROS 1, ROS 2, and applications without ROS. See [ROS Integration](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/integration-notes/ros-integration/#sick_scan_xd). |
| SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping) | Method in which a robot builds or updates a map of an unknown environment while tracking its own position in that map. See [Native ROS 2 SLAM](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/beginner-projects/native-ros2-slam/). |
| Slot | One column of measurements at a horizontal angle step. |
| SOPAS ET | SOPAS Engineering Tool for parameterization, configuration, diagnostics, and monitoring of SICK sensors and systems. The Windows application can discover devices and save, export, and import parameter sets. See [SOPAS ET](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/visualization/sopas-et/). |
| SOPASair | Application for parameterization, configuration, diagnostics, and monitoring of SICK sensors. In this guide, it is the sensor's web interface, opened in a browser. See [SOPASair](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/visualization/sopasair/). |
| STX / ETX | Start of text (`0x02`) and end of text (`0x03`), the control characters that frame a CoLa A telegram. |
| Swagger UI | Interactive viewer for OpenAPI files. |
| System plug | Customer-replaceable component required for device operation that provides device functions and may store communication parameters or other configuration, depending on the device. |

## T

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Teach-in | Learning process during configuration that collects data for later analysis during operation. In field evaluation, it learns the current environment as the reference contour of a field. See [Field Evaluation](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/on-device-applications/field-evaluation/#teach-in). |
| Telegram | One message exchanged with the sensor, for example a CoLa command or a Compact data packet. |
| Telegram type | Number in a Compact telegram that identifies its content, for example scan data or IMU data. |

## U

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Unicast | Transmission of a data stream to one receiver. |
| User level | Access level that defines which settings a user can change: Maintenance, Authorized Client, or Service. See [User Levels](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/shared-features/user-levels/). |

## V

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Virtual Sensor Lab | Browser-based simulation of SICK sensors. See [Virtual Sensor Lab](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/simulation/virtual-sensor-lab/). |

## W

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| WebSocket | Protocol for a persistent connection over which the sensor pushes events. See [WebSocket Events](https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/data-streaming/websocket-events/). |
| Wireshark | Network analysis tool. SICK provides a Wireshark dissector for the Compact format. |

## X

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| XOR checksum | Checksum of CoLa B telegrams: the exclusive OR of all payload bytes. |

</div>

# Contact SICK

> Contact local SICK sales, open a technical support case, or discuss LiDAR integration questions with the community.

Source: https://sickag.github.io/sick_lidar_developer_guide/contact/

# Contact

Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

Choose the contact option that best fits your question.

## Local Sales

Contact your local SICK sales representative for product selection,
application advice, pricing, and availability. Visit [sick.com](https://www.sick.com/)
and select your country or region to find the local sales contact.

## Support Portal Case

For technical troubleshooting, open a support case at
[support.sick.com](https://support.sick.com/). Describe the issue, your setup,
and the steps needed to reproduce it. Include the part number and serial
number from the device's type label, together with the firmware version.

If your device provides a diagnostic-file export, create the file through
its configuration interface and attach it to the case. Diagnostic information
helps SICK investigate the issue; the available export options depend on the
device and firmware.

## Public Discussion

For general integration questions and sharing experience with other users, join the
[GitHub Discussions space](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_lidar_developer_guide/discussions)
or [start a new discussion](https://github.com/SICKAG/sick_lidar_developer_guide/discussions/new/choose).

Discussions are public. Do not post credentials, confidential project data,
or diagnostic files containing sensitive information; use a Support Portal
case for information that should not be shared publicly.
